530759|2026-03.headline: Sterling Tools FY26 standalone fasteners EBITDA rose 17.1% to INR111 crore at 15.3% margin, but management flags Q1 FY27 cost pressure and a delayed EV timeline.
530759|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 standalone fastener business total income up 11.4% YoY to INR725.9 crore, EBITDA up 17.1% to INR111 crore, and margin of 15.3% versus 14.5%. Profit before exceptional items rose 27.6% to INR74 crore and operating cash flow was INR83.3 crore. A subsidiary-level Q4 loss of INR21 crore was attributed to a bad-debt provision on one bigger customer, which management said is still likely recoverable. The EV business timeline was pushed out by 3 to 5 years and target aspirations deferred by about a year, with SEM expected to return to profitability in FY28 rather than FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash flow from operations, standalone fasteners (FY26)

segments.name: Standalone fasteners (automotive)
segments.commentary: FY26 total income INR725.9 crore, EBITDA INR111 crore at 15.3% margin; management estimates 25-30% domestic automotive fastener share and is net debt free. Business is strongly cash generative.

segments.name: SEM (EV powertrain / power electronics)
segments.commentary: Profitable at EBITDA and PBT through FY25 but loss-making in FY26; management says it will not be profitable in FY27 but expects return to profitability in FY28. OBC and DC/DC lines due for commissioning by end Q2 FY27, commercial supplies from Q3 FY27; more than 28 active customer programs.

segments.name: STML (HVDC contactors and relays)
segments.commentary: Serial commercial production expected from July/August 2026; brand-label supplies already started. Management sizes current Indian HVDC contactor and pre-charge relay market at about INR300 crore, growing to over INR750 crore by end of decade.

guidance_outlook: Fastener FY27 capex around INR75 crore for capacity expansion, operational enhancements and growth programs; all to be commercialised by Q4 FY27.
Management expects fastener growth ahead of the Indian automotive industry in FY27, barring an extreme event such as the West Asia crisis.
Steady-state standalone EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at around 15% plus; short-term pressure expected in Q1 FY27 from steel, energy and chemical inflation.
Hopeful of customer price increases from Q2 FY27 to offset cost inflation; steel is a pass-through with a 1-3 month lag.
SEM not profitable in FY27, expected back to profitability in FY28.
Target of 50% of revenue from non-fastener businesses pushed back due to slower EV penetration.
Railway opportunity not expected to be meaningful revenue for the next 2 years.
Fastener revenue potential about INR800 crore plus with current and FY27 capacity, rising to INR900-1,000 crore with further capex next year; asset turn around 1.8-2x.
capex_capacity: Fastener capex of around INR75 crore in FY27, invested in existing facilities for capacity, balancing and efficiency/quality improvements.
SEM OBC and DC/DC production lines to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27 (Jaideep said Q3 in one answer); commercial supplies from Q3 FY27.
STML fully automated Bangalore facility for high-voltage components; serial production from July/August 2026.
Asset turn target around 2x (1.8x cited as benchmark) with payback of about 24 months on brownfield capex.
demand_pricing: Indian passenger vehicle sales hit record 46.4 lakh units in FY26, up 7.9%; Q4 FY26 PV sales up 13.2%. 2-wheelers reached 2.17 crore units, up 10.7%.

Management says steel is a straight pass-through with a lag of 1-3 months; energy, chemicals and plastics costs are not covered by norms and are being addressed through price increases and efficiency.
No annual price-reduction contracts with OEMs; prices negotiated on competitive and cost scenarios.
Imports not cheaper than domestic supply per management; localisation by OEMs is a slow, strategic process.
Management estimates e-bus industry could ramp to about 10,000 units a year; onboarded CV customers not yet shown in presentation.
Single-source OBC/DC-DC supply to start with; second source likely once volumes reach scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR21 crore subsidiary loss in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Wadhwa said it was a bad-debt provision on one of the bigger customers, taken prudently even though recovery is considered highly probable; operating PBT is not as severe as it appears.

qa_highlights.question: Are there annual price-reduction contracts with OEMs, and what margin pressure is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Aggarwal said there are no price-reduction contracts; Q1 FY27 will be a special pressure quarter, with price increases from customers expected from Q2 and efficiency gains to offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic market share and non-auto revenue exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates 25-30% share of the domestic automotive fastener market; revenue is predominantly automotive. Railway is early-stage and not expected to be meaningful for two years.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view payback on EV investments that will not yield revenue for 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said investments are strategic, first-of-kind products for India, value-margin dilutive for a phase; management acknowledged short-term pain in the next 1-2 years but believes in long-term payoff.

qa_highlights.question: When will SEM return to EBITDA and PBT profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep said SEM will not be profitable in FY27 but there is no reason it cannot be profitable in FY28; other businesses depend on their start-up timelines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable fastener margin, and will margins moderate near term?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said there may be short-term pressure, but steady-state EBITDA margin should be maintained around 15% plus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential and asset turn on the INR75 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said capex will be commercialised by Q4 FY27, revenue potential about INR800 crore plus, rising to INR900-1,000 crore; asset turn around 2x, with 24-month turnaround on brownfield capex.

qa_highlights.question: How is vendor selection for OBC and DC/DC supply, and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep said the company starts as 100% single source, with a second source possible at higher volumes. Right to win rests on partner credibility, technical support and multifunction (3-in-1 to 6-in-1) integration capability through GTAKE and Landworld.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin pressure from steel, energy and chemical inflation; pass-through is lagged and energy/chemicals not normed.
Whether OEM price increases from Q2 FY27 materialise as expected.
Continued SEM losses in FY27 and EV penetration remaining below expectations; non-fastener revenue target of 50% pushed back.
Customer credit quality after the INR21 crore subsidiary bad-debt provision.
Commissioning and commercial ramp of OBC/DC-DC lines and STML serial orders from July/August 2026.
Management described the capital allocation for new EV products as value-margin dilutive and capital-intensive.
West Asia crisis effects on crude, commodities, currency and shipping routes.

Management repeatedly acknowledged pain in FY27 and deferred timelines, and some answers on EV revenue and payback were vague.
key_quotes: Short-term, there's a lot of pain like we have seen pain last year and the next year or 2, but we strongly believe in our future.
No, we don't have any price reduction contracts , nowhere. Prices remain constant.
We are confident that we'll be able to mainta in our EBITDA margins around 15% plus.

530759|2026-06.headline: Sterling Tools standalone fasteners grew total income 23.7% to INR201.9 crore with PAT up 48.4%, while EV subsidiaries remain loss-making until FY28 breakeven.
530759|2026-06.overview: Standalone fasteners delivered Q1 FY27 total income of INR201.9 crore (+23.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR31.1 crore (+26.9%, margin 15.4% vs 15%) and PAT of INR16.4 crore (+48.4%, margin 8.1%). Management flagged steel and broader inflation (chemicals, tungsten, wages up to 35% in some areas) as cost pressures, with pass-through price negotiations at a mature stage and expected to hit P&L after a 2-4 month lag. Subsidiaries SEM and STML continue to lose money; both are guided to break even in FY28 at combined revenue of about INR225-250 crore. Capacity utilisation is 90-95% and an INR88 crore fasteners capex (misstated as INR80 crore on the call) is mostly expected to commission in H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin up only ~40 bps per analyst

segments.name: Standalone fasteners
segments.commentary: Total income INR201.9 crore (+23.7%), EBITDA INR31.1 crore (15.4% margin), PAT INR16.4 crore (8.1% margin); management says growth is outpacing the auto industry, with 20%+ growth in Q1 and similar near-term run-rate expected.

segments.name: Sterling E-Mobility (SEM)
segments.commentary: Loss-making; FY25 revenue was about INR380 crore on one anchor customer that in-sourced, a drop of about INR280 crore. Breakeven guided at about INR175 crore revenue in FY28; current capacity over INR300 crore; 33 active programs and 4 OEM business confirmations. Revenue mix planned at 30-35% two/three-wheeler and about 65% commercial vehicles.

segments.name: Sterling Tech-Mobility (STML)
segments.commentary: Pre-commercial; HV DC contactors and relays. Seven customer programs secured; commercial supplies to start Q2 FY27. Breakeven guided at about INR70 crore revenue in FY28; current capacity about INR140 crore on 3-shift basis. Testing/validation takes 8-16 months per customer.

guidance_outlook: Fasteners: management expects to hold margin structures on a full-year basis despite steel and inflation, citing customer price increases at an advanced stage.
Fasteners: near-term growth expected similar to Q1's 20%+ pace, unless the auto industry slows.
EV businesses (SEM and STML) revenue growth guided at 20-30% in FY27 and 30-40% in FY28.
SEM and STML both expected to break even in FY28; both will lose money in FY27.
Long-term EBITDA/operating margin for SEM and STML targeted at about 10%, plus or minus 2%, at breakeven scale.
Fasteners capex: INR88 crore in FY27, with a further INR25-30 crore next year to support about INR1,000 crore potential revenue, if markets support.
capex_capacity: Fasteners capex INR88 crore (stated as INR80 crore in the call, corrected by management), purely expansion of existing facilities in Bangalore and two NCR plants; some capacity kicked in marginally in Q1, bulk in H2 FY27.

SEM onboard charger and multifunction unit lines to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27; samples then need about 4 months of on-road trials (around 50,000 km), so supplies expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
STML fully automated facility in Bangalore; current capacity about INR140 crore on 3-shift basis; commercial supplies from Q2 FY27.
SEM current capacity over INR300 crore without further investment.
Total invested capital in subsidiaries about INR100 crore (STML about INR50 crore, SEM about INR48-49 crore).
demand_pricing: Steel price increases in Q1 created cost pressure; lower-cost inventory largely consumed, so impact expected to be more visible in the coming quarter.
Steel pass-through negotiations typically take 2-4 months; management says customers are positive on compensating for inflation this year.
Industry: PV sales +25.9% to 1.27 million, 2W +20.3% to 5.63 million, CV +18.3%, 3W +29.7% YoY in Q1 FY27 per management.
SEM: LCV, HCV and public transport bus programs gaining traction; EV demand supported by high oil prices.
Integrated units for heavy bus and truck platforms priced at about INR3-3.5 lakh per unit.
Two new 2-wheeler programs at advanced stage with one OEM response expected in coming months; management sees second-sourcing opportunity at incumbents.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin rise about 270 bps while EBITDA margin rose only about 40 bps in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited steel price increases plus broad inflation (chemicals, tungsten, minimum wages up to 35% in some areas), partly offset by shop-floor efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fasteners capacity utilisation and when will new capex be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 90-95%, described as fully utilised given product mix; most of the INR88 crore capex expected to commission in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How should standalone EBITDA margin be considered for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect EBITDA to weaken further and expects to hold full-year margin structures, based on price increases at an advanced stage.

qa_highlights.question: What are breakeven levels and timeline for SEM and STML?
qa_highlights.answer: Both expected to break even in FY28; SEM at about INR175 crore revenue and STML at about INR70 crore, combined about INR225-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity of the subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: SEM over INR300 crore and STML about INR140 crore on current capacity, total about INR440 crore (corrected from INR400 crore plus).

qa_highlights.question: Will the fasteners capex take capacity to INR1,000 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, if markets support it, with a further INR25-30 crore of investment next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new SEM onboard charger and multifunction line contributing soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Lines commissioned by end of Q2; customer trials of about 4 months mean supplies around December 2026 or January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SEM loss-making and what is the R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss due to revenue collapse after anchor customer in-sourcing (FY25 revenue of about INR380 crore falling by about INR280 crore) and continuing R&D; about 130 people, more than half in product or application engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS regulatory opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulation for medium and heavy CVs, about 0.5 million units a year, from October 2027, possibly pushed to January 2028; a Chinese partner signed.

risks_watch: Steel and inflation pass-through: lower-cost inventory largely consumed, so steel cost impact expected to be more visible next quarter; pass-through takes 2-4 months to reach P&L
Gross margin rose about 270 bps but EBITDA margin only about 40 bps; watch whether full-year standalone margin holds as management expects
Capex timing: most of the INR88 crore fasteners capex is expected to commission in H2 FY27, so benefits are back-ended
Subsidiary losses continue through FY27 for SEM and STML; breakeven depends on FY28 revenue reaching about INR225-250 crore combined
SEM onboard charger and multifunction lines due by end Q2 FY27; customer on-road trials of about 4 months put supplies around Dec 2026 or Jan 2027
STML testing and validation of 8-16 months per customer; commercial supplies from Q2 FY27 remain subject to certification timelines
key_quotes: So we are at a very mature stage of negotiations for price increases on account of steel.

We hope -- despite the pressures, we are quite confident that we'll be able to hold our margin structures on a full year basis despite the steel and inflation because we expect to get price increases from customers, which are in a very advanced stage.
So it's going to be slow.
So basically, both businesses put together, about INR340 crores revenue is the current capacity installed.

More cautious and evasive on subsidiary timelines, repeatedly stressing that the EV ecosystem is slow and that breakeven and growth depend on customer validation and market support.

rows.why: Management expects to hold full-year standalone margin structures (EBITDA 15.4%, PAT margin 8.1%) as customer price increases are at an advanced stage, but gross margin rose about 270 bps while EBITDA margin rose only about 40 bps, and steel cost pressure has not fully hit yet.

rows.why: Regulation covers about 0.5 million medium and heavy CV units a year, with a Chinese partner signed, but timing could slip from October 2027 to January 2028.

530813|2026-03.headline: KRBL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR1,526 crore as record domestic sales (+22%) offset a 33% export drop from Middle East disruption; PAT INR155 crore.
530813|2026-03.overview: Domestic revenue hit a record INR1,230 crore in Q4 (+22% YoY) on 16% rice volume growth and 5% realisation growth, while exports fell to INR279 crore (vs INR450 crore) as the Iran/Israel/US conflict and March 2026 shipping disruption hit Middle East shipments. Q4 gross margin fell to 29.6% (from 31.5%) and EBITDA margin to 15.5% (from 16.2%), with PAT of INR155 crore (10.1% margin) against INR154 crore a year earlier. For FY26, total income rose 9% to INR6,168 crore, with EBITDA margin of 15.8% and PAT margin of 10.5%. Management said Q1 export trends are hard to call and gave no monthly export numbers; it expects demand to rebound once the conflict settles.

financial_highlights.change: margin improved on lower input costs and higher other income

financial_highlights.metric: Net bank borrowings incl. treasury investments (31 Mar 2026)
financial_highlights.change: vs negative INR405 crore a year earlier

guidance_outlook: Domestic: management is targeting about 10% organisation-level volume growth in FY27, and expects a further 2–3% improvement in average domestic realisation in Q1 FY27 versus about INR79,000–80,000 per MT in Q4.

Exports: no numeric guidance; management said April ran in line with Q4 trajectory, while May and June were still unclear. It expects exports to rebound sharply once the Middle East conflict settles, and said the recent lost volumes could be recovered in three to four months after settlement.
Inventory: 530,000 tonnes of rice-equivalent stock at 31 Mar 2026. Management expects to build inventory in the coming season, depending on crop and pricing, and sees the export demand as strong.
Edible oil: expects healthy double-digit growth in FY27.
Real estate: Samalkha (Panipat) land parcel of about 130 acres; the 60-acre portion is earmarked for own warehousing near Sonipat/Barota, and no monetisation decision has been taken.
capex_capacity: Inventory at 31 Mar 2026: total INR3,714 crore, including paddy INR879 crore (230,000 tonnes) and rice INR2,667 crore (427,000 tonnes), versus INR2,934 crore rice at 31 Mar 2025 (476,000 tonnes).
Rice-equivalent inventory of about 530,000 tonnes against FY26 sales of about 560,000 MT domestic and 160,000 MT export.
Distribution: 3.4 lakh retail outlets, 16 C&F agents and 8 super stockists; supply chain shift towards an FOR model.
Samalkha land parcel (about 130 acres, split by GT road): the 60-acre side is for KRBL's own warehousing given space constraints at the Barota plant.
demand_pricing: Domestic branded basmati: Q4 realisation about INR79,000–80,000 per MT; price stabilisation and brand investment supported growth, while Q3 domestic revenue was flat YoY on competitive and pricing pressure.

Market share in packaged basmati (FY26): general trade 36.9%, modern trade 38.7%, e-commerce 40.1%. Management said Q4 share was 100–200 bps higher than the full-year level in each channel; it did not give a YoY comparison for Q4.

Exports: Middle East shipments were hit in March 2026. Cargo has largely reached destinations since April–May. Alternate routes (Khor Fakkan, Jeddah, Salalah, Jordan for Iraq) carry higher freight, insurance and transit times. Management reports Saudi business is continuing.

Industry: India's FY26 basmati exports rose about 8% to 6.5 million MT (record); non-basmati exports about 15 million MT (+6%). Pakistan Super Basmati has traded at a premium to Indian 1121 since October 2025 (USD1,180–1,220/MT FOB).
Global: USDA sees 2026-27 global rice production at about 538 million MT versus 543 million MT, with consumption rising to about 541 million MT. Management said this could keep prices firm.

qa_highlights.question: Export run-rate: how much further decline versus Q4 in Q1, and April numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no April or monthly export figures and said Q1 depends on the geopolitical situation. Ashish said April was 'in the same trajectory' as Q4, with May and June still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build-up for FY27 and the competitive environment in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Anoop Gupta said inventory will be built in the coming season, depending on crop and pricing. Management cited a 8–9% margin on unsold stock and about 35–40 tonnes of export rice at Kandla (about 20% cheaper than current prices), which could be sold domestically.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic volume growth and whether Q4 can be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 10% organisation-level domestic volume growth in FY27; Q4 volume growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Use of about INR1,000 crore cash: special dividend or buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish said only the approved INR103 crore dividend (450%) was in scope; no other capital return measures were announced.

qa_highlights.question: Real estate: why not monetise the Samalkha land and what about the buyback question?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60-acre portion will be used for own warehousing despite the higher profit from a sale. It is evaluating opportunities but will only invest in real estate if the return could double the investment.

qa_highlights.question: Basmati price outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment, as the India Rice Exporters' Association crop-size contract is still being mapped; a view on FY27 pricing awaits the crop size.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi distributor appointment and channel inventory in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is staying selective and direct with wholesalers in Saudi Arabia; no distributor has been appointed. Ashish declined to quantify channel inventory but said most Middle East markets are below normal stock levels.

Export volumes in Q1 FY27 with no April or monthly data given; management declined to share run-rate figures.

Pending ED matter (sub judice): management would not take questions on it.
Real estate capital allocation: the Samalkha land parcel and about INR1,000 crore of cash, with no clear return-deployment plan.
Domestic competitive intensity and channel share, with Q4 share gains not quantified and the FY share trend showing a decline per the analyst's reading.
Monsoon and crop outcome for 2026 (possible deficient monsoon) and the basmati price trajectory.

Gross margin (including other income) jumped to 36.3% from 25.7%, and EBITDA margin to 23.8% from 13.9%, helped by INR64 crores of other income including MTM and forex gains. Management called the margins unsustainable and guided FY27 to about 30% gross margin and 17-18% EBITDA margin.

530999|2026-03.headline: Balaji Amines Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% YoY to INR403 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25% versus 19% a year earlier.
530999|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR403 crore (up about 12% YoY) and EBITDA was INR102 crore against INR68 crore, lifting margin to 25% from 19% in Q4 FY25 and 18% in Q3 FY26. PAT reached INR65 crore versus INR40 crore a year earlier. Management said production was briefly hit in March 2026 by a geopolitical situation but was managed through inventory planning. For FY27 management guided to 10-15% consolidated volume growth in Q&A, and to 20-30% volume growth and 22-23% EBITDA margin by end-FY27 (wording varied during the call). Specialty subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals was running partially during modifications, which depressed its quarterly margins.

qa_highlights.question: PAT grew about 25% against 4% revenue growth: how much is from finance costs or tax, and what is the normalized PAT growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs fell by almost Rs 10 crore YoY on lower debt and are expected to stay at a reduced level. EBITDA margin is around 13-14%, so the PAT gain is mainly from lower interest. Current-year PAT growth estimate is about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the existing order book support double-digit growth without material new wins, and what is its execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is to be executed over about 3 years, with book-to-bill around 3x. Target new order inflow is about Rs 8,000 crore this year, needed for 10% growth this year and 15% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company have any exceptional items in FY27, after about Rs 150 crore in the last two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect exceptional items this year. Last year's items were mainly Vivaad-se-Vishwas settlements and some investment write-downs.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the Telangana land sale and further monetization?
qa_highlights.answer: The sale was 27 acres for Rs 26-27 crore, leaving about 400 acres in Telangana. Other parcels are under discussion. Non-core monetization target is Rs 150-200 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge reduction timeline?

qa_highlights.question: Patel Smondo OC timing and occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: OC is expected this financial year after a pending litigation closes. The third tower is a service apartment tower, ready to occupy once OC comes. Some buyers have taken possession for fit-outs.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 15%, and are buybacks or ESOPs being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm 15% margins because competition has risen and a large project was lost last year. Margins are targeted at 13-14%. Buybacks will be considered after debt reduction, which may take two to three years. ESOPs will be handled through the existing ESOP trust.

qa_highlights.question: How much working capital and capex will execution need, and how will it be funded?

qa_highlights.question: Dredging, and the arbitration awards above Rs 1,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is looking at dredging work, alone or with partners. Arbitrations are being followed up, and settlements are explored where possible. PSUs usually litigate through all courts.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and Q2 revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 40-45, and this continues in new contracts. Q2 is seasonally slower because of monsoon, with some ups and downs but no major disruption expected.

qa_highlights.question: Hydro bids under evaluation and outcome timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Bids under evaluation total about Rs 9,000 crore, mostly Arunachal and North-East hydro, with a Rs 60,000 crore pipeline. Management said outcomes are hoped for by Diwali, which the CEO called hopeful.

qa_highlights.question: Retention money and release timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention is about 5% of each contract, around Rs 200-250 crore on the balance sheet. It is mostly released at project end, though some projects allow withdrawal against bank guarantees.

531279|2026-03.headline: Trishakti FY26 revenue rose ~90% to INR 32.44 crore, but EBITDA includes INR 4.58 crore subvention income and receivables sit near 200 days.

FY27 order book stated at INR 60-62 crore, excluding variable overtime; contracts run to 31 December on paper and management expects extensions.
Target ROC 22-25%; management says ROC guidance is conservative because the INR 400 crore capex will not be full-year.
Management expects receivables to normalise in FY27 after a family settlement is cleared; expects debt-to-equity to settle around 1.5 over time.
Fleet target for next phase is 50-250 ton machines for the first ~INR 400 crore of capex, to keep utilisation above 95%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management says other income is part of core hiring; margins are stable on an adjusted basis. An analyst computed ~58% including subvention in revenue, versus a September quarter level.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity will remain around 1.5 to 2 times equity and that it intends to stay below 2 times; cost of borrowing is ~5% flat.

531335|2026-03.headline: Zydus Wellness Q4 FY26 net sales grew 62.1% on Comfort Click, but net profit fell 5.8% as seasonal brands dropped 9.8% in the domestic business.

531344|2026-03.headline: CONCOR posted record FY26 throughput of 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), but PAT fell 4.5% and Q4 domestic EBIT margin collapsed to 0.2%.

531431|2026-09.headline: Shakti Pumps Q2 FY27: solar EPC revenue ~INR543 crores on 23,865 pumps installed (+7% YoY), with PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval still pending.

531548|2026-03.headline: Somany Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin rose to 11.4% and FY26 to 9.3%; management guides at least 150 bps more margin improvement in FY27 despite gas-price shock.

Capacity utilisation was broadly flat at about 79% for the year, rising to 82% in Q4, and Somany Max reached near breakeven versus a loss of about INR 9 crore in Q4 FY25. Gas prices jumped from about 9 March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation, and Morbi capacity was disrupted, which management sees as a share-gain opportunity for organised players. Working capital improved sharply, with receivable days at 40 (from 51) and working capital lower by 4 days to 9 days. Management passed through about 16-17% tile price hikes and about 8% bathware and sanitaryware hikes, and said input cost increases are being fully recovered in retail but only about 85-90% in projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a tipping point where gas costs make running plants unviable?

rows.why: Cost-to-income fell to 44.2% from 49.4% in Q4 FY26 and management guides 44-45%, with AUM per employee up to INR3.4 crore from INR1.8 crore a year earlier.

rows.label: Funding diversification away from banks
rows.why: NCDs, CP, bank refinancing and a GMTN programme are under way with bank share to decline, while cost of funds is guided broadly stable for the rest of FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on gold growth, branch economics, 19-21% ROE and the raised FY28 AUM target, but cautious on Stage 2 migration, construction NPA and gold price risk; analysts pressed on the Stage 2 coverage drop (11.8% to 9.4%), branch pacing and leadership churn.

531642|2026-03.headline: Marico guides FY27 to double-digit revenue growth past INR15,000 crore and high-teens EBITDA growth, assuming macro normalises, after copra fell ~35% from peak.
531642|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of multi-year highs in India volume growth, International constant-currency growth and consolidated revenue, with double-digit profit growth despite sharp input inflation. Copra has corrected about 35% from peak and is expected to stay range-bound, while vegetable oils and crude-linked inputs are rising on Middle East tensions. Marico passed on copra benefits through price cuts of about 10% on non-price-point and small packs of Parachute, and took 6-7% price increases in VAHO. The FY27 guidance was raised to high-teens EBITDA growth, and the FY30 aspiration was set at mid-teens EBITDA growth with revenue crossing INR20,000 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Double-digit growth to cross INR15,000 crore

financial_highlights.change: Raised vs prior call (previously mid-teens, per management)
Gross margin +350-400 bps over FY26 exit; A&P up 200-250 bps
Inflated by denominator effect from revenue growth
Mid-teens growth in FY26; ~16-17% in Q4 incl. acquisitions

financial_highlights.value: INR350+ crore (Serums, Male Grooming, Skin Care); INR1,100+ crore digital-first portfolio

financial_highlights.metric: Foods + Premium Personal Care share of India business

segments.name: Parachute (India coconut oil)
segments.commentary: Delivered low single-digit volume growth after adjusting for mlage; non-price-point and small packs cut by ~10% as copra fell ~35% from peak. Management says RPI is not significantly off despite ~60% price increase taken last year.

segments.name: Value Added Hair Oils (VAHO)
segments.commentary: Volume growth in low-20s% in Q4 and ~20% for FY26, led by mid and premium segments growing close to double-digit on a two-year CAGR. Took 6-7% price increase in response to crude-derivative inflation; expects double-digit volume-led growth.

segments.name: Saffola Edible Oils
segments.commentary: Steady performance in an elevated pricing environment; guided to low-to-mid single-digit volume growth subject to a margin threshold, with pricing passed on and focus on Saffola Gold, Total and cold-pressed.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: Mid-teens growth in FY26; core Saffola Foods grew double digits in Q4, while True Elements lapped a high base and SKU rationalisation. Management base case is 20-25% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Premium Personal Care / digital-first brands
segments.commentary: Beardo and Plix on accelerated growth with improving profitability; Plix estimated at mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin, targeting double digits soon. Aim to exit FY27 at double-digit EBITDA margin and teens by FY30.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Bangladesh grew 35% in the latest quarter vs 25% for the full year, with guidance of at least double-digit growth. Vietnam, South Africa and exports are scaling; Middle East (4% of turnover) hit by March supply constraints, with alternate routes via Egypt. FY27 guided to mid-teens constant-currency growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India volume growth: high single-digit; International: mid-teens constant-currency growth.
FY27 consolidated: double-digit revenue growth to cross INR15,000 crore and high-teens EBITDA growth, assuming normalisation of macros; management said it is a best-case view given crude uncertainty.
FY27 gross margin expansion of about 350-400 bps over FY26 exit; operating margin expansion about 150 bps after higher A&P.

FY30 aspirations: revenue to comfortably cross INR20,000 crore, mid-teens EBITDA growth; Foods+PPC share of India business to about one-third by FY30; commodity-linked share to fall from over 70% to 50% over a decade.
Weighted average input cost increase for FY27 described as extremely marginal, with price hikes said to neutralise the impact.
capex_capacity: No specific capacity, utilisation or capex figures were discussed in the call.
Acquisitions cited: 4700BC, Cosmix (profitable, high-teens margin) and Skinetiq (mid-20s margin); integration described as positive with no hiccups, and modern trade synergies started.
Supply chain: company says it is well stocked on raw materials, packaging and finished goods, with no material disruption foreseen near term.
demand_pricing: Demand sentiment broadly stable in Q4; more than 95% of portfolio gaining or sustaining share and over 90% maintaining or improving penetration on MAT basis.
Parachute: copra corrected ~35% from peak, price cut ~10% on non-price-point packs; expects volume pickup visible from Q1 FY27.
Competition: smaller players constrained by packaging, polymer and working-capital pressures; management believes this supports share gains.
Core Saffola Foods grew double digits in Q4; Foods overall growth partly held back by True Elements base effects and SKU rationalisation.
Management flagged risks from West Asia inflation, monsoon onset and a possible strong El Nino affecting H2 FY27 consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EBITDA guidance raised despite acquisition drag and sharp crude-derivative inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a firmer copra view, acquisitions (Cosmix, Skinetiq) already profitable, improved digital margins and procurement synergies; the guidance is a best-case view and stress-tested for crude.

qa_highlights.question: Why are FY27 margins below historic peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak years had low commodity inflation; expansion of 150 bps operating margin is planned, with A&P increased 200-250 bps and denominator effect from revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will Parachute price cuts be cross-subsidised by inflationary categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management takes a portfolio approach, with ~10% cut on non-price-point and small packs; it sees a competitive advantage from smaller players' supply issues rather than cross-subsidising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Plix and its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Plix is at mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin, targeting double digits; D2C is ~45% of the business, and the brand is pivoting to personal care with nutraceutical launches (ACV canned drink).

qa_highlights.question: What are the top risks for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Macro and geopolitical factors, inflation hitting FMCG consumption (especially rural/bottom of pyramid), and a strong El Nino affecting H2 FY27 and Q1 FY28; internal execution is seen as on track.

risks_watch: Crude and crude-derivative inflation (VAHO, packaging) versus copra tailwind; guidance assumes normalisation and management said visibility improves after 1-2 quarters.
Middle East supply disruption and Gulf sales; MENA is 4% of turnover.

Plix scale and growth beyond INR1,000 crore ARR; Foods growth delivery vs 20-25% base case; Bangladesh growth normalisation after 35% quarter.

531642|2026-06.headline: Marico Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 23% and EBITDA/PAT up 25%, with India volume up 11% and FY27 guidance of 20% EBITDA growth.
531642|2026-06.overview: Marico reported a very strong Q1 FY27 with consolidated revenue up 23% and EBITDA and PAT up 25%, its highest profit growth in 28 quarters, on top of a high base. India business grew 11% in volume and 21% in revenue, with Parachute Rigids volume up 10% and VAHO value up 22%. Gross margin expanded 30 bps and EBITDA margin rose 40 bps to 20.7%, even as A&P grew 25%. Management raised confidence in FY27 (revenue above INR15,000 crore, EBITDA growth high-teens aiming for 20%) but flagged higher crude-linked and edible oil input costs from Q2.

segments.name: India - Parachute Rigids
segments.commentary: Volume up 10%, strongest in 20 quarters, with over 400 bps volume share gain; revenue up 23% on anniversarisation of prior price increases and a one-time ~10% price cut on loyalty packs.

segments.name: India - VAHO (value-added hair oils)
segments.commentary: Value up 22%, led by mid and premium hair oils (high-teens volume growth); almond oil targeted at INR100 crore ARR by FY28.

segments.name: India - Saffola Edible Oil
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7% on calibrated pricing; high single-digit volume decline from rationalising select variants to protect threshold profitability.

segments.name: Foods (incl. 4700BC, Cosmix)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 43%, annualised run rate above INR1,300 crore; ex-acquisitions growth is in double digits.

segments.name: Premium Personal Care
segments.commentary: Annualised revenue run rate of around INR450 crore; shampoo targeting ~INR100 crore revenue this year after national launch.

segments.name: Digital-first brands (Beardo, Plix, Cosmix, 4700BC)
segments.commentary: ARR above INR1,100 crore; Beardo at double-digit profitability, Plix high single digit trending to double digit; Plix at ~INR800 crore.

segments.name: International - Vietnam
segments.commentary: Constant currency growth 27%, driven by male and female personal care.

segments.name: International - MENA
segments.commentary: Growth 24%, with Gulf and Egypt both performing well despite inflation and operating challenges in the Gulf.

segments.name: International - Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Constant currency growth 4%, hit by pricing anniversarisation, demand softness from high inflation and fuel price spikes.

segments.name: International - South Africa and new country/export
segments.commentary: South Africa grew 8% (hair care led by Black Chic, Just for Kids, Isoplus); new country development and exports grew 16%.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Core business growth above 50%; about 5% of India revenue excluding digital brands; all digital channels above 20% of India revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing power and competitive intensity in plant protein, collagen and ACV (Plix, Cosmix)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said D2C LTV/CAC and repeat rates are healthy; competition is acceptable for category building, and Plix and Cosmix will not be confined to protein and ACV, with Cosmix at a mid-to-high-teens margin at acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Can almond hair oil reach INR100 crore by FY28 and what about 4700BC and Cosmix versus plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees room for disruption of a leader earning super-normal profit, citing its Amla playbook and SETU distribution; both 4700BC and Cosmix are tracking well and are expected to end the year ahead of initial assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: Parachute price decline outlook and copra risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Total price cut was ~10% on loyalty packs only; copra expected range-bound at 30-35% below peak; only one price drop, no further pricing action; decent volume growth expected in the next one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How to reconcile gross margin and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin likely to be held but gains from copra offset by crude-linked LP/polymer and edible oil costs; full-year reverse math implies 140-150 bps EBITDA margin expansion for INR15,000 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% Parachute volume growth organic, and is India 11% like-for-like?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; no grammage changes, 11% India volume is organic and excludes 4700BC and Cosmix; 10% called an aberration against mid-single-digit guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is A&P growing only 9% at consolidated level, and what about the tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P grew 25% in the quarter, funded from cost tailwinds and acquisitions being capital outlay; tax rate ~17.5% this quarter, guided ~18% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for VAHO and Saffola volume decline risk?
qa_highlights.answer: VAHO mid-and-premium volume up high teens with double-digit trajectory expected and high-teens targeted; Saffola mid-single-digit volume growth considered fine as it pivots toward food.

531761|2026-03.headline: Apollo Pipes targets INR400 crore Q1 FY27 revenue and 35% revenue CAGR to INR5,000 crore by FY31 after FY26 consol EBITDA fell 30%.
531761|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as volatile: PVC fell 15% in the first 8 months, rallied 75% over the next 4, then fell 25% in 2 months to about INR84/kg. Standalone volume rose 7% and Kisan was flat; the company crossed 1 lakh tonnes of annual sales volume and consolidated EBITDA fell 30% on inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing and fixed costs of new verticals. Q4 revenue was about INR350 crore at NSR of about INR110/kg, and management guided to INR400 crore for Q1 FY27 with double-digit volume growth. Management expects Kisan to be merged into Apollo Pipes later, and South India plant to go live around FY28 end.

financial_highlights.value: up 7% YoY; crossed 1 lakh tonne annual volume

financial_highlights.change: vs INR60 crore in Q3 (volume 5,000 tonne)

segments.name: Apollo Pipes standalone (PVC pipes)
segments.commentary: Target EBITDA of INR8,000-10,000/tonne (about 10% margin), with spreads expected to rise from INR8,000 to INR8,500-9,000/tonne. Plumbing construction is about 60-65% of sales; agri and government infra about 35-40%.

segments.name: Kisan Mouldings
segments.commentary: Currently barely breakeven, with EBITDA of about -1% to -2% over the last 4 quarters. Targets INR5,000-6,000/tonne sustainable EBITDA, with a plan to scale to INR500 crore, then INR1,000 crore revenue at 10-12% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Window profiles and allied products
segments.commentary: Contributes about 1.5% of total sales, sold per length rather than per kg; present in North and South India. Expected to contribute at least 4-5% of construction plumbing revenue this year.

segments.commentary: CPVC grew about 10% in FY26 and is expected to grow more than 20% in FY27 with Lubrizol tie-up support; water tanks grew 20-30%.

5-year plan: 35% revenue CAGR to INR5,000 crore by FY31; industry assumed to grow 7-8%, with market share rising from about 2-2.5% to 3-3.5% in 3-4 years.
Standalone EBITDA target INR8,000-10,000/tonne (about 10% margin); consolidated EBITDA per tonne expected to move from INR6,000-8,000 toward INR10,000-12,000 over 2-3 years.

Kisan to be merged into Apollo Pipes Limited; timeline to be shared in coming investor calls.

New South India plant (Malur/Tumkur/Bangalore belt): land work to start after about a year; go-live about 18 months after land finalisation, expected around FY28 end.

Current installed capacity cited as INR3,000 crore revenue potential, against INR1,100 crore FY26 revenue.
demand_pricing: Demand described as encouraging; April was good but below expectations after a strong March channel fill. Agri demand is good and rural is outperforming urban over the last 2-3 months.
Channel inventory is low to normal after destocking; channel refilling from May and June, a seasonal quarter.

PVC resin: Reliance around INR84-85/kg vs local trade about INR79/kg. Management expects a move of plus/minus 5% in the near term; the duty exemption ends 30 June, after which 8.25% duty applies and may push prices up.
Expected import surge for 15-30 days before duty returns; management expects monsoon demand pressure in Q2.
Gross margin fell YoY and QoQ despite 13-14% higher realisation, due to aggressive pricing, window profile sampling costs and write-downs on unsold finished goods; inventory gains were negligible.
Competition has intensified over 3-4 years with price war among organised players; management expects capacity clean-up of small unorganised players.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall despite higher realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited aggressive pricing to rebuild volume, window profile sampling costs, and write-downs from clearing unsold finished-goods inventory. Raw material inventory gains were negligible.

qa_highlights.question: Is April volume on track for the INR400 crore Q1 target after destocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track, with channel inventory already low and refilling from May; April was light after a heavy March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kisan performance disappoint in Q4 and what happens next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jan-Feb demand was weak, so push sales hurt margins; Q4 revenue rose to INR80 crore with volume up to about 7,000 tonne, and margins should improve from Q1 with operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and when will the South India plant come?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR100 crore. The South plant is expected around FY28 end, about 18 months after land is finalised, with work starting after roughly a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise and when will they normalise?

531761|2026-06.headline: Apollo Pipes Q1 FY27 volumes flat YoY; normalised consolidated EBITDA margin 7% after inventory write-downs, with Q2 guided to double-digit YoY volume growth.
531761|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was soft: total sales volume was flat YoY as PVC resin prices fell Rs.32/kg in April and Rs.5/kg in June, hitting primary and secondary demand in April. Normalised consolidated business EBITDA margin was 7% (Apollo standalone 8%, Kisan standalone 6%), with the gap to reported numbers mostly inventory write-downs, plus about 0.5% cost from new businesses (Varanasi plant and Window profiles). Management says prices have stabilised since a MIP of $766/MT (about Rs.82/kg) was imposed about 12 days before the call, and expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and H2 better than H1. Management maintained high double-digit volume growth ambition and reiterated 7-8% business EBITDA margin for the next 12-15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What one-offs related to new businesses were in Q1 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Upfront costs for Varanasi ramp-up and salary costs for building a Window profile ground team; the new businesses cost about 0.5% of Apollo standalone margin, and the rest of the margin gap was inventory write-down.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-8% margin achievable near term given competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said business margin was 8% at Apollo and 6-7% at Kisan before inventory losses; expects to maintain 7-8% at company level, with 50-100 bps upside as new plants stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the inventory loss in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure, saying the majority of the gap between the 7% normalised margin and reported EBITDA was inventory losses.

qa_highlights.question: Is PVC resin availability an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Recent delays were due to port rains delaying container de-stuffing, not supply shortage; material normally arrives within about 10 days and importers are returning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kisan volume and profitability picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume flat at about 5,500 tons per quarter for four quarters, versus nearly 7,000 tons in Q4 FY26; plant can do 8,000-8,500 tons per quarter; business EBITDA about 5-6% but reported P&L is weaker due to inventory losses and weak industry.

qa_highlights.question: Segment volume growth and return ratio math?
qa_highlights.answer: No segment-level growth given; CPVC and water tanks growing, government infra near zero. Return math kept: Rs.1,500 crore gross block plus Rs.300-400 crore working capital on Rs.5,000 crore revenue at 10-12% EBITDA gives about 25% ROC.

531768|2026-03.headline: Poly Medicure Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 21% YoY to INR534 crore; FY27 consolidated guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore with margin pressure from raw-material costs.

FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12.3% to INR1,875 crore, while standalone grew about 4% to INR1,662 crore and standalone EBITDA margin came in at 26.8%. Management flagged a raw-material cost increase of about 20% linked to crude, plus freight and wage pressure, and said gross margin could fall to roughly 66% (200-300 bps lower) on current conditions. FY27 guidance calls for consolidated revenue of INR2,300-2,400 crore and standalone of INR1,900-1,950 crore, with capex of INR200-225 crore.

West Asia disruption: about 6-8% of revenue from the region; demand described as intact, but shipments are delayed by logistics bottlenecks.

Europe: management says demand has recovered over the last 3-4 months after over-inventory and slowdown; distributors added in Northern Europe, UK and Germany. Management targets about 15% growth in Europe.

Export receivables rose because the company extended better credit terms to international customers to support volumes; management expects receivable cycle similar in FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Brazil target is a small, non-operating medical-device storage and distribution company acquired for about USD40,000, saving 18-24 months. Citieffe and PendraCare are each about 50% Europe and 50% RoW; Citieffe also has about 35-40% in North America and Mexico.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition is from imports, not domestic players. Renal growth target for FY27 is about 20%, versus an earlier 30-35%, because of Chinese competition and cost inversion.

qa_highlights.answer: Standalone inventory rose about INR30 crore, with finished goods around INR30-35 crore (5-6 days). Receivable days rose from 68 to 86 mainly because of international customers, and management expects a similar cycle in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin dip QoQ despite growth in higher-margin products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q4 dip to product mix, with some lower-margin products in the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time INR9 crore cost and what was the acquired businesses' EBITDA impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR9 crore was transaction-related adviser costs and regulatory and employee provisions booked at year-end at international entities; no manpower rationalisation. The acquired entities had a negative EBITDA impact of about INR2.6 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable organic growth rate and the long-term revenue mix target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FY27 guidance of over 25% consolidated growth and 15-16% standalone growth. Long-term target is about one-third India and two-thirds RoW.

532067|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue about INR142 crore and PAT nearly INR60 crore; management guides 15-20% growth for FY27 across the group.

Standalone non-export revenue grew about 7.1% and exports about 25%, and the company guided to 15-20% growth in FY27 with margins broadly maintained. Coris carries a loss-making first half and is guided to be only slightly EBITDA positive in FY27, while management said M&A is still under way with no deal closed.

532134|2026-03.headline: Bank of Baroda Q4 FY26 net profit rose 11.2% YoY to a record Rs 5,616 crore; FY26 net profit Rs 20,021 crore, with FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14%.
532134|2026-03.overview: Global business crossed Rs 30 lakh crore at Rs 30.78 lakh crore (+13.9% YoY), with global advances up 16.2% and total deposits up 12%. Q4 operating profit was Rs 9,069 crore (+11.5% YoY) and NII grew 8.7%, with NIM at 2.89% (+10 bps QoQ) helped partly by interest on income-tax refunds. Asset quality improved (GNPA 1.89%, net NPA 0.45%), but Q4 credit cost rose to 0.76% after a Rs 1,500 crore floating provision funded from IT refunds. Management raised FY27 loan and deposit growth guidance and set a Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 raise plan, while cautioning that cost of deposits will stay sticky in Q1 given tight liquidity and West Asia tensions.

532143|2026-03.headline: SKM Egg Products FY26 sales rose 58% to ₹767 crore and PAT crossed ₹100 crore for the first time (₹102 crore).

Q4 FY26 sales were ₹197 crore, with PBT ₹41 crore and PAT ₹32 crore against ₹9.7 crore and ₹6.22 crore a year earlier. Management said powder capacity is now running at full utilisation, so FY27 volume growth will be modest. The company is funding a ₹400 crore layer-shed expansion (about 20 lakh birds, completion targeted 2028-29) and is bringing the associate SKM Universal into the listed entity.

rows.why: Management guided Q2 FY27 realisation above Rs 700/kg, possibly Rs 720-750 versus Rs 770 this quarter, and egg white prices may improve 2-3/4, but the rupee-led gains and high processor inventories make upside uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Soya feed cost pressure is expected to persist for at least two more quarters and cannot be passed on, while realisation guidance range (Rs 720-750) sits below the Rs 770 print and depends on the exchange rate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Branded domestic eggs structure set up with business plan due end-March and Rs 40-50 crore turnover to be added this year; organic fertiliser to reach commercial sale by September; Japan business expected in H2 FY27 after 1-2 month approval delay.

rows.label: Japan office approval and new business
rows.why: Approval delayed 1-2 months for resubmission with direct contracts already in place; new business expected in the second half of the year, with no revenue figure given.

rows.label: Europe summer demand and egg white pricing
rows.why: Management said Europe's severe summer could support demand toward the end of the financial year and egg white prices may improve 2-3/4, but processors still hold high inventories.

rows.label: Easy-shed cost advantage
rows.why: Management said easy sheds give a minimum 5% reduction in overall production cost from higher productivity and feed efficiency, but no timing or amount was given before completion.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term capacity plans and the Rs 720-750 realisation range but was vague on numbers, deferring capex amounts, branded margins and ROCE; analysts pushed on pricing drivers, ROCE on easy-shed and biogas capex, and branded contribution.

532143|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 turnover ~363 crore vs 380 crore, PAT ~40 crore flat; Q2 PAT fell to ~16 crore as feed raw material costs rose.
532143|2026-09.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as broadly flat year on year: turnover about 363 crore versus 380 crore, EBITDA about 67-44 crore (transcript reads "6744 crores", unclear) and PAT about 40 crore in both periods. Q2 turnover rose to about 184 crore from 179 crore in Q1, but EBITDA fell to about 28 crore from 38 crore as feed raw material costs increased. Q2 PBT was about 22 crore (32 crore in Q1) and PAT about 16 crore (24 crore in Q1). Management guided to a 100 crore-plus profit for the full year but declined to give quarterly guidance, and the company is in a heavy capex phase funded largely by term debt.

segments.name: Egg powder / egg products
segments.commentary: Powder sales were 1,625 MT in Q2 versus 1,831 MT in Q1, and 3,457 MT in H1 versus 4,289 MT in the prior-year half. Average realisation was cited at about 700 rupees per unit, with management expecting 700-plus in H2 and volumes slightly better.

segments.name: Domestic shell eggs / branded eggs
segments.commentary: Management said it currently sells about 1.5 lakh eggs a day in the branded egg segment and targets 5 lakh eggs a day in two to three years. Business model, segment (premium vs mass) and pricing are still under internal discussion, with a decision expected in about three months.

segments.name: SKM Universal (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Board approved merger of SKM Universal into the listed company; it will cease to exist by April next year. Management said scale-up plans begin in FY28, and a 17.5 crore goodwill-like item in Q2 was described as a share purchase cost from a sister company.

guidance_outlook: Full-year PAT of 100 crore-plus reiterated, described as a ballpark figure; no quarterly guidance given, citing SEBI limits and export volatility.
Next six months expected to continue the past six months with a small margin improvement; more aggressive growth expected from next financial year.
Average realisations not expected to correct significantly over the next six months; Japan pricing reduced due to US oversupply, with pressure elsewhere limited.
Real sales increment from the expanded capacity expected from FY28-FY29; no top-line or bottom-line numbers given.
Dividend payout to be maintained at about 25% even during the high-investment and debt phase.
capex_capacity: EC (layer) farm phase two: 2.4 million birds target by September 28; first rearing house expected complete in about two weeks, chicks to be placed from November 15; project running about one week behind schedule.
Board approved term loan of nearly 300 crore (200 crore State Bank, 100 crore Access Bank); documents to be signed the following week.
Powder capacity expansion from 7,000 to 10,000+ tons at about 180 crore (30 crore margin, about 150 crore term loan at 8.25%), with capacity commissioning around H2 FY28 and 3-5 years to fill.
Management described total debt for the investment phase as about 450 crore.
Cash of about 167 crore held; management said about 100 crore is kept as a minimum for seasonality.
demand_pricing: US oversupply of eggs is reducing prices in Japan; management said pressure elsewhere has been limited and international prices are set by global competitors (Europe, Ukraine, South America, Mexico), not by Indian costs.

Feed raw material (soya and other ingredients) costs rose sharply in Q2; the company cannot fix prices in contracts and has no pass-through mechanism. Management could not confirm pass-through to customers.
Management plans to import soya for about six months of requirement, expected to be about 10% cheaper than local prices; implementation expected in a week or two.
South Korea: two customers have approved samples; bigger trial shipment is under way, with a first order targeted for October-December quarter.
Freight costs rose due to the US-Iran conflict and the Ukraine-Russia war; management said the rupee depreciation offsets part of this and demand has not been affected.

qa_highlights.question: What are realisations outlook for the next six months, and will domestic sales drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US oversupply has hit Japan pricing only; average realisation is about 700 rupees and not expected to correct much. Grading equipment arrives by April, and a relaunch strategy will follow, with the business model still under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Will profit stay around 100 crore for the year, and can raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very confident of repeating 100-plus crore this year. It said international prices are set by global competition, not Indian cost, so pass-through is uncertain; soya imports and backward integration are the offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Will quarterly profits exceed 16 crore in the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly projections, saying it did not think SEBI permits it, and reiterated only the 100 crore-plus ballpark for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion receive interest subvention, and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: The 3% interest subvention applies only to farm investment, not egg processing. Powder expansion is about 180 crore with 150 crore term loan at 8.25%; benefits from the farms come gradually and fully by September 28.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold about 167 crore cash while borrowing 300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps about 100 crore for seasonality and that its cost of funds is about 5.25% after 3% interest subvention; it targets returns above 10% on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will branded domestic eggs become a substantial part of turnover within two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to become an important revenue stream within two to five years, but segment choice (premium, mid, or mass) is still being decided and should be firmed up in about three months.

risks_watch: Feed cost inflation (soya and other ingredients) compressing EBITDA; Q2 EBITDA fell to about 28 crore from 38 crore.
Japanese price pressure from US oversupply and softening international egg-powder prices.
EC farm commissioning slippage (already about one week behind) and the 2.4 million bird target by September 28.
Debt rising to about 450 crore for the investment phase, with finance costs and dividend policy (25% payout) to watch.
Branded domestic egg strategy and business model still undecided; decision expected in about three months.
Freight cost increases from geopolitical events; South Korea first order targeted October-December.
532143|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the 100-crore-plus full-year profit target, but guarded on quarterly numbers, pass-through of costs, and the timing of the domestic branded egg strategy. Management repeatedly stated that it cannot give quarterly guidance and that the business model is still being worked out.
key_quotes: Yes, we are very confident of repeating 100 plus this year.
So, to be cash surplus in a growth phase is an important criterion than the risk that we have on having a bigger loan.
So, we will try to maintain the 25% even during the high investment phase and the debt period.
So, after all the equipment for grading and will be in place by April next year, we will be relaunching new strategy for growth.

rows.why: Egg powder volume fell to 1,625 MT in Q2 from 1,831 MT in Q1 and 3,457 MT in H1 from 4,289 MT a year earlier, so growth is flat-to-slightly-positive near term; real volume increment from expanded capacity is expected only from FY28-FY29.

rows.why: Capex is already under way: the board approved a term loan of nearly 300 crore (200 crore SBI, 100 crore Access Bank) with documents to be signed the following week, and the powder expansion of about 180 crore is approved; total investment-phase debt is about 450 crore.

rows.label: Feed cost pass-through and soya import hedge
rows.why: Feed raw material costs rose sharply in Q2 with no contractual pass-through, and management plans soya imports for about six months at roughly 10% below local prices, implementation in a week or two; realisation about 700 rupees per kg is not expected to correct much.

rows.why: Two South Korean customers have approved samples and a bigger trial shipment is under way, with the first order targeted for the October-December quarter; size not disclosed.

532149|2026-06.headline: Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.23% YoY to Rs 3,068 crore; Global NIM eased to 2.52% and FY27 guidance was kept unchanged.
532149|2026-06.overview: Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs 3,068 crore, up 36.23% YoY, with operating profit up 25.99% to Rs 5,051 crore and NII up 12.61% to Rs 6,833 crore. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with Gross NPA at 1.81% and Net NPA at 0.51%, and slippage ratio at 0.24%. Global business grew 16.57% YoY to Rs 17.55 lakh crore, with advances up 18.64%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for advances growth of 15-16% and deposit growth of 13-14%, and raised a dollar-funding target of $4.2 billion through FCNR(B), OFCB/MTN and ECB routes by December 2026.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -111 bps YoY; NNPA -24 bps YoY

segments.name: Global business and deposits
segments.commentary: Global business Rs 17.55 lakh crore (+16.57% YoY). Global deposits Rs 9.58 lakh crore (+14.90%); domestic deposits Rs 8.25 lakh crore (+16.15%). CASA Rs 3.02 lakh crore, CASA ratio 36.68%.

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global gross advances Rs 7.98 lakh crore (+18.64% YoY); domestic advances Rs 6.74 lakh crore (+19.20%). RAM advances Rs 3.93 lakh crore (+19.75%), 58.30% of advances.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at yield of about 9.10%, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International business touched about Rs 2.56 lakh crore; around 32% of international loan book is trade finance, which management plans to reduce.

segments.name: Mutual fund subsidiary
segments.commentary: Bank of India mutual fund AUM about Rs 16,000-17,000 crore; no near-term plan for public issue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guidance unchanged at 15-16%; global deposit growth guidance unchanged at 13-14%.
Global NIM guidance for FY27 at 2.55%-2.60%, though management said NIMs are under challenge.
Cost-to-income ratio at about 46% in Q1, but guided to 48%-49% on a consistent basis during FY27.
ROA guidance of 1% and above on a consistent quarter-on-quarter basis in FY27 (Q4 FY26 1.01%, Q1 FY27 about 1%).
FCNR(B) target of $1.2 billion by 30 September 2026; OFCB/MTN target about $2 billion by 31 December 2026; ECB target about $1 billion; total dollar raising about $4.2 billion by December 2026.
capex_capacity: Opened a dedicated Strategic Business Branch in Mumbai for high-value pool buyouts, co-lending, TReDS and supply chain financing.
Centralised Video KYC centre operationalised in Mumbai for end-to-end digital account opening.
Around 22% of domestic credit book now sanctioned digitally; data lake and CRM Next linked lead flow has built business of more than Rs 18,000 crore.
ATM network rationalised: loss-making capex-model ATMs exited, reducing total ATM count by about 300.
Plans to add 19 emerging corporate credit branches' focus on Rs 25-250 crore mid-corporate advances; credit card base target of 3 lakh by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Corporate plus international pipeline about Rs 70,000 crore; total loan pipeline above Rs 1 lakh crore including RAM, digital, pool purchase, TReDS and supply chain financing.

FCNR(B) deposits: about $200 million garnered so far; three-year FCNR at 6.25%, 3-4 year at 6.30%, five-year at 6.50%; leverage product up to nine times; management cited a spread of about 50 bps on five-year deposits, with CRR/SLR not applicable.
Management declined to give current leverage spread, citing a moving target in borrowing and dollar rates; leveraged share of FCNR not quantified.
Personal loans grew only about 3% YoY after guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans.
ECLGS: about Rs 6,000 crore sanctioned, Rs 4,600 crore disbursed; expected total sanctions and disbursal of about Rs 8,000 crore by scheme end.
SMA-0 for accounts of Rs 5 crore and above fell to about Rs 4,090 crore (0.52% of standard book), from about Rs 4,700 crore at March 2026 and above Rs 7,000 crore at June 2025.
Q1 fresh slippages including incremental NPA debits about Rs 1,800 crore vs Rs 2,100 crore in Q1 FY26; sectors under watch include chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas importers/exporters.
PSL income about Rs 277 crore in Q1; management said further PSL income possible in Q2 and Q3 but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Is stress visible in MSME and small loan accounts from the West Asia crisis, and what is the ECLGS position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMA and slippages show no major stress; ECLGS sanctions of about Rs 6,000 crore with Rs 4,600 crore disbursed, expected to reach about Rs 8,000 crore. Certain sectors are being monitored closely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB plan and how does the leverage product work?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) target is $1.2 billion by 30 September; OFCB/MTN about $2 billion by 31 December; ECB about $1 billion (about $500 million already approved in principle). Leverage product is up to nine times, with three-year FCNR at 6.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at about 9.10% yield, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore; three-notice, 90-day auction SOP applied.

qa_highlights.question: Why did personal loans grow only 3%, and what is the credit card plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans, shifting to salaried and service-sector borrowers with NACH. Credit card base target is 3 lakh by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CASA and retail term deposit ratios fall while cost of deposits dropped 15 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly 3% fall in CASA and retail term deposit share, as bulk deposits above Rs 3 crore were used to fund credit growth; cost of deposits was reduced via Rs 3-25 crore FD campaign and mix changes.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM and CIR hold, and how will yields on advances move?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is NIM 2.55%-2.60% and CIR 48%-49% for FY27. Yields on advances expected to pause falling, supported by MCLR-linked loans, mid-corporate growth and reduced low-margin trade finance.

risks_watch: Dollar-raising targets ($4.2 billion) depend on FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB windows (FCNR to 30 September; OFCB/MTN to 31 December 2026); leverage spreads are moving.
NIM under pressure from the interest rate environment and West Asia developments; guidance requires 2.55%-2.60% vs 2.52% in Q1.
CIR guidance steps up to 48%-49% from about 46% in Q1, implying higher costs ahead.
Stress in chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas-linked import/export accounts; Q1 is seasonally high for slippages per management.
Declining CASA ratio (36.68%) and retail term deposits; cost of deposits benefit depends on bulk and FCNR mix.
Treasury gains in Q1 may not repeat as yields move adversely.
532149|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, asset quality and profitability, with guidance reiterated unchanged. Cautious on NIM, the West Asia impact and sector stress, and evasive on FCNR spreads and leverage economics and on the PSU merger question.

So , we are very confident that Quite a few.
Yes, $1.2 billion is our target that we have set for ourselves that and we are very confident that we'll be achieving it very quickly.
