rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Global advances up 18.64% YoY to Rs 7.98 lakh crore and FY27 guidance held at 15-16%, backed by a Rs 1 lakh crore+ loan pipeline including Rs 70,000 crore corporate and international.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex or utilisation was not discussed; the call gave no capacity utilisation figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was reiterated unchanged on advances, deposits, NIM, CIR and ROA, and CIR is guided to step up from about 46% in Q1 to 48%-49%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 NIM of 2.52% must rise to 2.55%-2.60%, CIR must rise from about 46% to 48%-49%, and the $4.2 billion dollar raise depends on FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB windows with moving spreads.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: FCNR(B) leverage product (up to nine times) and FCNR rates of 6.25%-6.50% are already live, and a Mumbai Strategic Business Branch has opened, but no new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Rs 1 lakh crore+ loan pipeline
rows.why: Total pipeline above Rs 1 lakh crore, including Rs 70,000 crore corporate and international, backs FY27 advances growth guidance of 15-16%.

rows.label: Dollar raise of $4.2 billion by December 2026
rows.why: FCNR(B) target $1.2 billion by 30 September, OFCB/MTN about $2 billion and ECB about $1 billion; only about $200 million of FCNR garnered so far.

rows.label: ECLGS disbursal to about Rs 8,000 crore
rows.why: About Rs 6,000 crore sanctioned and Rs 4,600 crore disbursed so far, with total expected at about Rs 8,000 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on advances growth, asset quality (GNPA 1.81%, SMA-0 down to Rs 4,090 crore) and ROA about 1%, but cautious on NIM (2.52%), the West Asia impact and sector stress, and evasive on FCNR leverage spreads and the PSU merger question.

532149|2026-09.headline: Bank of India Q2 FY27: H1 net profit about Rs 6,000 crore, Global NIM 2.47%, Gross NPA 1.60%; ECL front-loading planned from Q3, about 0.5% CRAR impact per year.
532149|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong YoY growth: global business up 21.13% to Rs 18.92 lakh crore, and global advances up 20.58%. Operating profit rose 33.18% to Rs 5,089 crore and net profit rose 25.32% to Rs 3,202 crore for Sept'26 (the Q2 figure as stated on the call). Asset quality improved, with Gross NPA at 1.60% and Net NPA at 0.42%, and credit cost fell to 0.12% from 0.15% in June'26. Global NIM eased 5 bps YoY to 2.47%, which management attributed mainly to FCNR-linked leverage. Management guided FY27 global advances growth of 15-16% and global deposit growth of 16-17%, and said ECL provisioning will begin from Q3 after Board approval.

financial_highlights.change: +Rs 20,539 crore YoY; ratio down from prior quarters
down 5 bps from 2.52% (management cited Sept'25 at 2.41%)

segments.name: Corporate and pipeline
segments.commentary: Corporate pipeline about Rs 65,000 crore as of 30 Sept; total pipeline across corporate, RAM, digital, pool/co-lending and supply chain about Rs 86,000-87,000 crore. Largest sector pipelines are renewable energy (over Rs 12,000 crore), power (over Rs 9,000 crore) and roads (over Rs 5,000 crore).

segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances up 18.68% YoY to Rs 4.13 lakh crore, 58.63% of gross advances, with RAM pipeline about Rs 20,000 crore.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 61,000 crore, mostly agriculture with some MSME and retail; gold loan NPA about 0.13%, LTV capped at 75%.

segments.name: Overseas book
segments.commentary: Overseas advances up 35.21% YoY to Rs 1.51 lakh crore against overseas deposits up 11.52% to Rs 1.37 lakh crore; FCNR raise of USD 2.2 billion was deployed into the international loan book.

segments.name: Supply chain / trade
segments.commentary: Supply chain book just over Rs 1,000 crore, with a Rs 1,500 crore first-year target; trade and MSME-linked assets grew about 10% in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guided at 15-16% and global deposit growth at 16-17%.
ROA guided above 1% on a quarterly basis; management said ROA was above 1% in March'26, June'26 and Sept'26, and expects above 1% in March'27. FY28 expected to be better.

ECL: provisions expected to start from Q3 FY27 after Board approval, with Q3 and Q4 as front-loading quarters; ECL regime applies from 1 April 2027. Ballpark CRAR impact about 0.5% per year over the next 4 years.
NIM expected to gain about 6-7 bps from the 25 bps repo hike, with deposit repricing staggered because about 60% of term deposits mature in 1 to 18 months.
Recovery in written-off accounts expected to sustain the run rate of about Rs 900-1,000 crore a quarter; non-interest income expected to hold above Rs 2,500 crore a quarter.
capex_capacity: Technology budget for opex and capex (core IT, digital, cybersecurity) said to be unchanged for FY27; Big Four consultants engaged on IT, digital and cybersecurity transformation.
AI policy approved by the Board; current AI use is predictive (Data Lake project), with analytics-led leads above Rs 21,000 crore.
Centralised supply chain branch in Mumbai handles pool, co-lending, trades and supply chain; 69 zones each asked to onboard one new supply chain vendor per month.
ECL: consultant onboarded; computation covers PD, LGD and SICR; Board note to be presented, with clarity expected by Q3.
demand_pricing: Domestic deposit and advances growth remained strong YoY, with management saying no impact from the macro headwinds is foreseen on FY27 business growth.
66% of domestic advances are repo-linked; the bank passed on the 25 bps repo hike on the day of the ALCO meeting.
Management said that about 7% of the retail portfolio is unsecured.
Infra: outstanding roughly flat YoY despite sanctions; some COD projects refinanced by other lenders at low rates, leading to churn; full disbursement takes 7-8 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the ECL provisioning need, how much is already provided, and what is the road ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the broad total will not be shared until the Board note; the CRAR impact is about 0.5% per year over 4 years, covered by profits (H1 profit above Rs 6,000 crore, run rate of about Rs 12,000 crore for FY27). No ECL provision has been made yet; front-loading expected from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank still meet its growth targets given global and drought headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no impact on FY27 business growth at present, citing a pipeline of about 10% of the loan book, GST collections above Rs 2 lakh crore a month and e-way bills of Rs 13-14 crore a month.

qa_highlights.question: How much can NIM improve from the rate hike, and how will CASA be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: The FCNR raise cost about 5 bps of NIM. The repo hike is expected to add 6-7 bps, with a lag on deposits. Bulk deposits are being used to fund credit growth, while retail term deposits are about 43% of total deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What drove non-interest income, and why is other income down?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries from written-off accounts rose about 190% YoY to Rs 978 crore, and treasury/forex profit rose 157% to Rs 411 crore. Non-interest income was Rs 2,700 crore, up 25% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in the gold loan book after NBFC concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan NPA is about 0.13%. Management said the SOP calls for two notices before auction, the CBS system monitors LTV, and the LTV is capped at 75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the government stake and any capital raise plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding is 73.8%, within the 75% SEBI limit. No government indication to reduce stake further and no capital raise plan.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027: quantum of front-loading and CRAR impact, pending Board approval and the Q3 update.
NIM pressure from the FCNR leverage and falling CASA ratio (34.16%); pace of deposit repricing after the repo hike.
Dependence on lumpy recoveries from written-off accounts for non-interest income; 2-3 large accounts drove the quarter.
Macro risks: West Asia crisis, crude prices, drought and El Nino effects in parts of Maharashtra, and possible further RBI rate hikes.
Overseas advances growing 35% YoY against 11.5% overseas deposit growth, which lifts reliance on FCNR funding.
532149|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and profitability, with management stressing the strength of its systems. It was more cautious and deflecting on ECL quantum, CASA ratio and macro risks, and gave no number on the total ECL requirement.
key_quotes: So, ECL impact, we have already started doing the computation and other kinds of things, whether it is the PD, whether it is the LGD, SICR, and other kinds of things.
So, we expect that from Q3 onwards we will be making the provisions.
At present, we do not see any impact which may have on our business growth numbers for this financial year.

rows.why: Management expects NIM to gain about 6-7 bps from the 25 bps repo hike, with 66% of domestic advances repo-linked, partly offset by staggered deposit repricing (about 60% of term deposits mature in 1-18 months); Global NIM was 2.47%, down 5 bps YoY.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 global advances guided at 15-16% and deposits at 16-17%, backed by a corporate pipeline of about Rs 65,000 crore (total ~Rs 86,000-87,000 crore) against global advances of Rs 8.55 lakh crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation or capacity metric disclosed for a bank; capex discussed only as IT budget unchanged for FY27.

rows.why: ECL front-loading from Q3 with about 0.5% CRAR impact per year over 4 years, plus NIM pressure from FCNR leverage (5 bps cost) and CASA ratio down to 34.16%, could pressure reported profit even though H1 profit is above Rs 6,000 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI policy approved and predictive analytics (Data Lake) in use with analytics-led leads above Rs 21,000 crore, and supply chain book just over Rs 1,000 crore against a Rs 1,500 crore first-year target, but no specific product launch was named.

rows.label: ECL regime from 1 April 2027 with front-loading from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Provisioning starts Q3 after Board approval with Q3 and Q4 as front-loading quarters, costing about 0.5% of CRAR per year over 4 years, against H1 profit above Rs 6,000 crore and a run rate of about Rs 12,000 crore for FY27.

rows.label: Recoveries from written-off accounts sustain Rs 900-1,000 crore a quarter
rows.why: Recoveries rose about 190% YoY to Rs 978 crore this quarter, but 2-3 large accounts drove it, so the run rate depends on lumpy recoveries.

rows.label: Overseas book outgrowing overseas deposits
rows.why: Overseas advances rose 35.21% YoY to Rs 1.51 lakh crore against overseas deposits up 11.52% to Rs 1.37 lakh crore, so reliance on FCNR funding rises.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, asset quality (Gross NPA 1.60%, credit cost 0.12%) and profitability, but deflected on the ECL quantum (no total number given), CASA ratio (34.16%) and macro risks; analysts pushed on ECL and NIM.

532156|2026-03.headline: Vaibhav Global FY26: PBT up 41% YoY, record FCF of INR272 crore, EBITDA margin 10.8%; FY27 guidance 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion.
532156|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR935 crore (+10% YoY) with EBITDA of INR96 crore (about 10.3%) and PBT of INR64 crore (+41% YoY). For FY26, revenue was INR3,691 crore, EBITDA margin rose 140 bps to 10.8%, and free cash flow hit a record INR272 crore. In-house brands crossed 50% of B2C sales about a year ahead of plan, and Germany reached full-year EBITDA breakeven. Management guided FY27 to 9-11% revenue growth and a 50-100 bps EBITDA margin improvement, but gave no constant-currency guidance. U.S. and U.K. growth stayed weak in Q4, and the Mindful Souls write-off of about INR25 crore was a notable one-off.

financial_highlights.change: ROE includes one-time MAT credit benefit per management

financial_highlights.value: INR6 per share (incl. final INR1.5 recommended)

segments.name: U.S.
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 1% in local currency; growth driven by digital mix, proprietary brands and AI-led marketing, with an in-house jewellery casting line in the U.S. helping offset tariffs.

segments.name: U.K.
segments.commentary: Q4 headline revenue flat (-1% local currency). Ideal World grew 15% while TJC declined 7%; U.K. EBITDA margin improved 220 bps YoY.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 7%; Germany achieved full-year FY26 EBITDA breakeven and is expected to contribute to group profit from FY27.

segments.name: Mindful Souls
segments.commentary: Digital-first acquisition; INR25 crore write-off taken on conservative impairment testing. Management says the business is still profitable and shows cross-learning benefits; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Positive numbers were seen in the current quarter.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Lifestyle products are ~35% of total sales (medium-term target 50%). Lab-grown diamonds are ~11% of retail revenue at ASP around USD 250 (about 18 months old category).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 9-11% (INR terms).
FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-100 bps; gross margin and employee-cost efficiencies named as main sources, with shipping leverage unlikely this year.
Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 10-12% in INR.
Tax rate steady at around 22% for upcoming years.
Content and broadcasting spend to stay around 20% of sales; SG&A leverage not expected as TV savings are reinvested into digital.
Depreciation to be broadly similar in FY27 vs FY26 after the new U.K. lease; consolidation of 4 buildings into one expected to cut operating costs.
Digital mix target of 50% of B2C sales by end of FY27; long-term peak EBITDA margin of 15% seen as achievable but no precise timeline.
capex_capacity: In-house jewellery casting line operationalised in the U.S. during FY26, reducing tariff impact on shipments.
New U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026; existing buildings to be vacated and move completed during FY27, consolidating 4 buildings into one.
100% of manufacturing power from solar; two U.S. sites and one each in U.K. and Germany run fully on renewable energy.
Capex quantum and timing for FY27 were not discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Volumes fell about 9-10% YoY across TV and digital per an analyst; management attributed this to higher average ticket size (lab-grown demand, higher metal prices) rather than weaker demand, and pointed to customer count, repeat rate and reach as better metrics.
Unique customers at 6.8 lakh in Q4; retention stable at ~38%; average 23 pieces purchased per customer on trailing 12 months; unique customer count fell as low-value one-off customers were dropped.
Digital ~44% of B2C sales in FY26; TV networks reached ~127 million households globally in Q4.

Management reported early-April/May trends: better digital traction in U.S. and U.K., TV audiences still stressed by inflation and higher gas and interest rates; Germany traction better than last quarter.
Elevated precious metal prices and cautious discretionary spend were cited as headwinds across core markets; tariff uncertainty persists.

qa_highlights.question: How can EBITDA margin rise back toward the 13-15% levels seen in FY22 when revenue is much larger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Germany's breakeven and digital/paid media investments weighed on margin; margin rose from 7% (FY23) to 11% (FY26). Leverage expected in HR, SG&A and shipping; peak 15% seen as achievable over time but no precise timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter India, and will the company consider a buyback given the share price decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal said TV shopping never took off in India, so entry would be digital-only, to be considered after digital maturity in the Western markets. No buyback response was given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Lifestyle 50% target versus in-house jewellery mix: are these contradictory?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Panwad clarified that in-house brands are 50% of B2C, of which 85% is jewellery and 15% lifestyle; the 35% lifestyle share and 50% medium-term target are for total group sales, including external and umbrella brands.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins flat over three years despite digital mix shift, lab-grown and higher ASPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B sales growth (lower gross margin, no content cost) dilutes gross margin; Q4 gross margin rose ~180 bps and FY26 ~40 bps. Tariffs and metal spikes were a substantial headwind, and paid media channel margins are rising.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the 50-100 bps margin improvement come from, and what constant-currency growth to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin first, then employee cost efficiency; shipping leverage unlikely this year and SG&A not expected to leverage. No constant-currency guidance given; INR guidance used given macro and business transition.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a INR25 crore Mindful Souls write-off and what drove other expenses up ~16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment reflects conservative testing as double-digit growth did not materialise; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Other expenses rose on U.K. warehouse set-up, travel and AI technology spend, which management called temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in ROE and the ROU asset increase?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE was driven by PAT growth including a one-time MAT credit; normalised ROE still improves to ~15%. ROU increase is from a new U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Trends for U.S. growth and visibility from AI initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal cited AI across ad creatives, landing pages, conversion analytics and supply-chain forecasting, started about a year ago and accelerating recently. He expects U.S. and U.K. to reach double-digit growth in mid-to-long term but gave no timeline.

risks_watch: U.S. and U.K. top-line growth remained low (1% and -1% local currency in Q4); FY27 guidance depends on digital traction and Germany progress.
Tariff uncertainty in the U.S. and elevated precious metal prices pressuring discretionary demand and ticket sizes.
Mindful Souls impairment (INR25 crore) and payback extended to 7 years; further write-downs possible.
Digital marketing and AI investments may keep SG&A and content costs elevated (TV broadcasting ~20% of sales), limiting margin expansion.
Declining unique customer count (6.8 lakh) and volume trends; need to track whether quality-customer focus converts to growth.
Shipping costs may rise due to geopolitical disruption (management referenced Asian crisis and war).
532156|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins, cash flow and Germany, but cautious and somewhat evasive on U.S./U.K. growth, constant-currency guidance and tariff outlook. Management repeatedly deflected volume declines and the unique customer decline toward quality-of-customer metrics.
key_quotes: Profit before tax grew 41% year-on-year.
Germany has turned EBITDA positive for the full year, and we generated our highest ever free cash flow of INR272 crores in FY '26.
So overall unique customers, we monitor based on how many quality of customers we're acquiring.
So volume may not be the right barometer for you to look at it.

rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided up 50-100 bps from 10.8% in FY26, led by gross margin and employee-cost efficiencies; Q4 gross margin rose ~180 bps and FY26 ~40 bps, though shipping leverage is unlikely and SG&A is not expected to leverage.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at 9-11% in INR, but volumes fell about 9-10% YoY per an analyst, unique customers fell to 6.8 lakh, and U.S. and U.K. growth was only 1% and -1% local currency in Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex quantum and timing for FY27 were not discussed; the only facility move is the U.K. premises lease already signed, with no utilisation figure given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guide of 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion is new, with no constant-currency guidance and a weak U.S./U.K. backdrop (1% and -1% local currency in Q4).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: U.S. and U.K. top-line growth stayed weak, tariff uncertainty persists, precious metal prices are elevated, and management flagged geopolitical shipping cost risk; FY27 depends on digital traction and Germany progress.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product, brand or model launch was named on the call; lab-grown diamonds are an existing category (~11% of retail revenue).

rows.label: Germany contributes to group profit from FY27
rows.why: Germany reached full-year FY26 EBITDA breakeven and Q4 revenue grew 7%, with management expecting it to contribute to group profit from FY27.

rows.label: Mindful Souls payback extended to 7 years
rows.why: INR25 crore impairment taken and payback extended from 5 to 7 years after double-digit growth did not materialise, so further write-downs are possible.

rows.label: Digital mix reaches 50% of B2C by end FY27
rows.why: Digital was ~44% of B2C sales in FY26 and management said it remains on track for 50% by end FY27, ahead of the earlier in-house brand milestone already crossed.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, cash flow and Germany breakeven, but cautious and deflecting on U.S./U.K. growth, constant-currency guidance and tariffs; analysts pushed on volume declines (~9-10%), the falling unique customer count and the Mindful Souls write-off.

532156|2026-06.headline: Vaibhav Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.7% to INR917 crore and EBITDA rose 37% to INR102 crore, but constant-currency revenue was broadly flat.
532156|2026-06.overview: Reported revenue grew 12.7% YoY to INR917 crore, EBITDA rose 37% to INR102 crore (margin 11% vs 9.2%), and PAT rose 50% to INR56 crore. Management said reported growth was helped by favourable FX and a U.S. tariff refund of about INR38 crore, of which INR25 crore sits in other operating revenue and flows fully to gross profit and EBITDA. Excluding the refund, B2C growth in USD was largely flat, with the U.S. up 4% and U.K. flat in local currency and Germany up 6%. FY27 guidance of 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion was reiterated.

segments.name: U.S.
segments.commentary: Local-currency growth of 4% with U.S. revenue around INR530 crore; vertically integrated model helped margin expansion despite tariffs. Average ticket size fell from $50 to $46 while volume traction rose on lower price points.

segments.name: U.K.
segments.commentary: Flat overall; core TJC subdued but Ideal World grew at healthy double digits and Rachel Galley showed encouraging momentum.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Grew 6% in local currency with improving margins; EBITDA marginally above breakeven in Q1. Management expects positive contribution to group profit from FY27.

segments.name: Digital (B2C)
segments.commentary: 45% of B2C revenue; target to cross 50% during FY27. Digital volume flat at about 1.13 million orders while USD ticket size rose from $33.8 to $37.

segments.name: Television
segments.commentary: Revenue INR484 crore, up 9%; TV volume rose from 1.34 million to 1.37 million. TV networks reached about 127 million households.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 9-11% reiterated.
FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-100 bps over FY26 reiterated.
Mid- to long-term growth ambition of 12-15%; FY30 revenue ambition of INR5,000-5,500 crore, with currency assumed to depreciate about 3% a year.
Management said margin will keep improving but declined to give a specific FY30 margin number.
Digital customer payback target cut from about 9-10 months to 3 months; ROAS for pure digital acquisition currently about 2, targeting 3+.
Germany expected to contribute positively to group profit from FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex figures disclosed in the call.
Migration of all key e-commerce platforms from Salesforce to Shopify Enterprise completed in Q1; management said initial hiccups over the past couple of months were still being worked through.
AI tools deployed across product scheduling, content generation, personalised marketing and demand forecasting.
Lab-grown diamonds about 13% of retail revenue; management sees 14-16% over coming years.
Buyback withheld until a $50-100 million cash cushion is built for acquisitions or other opportunities.
demand_pricing: Constant-currency revenue broadly flat, with Middle East conflict disruption early in the quarter and cautious consumers in key markets.
U.S. consumers prioritising essentials as fuel costs rose; management said lower price points are gaining traction.
Lab-grown diamond ASP about $250, which management says is supporting higher lifetime value customers.
Unique customers 6.77 lakh (moderated), retention 38%, trailing 12-month pieces per customer 23.
Management says marketplace take rate is about 0% because less than 0.5% of sales come through marketplaces.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY30 INR5,000-5,500 crore revenue target realistic, and what margin is implied?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target was set for a volatile macro and that margins will keep improving, driven by gross margin gains and digital mix. It declined to give a specific FY30 EBITDA margin number.

qa_highlights.question: Why no buyback, and why not a new India or new-brand initiative given free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: The company wants a $50-100 million cushion for opportunities before any buyback. India is seen as a later option, after digital scales and Germany becomes PAT positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 growth is from FX and pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly currency and tariff refund; ex-refund USD growth was largely flat. Volume rose on lower price points, while U.S. average ticket size fell from $50 to $46.

qa_highlights.question: How much was the tariff refund and where does it sit in the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR38 crore received: INR25 crore in other operating revenue (flows to gross profit and EBITDA) and INR13 crore kept in inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Digital ad spend and ROAS hurdle?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend continues while it earns double-digit margin over spend; ROAS on new customer acquisition is about 2, targeted at over 3.

qa_highlights.question: Why are digital volumes flat despite 21% digital revenue growth and 3.5 lakh new users?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital growth came mostly from currency (about 11 points) and higher ticket size (about 10 points) as the mix shifts to lab-grown; volume was flat at 1.13 million.

risks_watch: Constant-currency growth is flat; reported growth depends on FX and the one-time INR25 crore tariff refund, which flatters Q1 gross margin and EBITDA.
Customer count moderated and retention is 38%; management says digital retention and repeat will decline as acquisition scales.
Digital volumes flat YoY; growth relies on ticket size and lab-grown mix against competition.
Shopify migration hiccups may still be affecting digital sales.
FY30 target needs about 10% CAGR while the rupee is assumed to depreciate 3% a year; a flat currency would make this harder.
Disclosure: analysts asked for constant-currency growth by country and a clearer refund breakdown. Management said it would consider adding these to the presentation.

532163|2026-03.headline: Saregama Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% YoY to INR 287 crore and adjusted EBITDA hit a record INR 133 crore (+31% YoY).
532163|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 287 crore (+19% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of INR 133 crore (+31% YoY) and operational PBT of INR 105 crore (+37% YoY). Management attributed the Q4 acceleration partly to the exit of Airtel Wynk, which shut in November 2024 and is no longer in the base. Music vertical (licensing, artiste management and retail combined) grew 17% in FY26 to INR 814 crore, with H1 at +8% and H2 at +26%. New content spend was INR 235 crore, below plan, as large films such as Love & War and Paradise slipped into FY27.

Below plan; plus INR 105 crore on inorganic catalogue purchases
Management cited FY26 net of other income at INR 73 crore vs INR 37 crore in FY25 (analyst cited INR 7 crore FY23, INR 16 crore FY24, INR 36 crore FY25)

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 814 crore (+17%), EBITDA INR 517 crore (+22%), net margin INR 377 crore (+28%). Medium-term guidance: 20-23% revenue CAGR and 60-65% EBITDA margin.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 108 crore (-44%), a conscious exit from in-house film production under Yoodlee in favour of the Bhansali Productions stake. Focus is now TV serials and short-format content; no major new projects greenlit.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 62 crore. Launched first festival IP UN40 (12,000 footfalls, 8 sponsors) with a loss; breakeven targeted FY28. Carvaan Live and US tours planned for FY27.

segments.commentary: Reached breakeven in FY26 per management; Saregama owns 91%.

Short-format video licensing remains one-year fixed-fee deals; social media deals are flat fee.
Q4 financials are affected by timing: society payments come in Q4, and Dhurandhar marketing sat in Q3 with revenue in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Punjabi music weak, and how much will be allocated over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted two past failed attempts in six years. A combined recorded-plus-live deal model is planned, with results expected by end-FY27 or Q3; no allocation figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Were provision write-backs in revenue and do they explain the ~42% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Write-backs relate to royalty provisions and sit in cost of revenue, not in revenue. Q1 provisions unwound in Q4; management asks for rolling 12-month evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 content budget, and what was the impact of Airtel Wynk ending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 new content budget is INR 300-350 crore. Wynk shut in November 2024; customers moved to Spotify, Saavn, Amazon, Gaana, Apple and YouTube.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the music margin step-up (net margin 42% FY25 to 47-48% FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Heavy content amortisation was booked in FY25 (Stree 2, Amaran); FY26 benefits from earlier content with lower charge-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the events business post a loss in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: The loss is mainly UN40, a year-one festival; festivals take 3-4 years to breakeven. Losses expected to shrink year-on-year, breakeven in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unallocable expense increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to lower interest income on the QIP funds deployed into content and Bhansali, which reduces netting off against other income. A detailed reconciliation was deferred offline.

532174|2026-03.headline: ICICI Bank Q4 FY26 PBT ex-treasury rose 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore, with provisions falling to just ₹96 crore.
532174|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 profit before tax excluding treasury grew 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore and profit after tax grew 8.5% to ₹13,702 crore, helped by provisions of only ₹96 crore versus ₹891 crore in Q3. Core operating profit grew only 5.1% YoY as operating expenses rose 12.0%, so the bottom line leaned on low credit costs and recoveries from written-off accounts. Loan growth accelerated to 15.8% YoY, led by rural (+25.6%), business banking (+24.4%) and mortgages (+13.2%), while deposits grew 11.4%. Management declined to guide on loan growth and said NIM should stay range-bound in FY27, while flagging West Asia conflict uncertainty without yet seeing portfolio stress.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 8.5% PAT growth came from low provisions versus core income?
qa_highlights.answer: Core operating profit grew 5.1% in Q4 and 7.7% in FY26; provisions fell about 89-90% YoY and PBT ex-treasury grew about 10%. Management said treasury was little changed.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates rise, given recent falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate direction depends on macro conditions and it is difficult to make a long-term call; the bank focuses on CASA and primary-banking relationships.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mortgage pickup and does the deposit-loan gap persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage growth reflects benchmark stability and better disbursements. Average deposit growth (about 10.8%) is close to average loan growth, and LCR is about 125-126%, so deposits will not constrain loans.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any provision release or write-back this quarter?

qa_highlights.question: Is the sub-50 bps credit cost sustainable into FY27, given the West Asia conflict?

532174|2026-06.headline: ICICI Bank Q1 FY27: PBT excluding treasury rose 20.9% YoY to ₹18,975 crore; NIM 4.36%, loans up 19.6% YoY.

Net interest margin expanded to 4.36% from 4.32% in Q4, helped by about 8 bps from income tax refund interest; excluding that, NIM was 4.28%. Loan growth accelerated to 19.6% YoY, led by a sequential pickup in domestic corporate (up 6.9% QoQ) and business banking, while asset quality was stable with net NPA at 0.35%. Management guided NIM to be range-bound in FY27 but flagged possible dilution from the FCNR(B) mobilisation push, and gave no FCNR amounts raised so far.

Record Q2 order intake of $158.4M (up nearly 21% YoY) excludes a €50M-per-year frame agreement with a consumer goods major. EBIT margin rose to 14.2%, aided by cost optimisation and billing days, and DET free cash flow reached Rs.214 Cr. Management flagged a wage hike in Q3 and Q4, a deferred semiconductor breakeven (still FY28), and softer near-term semiconductor growth on supply constraints.

segments.name: Networks & Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Flattish at -0.3% QoQ cc and +1% YoY, reflecting completion of project engagements and weakness in utilities; portfolio reshaping announcements expected soon.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew more than 26% YoY in INR; order book at a record high with book-to-bill above 1.6x; H1 revenue more than 30% above H1 last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TAO Digital run-rate and growth outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Will TAO margins be similar to DET?

qa_highlights.question: How will wage hikes affect margins in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-phase hikes over Q3 and Q4 with roughly equal impact; cost optimisation gives visibility to hold margins at current levels and grow through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor breakeven timeline and near-term growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven still targeted for FY28, possibly deferred a quarter or two; slowdown is supply-driven rather than demand-driven, with high-voltage chip revenue expected during FY28.

532178|2026-03.headline: Engineers India FY26 standalone turnover rose 27% to Rs.3,849 crore and PAT 37% to Rs.638 crore; order book hit a record Rs.15,109 crore.
532178|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: standalone turnover Rs.3,849 crore (+27% YoY), PAT Rs.638 crore (+37%), operating margin 16.22% (vs 14.76%), and EPS Rs.11.36 (vs Rs.8.28). Q4 turnover was Rs.899 crore with PBT Rs.195 crore and PAT Rs.152 crore. Order inflow was Rs.7,979 crore versus Rs.8,214 crore a year earlier, while the order book reached Rs.15,109 crore (Rs.11,717 crore a year earlier). Management flagged a slowdown in Middle East awards due to the regional conflict, while domestic and Africa activity was steady, and guided FY27 consultancy margins of 20-25% and LSTK margins of 5-7%.

segments.name: Consultancy & engineering
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.1,782 crore (vs Rs.1,678 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.489 crore with a reported Q4 margin near 29%, which management attributed to a Rs.221 crore change order, not a one-off write-back. Guided segment margin 20-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.2,067 crore (vs Rs.1,349 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.410 crore. Guided segment margin 5-7%. Dangote refinery (USD 360 million) and fertilizer (USD 70 million, four lines) contracts are being executed, started around January 2026.

segments.name: Subsidiary CEIL
segments.commentary: Profit rose to Rs.24.71 crore in FY26 from Rs.20.62 crore. Associate (refinery-linked) profit was about Rs.40 crore in the latest quarter after a shutdown-affected earlier period; management expects 100% plant capacity this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow to stay around Rs.8,000 crore (consultancy plus LSTK), with an aim to exceed it; management said FY27 inflow is hard to predict beyond one or two quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guided at a minimum of 10-15%, based on two months of the year elapsed.
Consultancy segment margin to be sustained at 20-25%; LSTK segment margin at 5-7%.
Consultancy revenue growth seen conservatively at 15-20% a year over the next two to three years.
Middle East: management expects a delay of a couple of months in big-ticket awards; Africa and the new Saudi Aramco agreements (5+3 years) are the growth routes.
Final dividend of Rs.2.5 per share proposed; with the interim Rs.2.5, total FY26 dividend is Rs.5 per share (100% of face value Rs.5).
capex_capacity: Dangote refinery and fertilizer projects are about four years in duration; site activity expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027.
Andhra (BPCL) project: feasibility underway; licensor selection next, with project activities targeted in FY27.
IOCL Paradip phase-2 balance order (about Rs.8-10 billion) expected to be awarded by end of FY27, after the investment decision.
Panipat (P25) project is in advanced construction and expected to commission soon.
Company is setting up a CBG plant in Maharashtra on its own investment and is the OT consultant for an MRPL sustainable aviation fuel plant.
demand_pricing: Order book is at a record Rs.15,109 crore, but FY26 inflow was slightly lower than FY25 at Rs.7,979 crore.
Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured, and roughly 10-15% of the current order book. Big-ticket Middle East awards are slower, with client decisions delayed by security concerns.
Africa is the main overseas focus after the Dangote awards; management sees investment shifting to Africa as an alternative hub.
Infrastructure is about 25% of FY26 order inflow (clients include ONGC, NTPC, Government of Rajasthan, IIMs/IITs and data centres).
Coal gasification: government raised viability gap funding; a consultancy opportunity of about Rs.300-400 crore was indicated. Project sizes of Rs.10,000-40,000 crore were cited.
Public-sector tenders are competitive or negotiated; hit rate on bids is about 20-25%. Nomination only for critical projects.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for FY27 consultancy inflow in domestic and international markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to sustain inflow at roughly the current level of about Rs.8,000 crore total; Middle East slowdown is the key risk, with domestic projects not being delayed or cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East share of the order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured and 10-15% of the current order book; a Saudi Aramco long-term agreement (5+3 years) was signed, with an out-of-kingdom agreement pending.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or change order behind Q4 consultancy margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no write-offs; a Rs.221 crore change order was received in FY26 and the expenditure already incurred, and the Q4 margins are described as normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue slippage Q4 vs Q3 and cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue slippage; the prior quarter included a change order over Rs.200 crore, which made it high-profit. Management did not report commodity cost impacts.

qa_highlights.question: Expected growth in FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum 10-15% growth expected in FY27 execution; FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance was deferred to next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East and Africa opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000-2,000 crore of projects is achievable over time, with an inflection expected around FY27-FY29.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict delaying big-ticket awards and revamp-led spending; monitor Saudi and out-of-kingdom agreement signing.
Consultancy order inflow, with FY26 slightly below FY25 and the Rs.8,000 crore FY27 target dependent on public-sector tenders.
Sustainability of 20%+ consultancy margins; Q4 margin benefited from a Rs.221 crore change order.
Dangote and IOCL Paradip conversion timing; large LSTK jobs carry 5-7% margins.
Associate plant operating at full capacity this year after a prior shutdown.
Disclosure readability: an analyst flagged that the figures uploaded to the exchanges are hard to read.

But we have not seen in the domestic market anywhere any project being delayed or anything being done.

532178|2026-06.headline: Engineers India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 55% to INR109 crores, while turnover fell 7% to INR801 crores on Turnkey decline.
532178|2026-06.overview: Standalone PBT rose about 55% YoY to INR145 crores and PAT to INR109 crores, helped by Consultancy growth of about 22% to INR499 crores. Turnkey turnover fell to INR302 crores from INR449 crores as major projects tapered. Order book stood at INR14,424 crores at 30 June 2026, but Q1 order inflow was only INR514 crores. Management kept the INR8,000 crore FY27 order inflow target and the FY27 operating margin guidance of 16%, and said the Middle East new-mega-project pipeline has slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore order inflow target still achievable, and how much would be consultancy?

qa_highlights.question: Will there be write-backs or change orders this year, including HPCL Barmer?

qa_highlights.question: How should consultancy growth and margins be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consultancy growth target is at least 10%+ overall, with consultancy above 50% of turnover; segment profit is targeted at 24-25%. Operating margin target is 16%, with possible upside from change orders.

qa_highlights.question: Have Middle East clients put projects on hold due to the conflict?

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue be recognised on the Dangote Nigeria order?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on cost-progress basis, with turnover booked as cost progress is achieved over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan to distribute surplus cash?

532209|2026-03.headline: J&K Bank posts FY26 net profit of INR2,363 crores, a fourth straight record, with Q4 profit near INR800 crores (up 36% QoQ); FY27 NIM guided at ~3.5%.

Business grew 13.6%, with advances up 16.8% and deposits up 11.3%, both above guidance. NIM for FY26 was 3.60%, a marginal miss against guidance, attributed to 125 bps of RBI rate cuts in 2025 and deposit competition. Operating expenses fell about 4%, and GNPA/NNPA stood at 2.50%/0.64%. FY27 guidance is conservative: credit growth 12%, deposits 10%, NIM about 3.5%, RoA maintained, RoE about 16%, GNPA below 2.25%.

segments.name: Retail, Agriculture & MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM remains more than two-thirds of the loan book. Car loans grew 17.5% and were the best-performing personal loan segment.

532209|2026-06.headline: J&K Bank Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR424 crore on margin compression to 3.28% and higher standard-asset provisions, despite 25.44% advances growth.
532209|2026-06.overview: Advances grew 25.44% YoY and deposits 16.75% YoY, with both up over 4% QoQ, and the bank crossed INR3 trillion business. Operating profit was INR703 crore (+5% YoY), but net profit of INR424 crore was below last year, driven by standard-asset provisions raised on strong credit growth and lower technical write-off recoveries. NIM compressed to 3.28% as cost of deposits stayed high (4.74%) while yield on advances was 8.56%. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged for now, to be reassessed after Q2, but indicated credit growth of 18-20% against the 12% guidance.

segments.name: Retail banking
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew double digit YoY; J&K personal loans +12%, car loans +20% bank-level and +30% in ROI; agriculture +18%. Retail segment profit fell from INR472 crore in Q4 to INR196 crore, which management attributed to technical write-off recoveries booked in Q4.

segments.name: Rest of India (ROI)
segments.commentary: ROI contributes around 26% of business as on 30 June 2026, versus less than 20% a year ago. Corporate lending in ROI at competitive rates drove the quarter's growth.

segments.name: J&K and Ladakh
segments.commentary: Home-market share of banking business at 61.13% (31 March 2026); deposit market share improved in 19 of 22 districts during FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance kept unchanged for now, to be reassessed only after Q2 results: credit growth ~12%, deposit growth ~10%, CASA ~45%, NIM ~3.5%, ROA around FY26 levels, ROE ~16%, GNPA below 2.25%.
Chairman-level view: actual credit growth 'will not be less than' 18-20% in FY27; J&K growth ~12-13%, ROI growth ~25%.
ROA of 1.25%+ guided for FY27, with management saying it should show from Q2; Q1 ROA was ~0.90%.
NIM expected to return to around 3.5% 'by end of Q3, definitely'; retail yields to be at least 200 bps above corporate book.

Expects retail advances growth of 55-60% in FY27 (as stated), with retail growth to exceed corporate growth by year-end.
Expects CASA ratio to improve substantially by end of Q3 FY27.

Possible one-off gain from sale of stake in MetLife; timing and use not decided, awaiting clearances.
demand_pricing: Corporate credit growth outpaced retail in Q1 as higher bond yields pushed companies back to bank credit; bank chose selective lending to well-rated corporates at competitive rates.
Loans to financial-market players were largely repo-linked and short-term; management says short-term lending has been avoided for ~12 months and some low-yield loans mature in the coming months.

Nearly two-thirds of industry bank credit now below 9% yield per RBI data, versus ~44% a year ago.

532209|2026-09.headline: J&K Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose about 29% QoQ to INR546 crore; management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 14%+ and sees ROA of about 1.20%.
532209|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 net profit was INR546 crore, up about 29% QoQ with double-digit YoY growth, after a weak Q1. Operating profit rose 27% YoY to INR789 crore, helped by operating expenses up only 2% QoQ and cost-to-income falling to 56.57%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.23% and NNPA at 0.51%, and H1 gross slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier. Management revised FY27 guidance after the mid-term review: credit growth 14%+, deposit growth 12%+, CASA 42%+, ROA about 1.20% and GNPA below 2%. Key open items are the ECL transition impact, which management will quantify in December, and NIM, which management declined to quantify.

financial_highlights.change: RoA +20 bps QoQ; RoE +250 bps QoQ
Gross slippage amount roughly halved YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Auto loans grew over 25% YoY; Rest of India housing grew double digits YoY. Retail yield about 10%. Management says 60% of FY27 growth target will come from retail.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri yield about 9.5%. Agri advances grew double digits in H1.

segments.name: Corporate / MSME
segments.commentary: MSME yield about 9%; Rest of India corporate yield about 7.2%. Little large corporate lending in J&K. Management targets 40% of FY27 growth from corporate.

segments.commentary: Outstanding about INR13,400 crore on the MoU personal loan book (management cited INR16,000 crore+ across two variants). Declined last year after product revamp and EMI/salary-ratio correction; H1 FY27 disbursals already exceed full FY26.

Management says it is 'conservative'; it aims for around 18% credit growth if retail momentum continues.
Management expects H2 FY27 ROA of about 1.40% or better, driven by recoveries from written-off accounts, a special OTS scheme, treasury, fee income and non-fund-based business.
NIM expected to improve substantially from Q3 as the 25 bps repo cut passes through, high-cost deposits are shed, and the repo rate may rise further. No numerical NIM guidance given.
Employee cost expected flat to slightly lower over the next two quarters, returning to current levels in FY28 after hiring.

demand_pricing: Retail and RAM led growth; management says retail is preferred for its higher yield.

Q1 CASA outflows were largely converted to term deposits within the bank, according to management; average and period-end balances are now close.
High-cost CDs of about 8% were taken in Q1 to fund loan commitments; most has been repaid. Remaining high-cost bulk deposits are under INR3,000 crore.
Non-fund-based business up about 30-40% QoQ. Two more life insurers added (SBI Life, HDFC Life); management expects volume growth to offset IRDAI commission cuts.

qa_highlights.question: What steps are being taken to improve the CASA mix, which lags term deposit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited salary-account MoUs with 20+ organisations, tighter monitoring of UPI POS and QR merchant routing, and a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU. It says CASA is at least held at around 42%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook, and what is the ongoing cost after ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the ECL impact until the end of next quarter, with the model going to the December board. It sees no reason for credit cost to rise; current provisions are ageing-based and H1 slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 credit growth of 14% realistic versus 24-25% currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14% is a conservative floor ('14% plus'), with an aim of around 18%. It does not expect 25%, since Q3 and Q4 of last year were strong comparators.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM outlook and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numerical NIM target but said it will rise substantially from Q3. Drivers are the 25 bps repo pass-through, the end of high-cost deposits, higher yields, and possible further rate hikes. About 65% of the book is repo-linked and 31% MCLR-linked.

qa_highlights.answer: TWO recoveries were INR25 crore in the quarter. A post-quarter equity stake sale and revaluation gain of about INR100 crore is not in Q2. AFS reserve movement was negative INR62 crore.

rows.label: ECL transition quantum and December board
rows.why: Management has about INR300 crore buffer and says the ECL hit will be below industry average, but has not quantified it; the range is due at the December board.

rows.label: Government and salary-account MoUs
rows.why: More than 20 organisations signed in the last quarter and a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU is expected the day after the call, aimed at fixing the CASA shortfall (41.97% vs 42%+ target).

rows.label: INR1,000 crore equity and INR500 crore debt raise
rows.when: debt this quarter; equity timing open
rows.why: Approval for the INR1,000 crore equity is in place and the INR500 crore debt is expected this quarter; CET1 is 13.88% and CRAR 16.57%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter's profit, asset quality (GNPA 2.23%) and the NIM direction, but guarded on numbers, declining to quantify NIM or ECL; analysts pushed on the ROA cut, high SMA-1+2 (about 5%), and whether 14% credit growth is realistic against 24-25% current growth.

532210|2026-03.headline: City Union Bank Q4 FY26: advances up 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore and PAT up 25% to INR360 crore, with gross NPA at 1.91%.
532210|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the bank's strongest quarter in recent years, with total business growing about 24% YoY and advances up 26% to INR66,698 crore. Asset quality kept improving: gross NPA fell to 1.91% from 3.09% a year earlier, and total SMA fell to 2.47% from 3.68% in Q3. Q4 PAT rose 25% to INR360 crore, the highest single quarter, and FY26 PAT rose 18% to INR1,326 crore with ROA at 1.56%. The call also marked the handover of MD and CEO from Dr. N. Kamakodi to R. Vijay Anandh effective 1 May 2026.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loans are about 30% of the book and growing faster than overall loans; management says the 30% level is near the upper limit, with 1-2% flexibility. Per-gram lending was capped around INR10,000-10,500 even at peak gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Core focus segment, with management citing rising capacity utilisation and CC limit usage as demand drivers. FY27 plan keeps MSME at 55-60% of the mix. Only 3-4% of MSME loans are under CGTMSE cover.

segments.name: Secured retail
segments.commentary: Housing and loans against property are growing and are an additional growth driver. FY27 plan uses secured retail to fill the remaining share of the mix after MSME and gold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth planned at 2-3% above industry credit growth, with MSME at 55-60%, gold loans and secured retail as additional enhancers.
FY27 NIM expected to stay in a narrow 5-10 bps band around the FY26 level of 3.74%.
FY27 operating expenses expected to rise 15-18% YoY, with about 75 branches to be opened in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end).
ROA to exit FY27 at least 10 bps higher, at about 1.65-1.67%, supported by retail income and lower cost-to-income.
CD ratio to be kept at 85-87%. Third-party business to be 1-2% of the book. Fee income to be 55-60% of other income.

Credit cost expected to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60% over the next 15 years; individual years may vary. Management said the ECL circular lets banks adjust the opening balance, so the ECL impact on P&L is expected to be limited.
capex_capacity: Branch network reached 1,000 with the opening of the 1,000th branch at Kumbakonam on 4 May 2026, up from about 950 at FY26 end.
About 75 branches to be opened in FY27, with about 50 in April 2026 (70 opened in the first month per the CEO-designate); branches typically reach breakeven in year one.
Distribution capacity was lifted by the Newgen LOS and digital process set, which the management credits for secured MSME and retail growth.
demand_pricing: Advances grew by over INR5,800 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR13,600 crore for the full year; double-digit growth has run for eight consecutive quarters.
Deposit growth was matched to credit growth, with CASA at 28% of deposits and the average CD ratio at 85% for FY26. Some CDs were replaced by retail term deposits.
Yield on advances was 9.80% in Q4 (9.73% in Q3) and 9.75% for FY26 (9.79% in FY25). The cost of deposits was 5.60% in Q4 (5.57% in Q3).
Management said rate passthrough was completed around December 2025, and incremental yields are holding up, with non-agri gold loans at double-digit yields.
Management is watching the US-Iran conflict and oil prices; no visible impact on asset quality so far. Management expects a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: How does the bank manage risk on gold loans given a 10-15% gold price fall from the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-gram lending was capped at about INR10,000-10,500 even when gold peaked at INR15,000-16,000, so there is a cushion. It cited a loss of about INR5 crore in the 2014 gold price crash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise 3 bps QoQ, and where will it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some deposit rates were fine-tuned by 10-25 bps to support fast credit growth. It said the 3-5 bps movement is noise from CASA rate variation and it can add INR3,000 crore of advances without new deposits.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield on advances keep falling after the rate cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate passthrough is complete, and roughly 30% of the book is fixed-rate gold. Incremental book of about INR5,000 crore booked in H2 was at higher yields, which held the margin.

qa_highlights.question: When does ROA move to 1.7-1.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO-designate said FY27 exit ROA should be 1.65-1.67%, at least 10 bps above the FY26 level, based on retail income and lower cost-to-income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for steady-state credit costs after the ECL norms?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the 15-year average credit cost is about 0.60%, and FY25 and FY26 were 0.09% and 0.04%. He expects at least a 50% reduction over the long run, with AI-based underwriting cited as the reason.

qa_highlights.question: Will underwriting filters tighten given fuel prices and demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it watches SMA trends and branch and customer feedback. It would add some caution to filters but has no plan to change them now, as underwriting is set for multiple business cycles.

risks_watch: Gold price correction on the INR30%+ gold book and whether LTV cushions hold.
Impact of the US-Iran conflict and oil prices on MSME demand and slippages; management expects an extra 1-2% slippage in a downturn.
Rising deposit costs as the bank fine-tunes rates to fund faster credit growth; the CD ratio is at 85% and CASA at 28%.
Opex growth of 15-18% in FY27 from branch expansion, against the ROA target of 1.65-1.67%.
Leadership transition: MD and CEO handover on 1 May 2026, plus the retirement of two independent directors in February 2026. The retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.
532210|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and asset quality, with management saying it met all earlier guidance. More cautious on macro risks, particularly the US-Iran conflict and fuel prices. Evasive on the ECL steady-state credit cost, deferring that question to the CEO-designate.
key_quotes: By and large, almost all the expectations whatever we shared with you in the earlier con-calls for the financial year 2026 were met in the same spirit whatever we had shared with you.
The gross NPA has come below 2 % mark after 11 years.
I think we should exit this year with at least 10 bps more in ROA, so we should be there between 1.65% to 1.67%.

Q4 vs 3.89% in Q3; FY26 up 14 bps from 3.60%

financial_highlights.value: INR1,856 crore in Q4; INR6,870 crore in FY26

financial_highlights.change: up from 78% and 60% a year earlier
recoveries INR231 crore (INR153 crore from live NPAs, INR78 crore from technical write-offs)
down from 3.68% in Q3 and 5.60% in Q2

rows.why: NIM is guided to stay within a narrow 5-10 bps band around FY26's 3.74%, and cost of deposits rose to 5.60% in Q4 from 5.57% in Q3 as rates were fine-tuned to fund credit growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network reached 1,000 after the Kumbakonam opening on 4 May 2026, with about 75 more branches planned in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end), a 7.9% addition to the network.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management plans advances growth 2-3% above industry credit growth, following 26% YoY in Q4 and INR13,600 crore added in FY26, with MSME at 55-60% of the mix and gold and secured retail as enhancers.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Advances grew 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore against FY27 guidance of only 2-3% above industry credit growth, and gross NPA fell to 1.91%, so the guide looks conservative if growth holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Opex is guided up 15-18% in FY27 against an ROA exit target of 1.65-1.67%, and management flags a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn tied to the US-Iran conflict and oil prices.

rows.label: Credit cost to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60%
rows.when: over the next 15 years, individual years may vary
rows.why: FY25 and FY26 credit costs were 0.09% and 0.04%, and management cites AI-based underwriting, but the long-run timing is uncertain and the CEO deferred on steady-state ECL questions.

rows.label: Gold loan price correction risk
rows.why: Gold is about 30% of the book with per-gram lending capped near INR10,000-10,500 versus a peak of INR15,000-16,000, and a 10-15% fall would be cushioned by LTV headroom.

rows.label: CEO handover to R. Vijay Anandh
rows.why: Leadership changed on 1 May 2026, and the retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, asset quality and branch expansion, but cautious on the US-Iran conflict and fuel prices and evasive on steady-state ECL credit costs, which it deferred to the CEO-designate.

532210|2026-06.headline: City Union Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 383 crore, a record, with GNPA down to 1.73% and NIM guided to 3.65-3.70%.
532210|2026-06.overview: Advances grew 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crore and deposits 21% to Rs 79,342 crore, with CD ratio at 85%. Operating profit rose 29% to Rs 581 crore and PAT 25% to Rs 383 crore, both stated as record highs. Asset quality improved further: GNPA 1.73% (from 2.99% a year ago), Net NPA 0.61%, and recoveries exceeded slippages. Management guided to a moderate NIM dip from higher cost of funds, cost-to-income of 47-48% for FY27, and an exit ROA of 1.60-1.65%.

financial_highlights.change: up 25% QoQ as stated; vs Rs 54,020 crore in 1QFY26

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME average disbursement about Rs 3,500 crore per quarter; management targets MSME at 55-60% of book and growth 2-3% above system. Average utilisation fell from 73% to 70%; repayments about Rs 900 crore per month.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Share of book at 30-31%, guided to stay 31-32%. Agri gold yield about 10-10.5% and non-agri 11-11.5%; agri priced 100 bps lower. Average LTV 62.07%. Branches rose from 700 to 1,000.

segments.name: Retail secured (LAP)
segments.commentary: LAP yield about 9.60-9.70%. Management expects retail secured at about 10% of book.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Yield on investments fell to 6.42% from 6.61% in 4QFY26 because Rs 12 crore of mutual fund income (on about Rs 700 crore invested) was classified under other income; 6.67% on an interest-income basis.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27; DSA business about 1-2% of book.
NIM expected at 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps; long-term view 3.70-3.75%.
Cost of deposits guided at 5.60-5.70%; borrowing cost of about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.
Cost-to-income guided at 47-48% for FY27 (currently 45%) because staff hikes start from July; long-term aspiration below 45% in about three years.
Exit ROA guided at 1.60-1.65%; full-year ROA 1.55-1.65%. Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%.
ECLGS participation: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date; total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provisioning about 0.45% of loan book, CAR consumption capped at 0.65%.
capex_capacity: Branch rollout front-loaded this year; branch count rose from 700 to 1,000 in the gold-loan context.
AI-led automation invested in operations; management expects it to lower cost further.
Liquidity: average LCR at 150%.

Business enterprise (non-MSME, no Udyam registration) loans at Rs 18,827 million; large-industry book fell from Rs 22,500 million (Dec-25) to about Rs 15,000 million then rose to Rs 19,000 million on exits and yield pressure.
demand_pricing: Gold loan rates unchanged; management ruled out raising rates to slow growth, citing agri customer needs and competitiveness in non-agri gold; rates up 20-25 bps over last year.
MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74% norm; management attributes it to cautious borrowers and sees it recovering with textile demand after the European trade agreement.
Term deposit rates expected to rise on high demand; FCNR window brought in fresh deposits of Rs 150 crore.
SMA-0/1/2 at 1.20%/0.70%/0.90% (total 2.85%), down from 7.12% in June 2025 and 10.78% in September 2024. Domestic consumption said to be insulated from West Asia stress.
Fee income fell about 15% YoY and 19% in one comparison per analyst question; management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move beyond the near-term cost-of-funds increase (FY27-FY28 levers), given stagnant lending yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME, gold and retail secured yields (agri gold ~10-10.5%, non-agri 11-11.5%, LAP 9.60-9.70%, MSME 9.30-9.40%) and a low-cost deposit franchise; long-term NIM view 3.70-3.75%. The Q1 cost-of-funds decline was attributed to better repricing and lower borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MSME growing about 15% when system MSME growth is above 20%? Is utilisation falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Rs 900 crore monthly repayments, MSME utilisation down to 70% from a 73-74% norm, and slightly more cautious pricing. Guidance is MSME growth 2-3% above system, with MSME at 55-60% of book.

qa_highlights.question: What slippage and credit cost levels are sustainable over one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%. Recoveries have exceeded slippages for about 10 quarters and are expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank reach 25-30% higher growth with the mix intact (gold 31-32%, MSME 55-60%, retail 10%), and what is the MSME outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the mix targets and said lower utilisation cost about 3-4% of MSME growth. It expects MSME growth 2-3% above system, with the European trade agreement seen supporting textile utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in cost of funds despite lower deposit costs, and what is the treasury and borrowing cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost rose to Rs 94 crore from Rs 72.5 crore in 4QFY26; treasury gains were Rs 52.54 crore vs Rs 29 crore in 4QFY26. Borrowing cost is guided at about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bank participating in ECLGS, and how is the ECL provisioning assessed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date (Rs 200 crore last quarter); total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provision about 0.45% of loan book, with CAR consumption capped at 0.65%; flow impact described as negligible given the secured book.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income decline and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income was down about 15% YoY (analyst cited 19% in one comparison). Management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance income; non-treasury other income was Rs 243 crore in Q1 vs roughly Rs 300 crore in Q4 last year.

risks_watch: Utilisation trend in MSME (70% in Q1 vs 73-74% norm) and whether the European trade-agreement recovery in textiles materialises.
Cost of deposits moving to 5.60-5.70% and the ~5 bps NIM hit; NIM guided 3.65-3.70%, below the 3.78% reported in Q1.
Cost-to-income rising to 47-48% for FY27 from 45.42% as staff hikes start from July; exit ROA 1.60-1.65% depends on fee income recovery.
Gold loan pricing: management ruled out rate hikes, so growth is supported only by volume; agri gold LTV around 62% with sensitivity to gold price drops.
West Asia stress and SMA trends (SMA-0/1/2 total 2.85%) and ECLGS-linked disbursements that may affect future asset quality.
Large-industry book volatility (Rs 22,500 million in Dec-25, down to ~Rs 15,000 million, then ~Rs 19,000 million) and the non-MSME business enterprise book of Rs 18,827 million.
key_quotes: For 1QFY27 as well, we have achieved 25% credit growth quarter-on-quarter, the highest growth rate in June-to-June and our advances had increased to Rs. 67,645 crores from Rs. 54,020 crores in 1QFY26.
So, the trend of recovery more than slippages continues, and we are confident of maintaining recovery more than slippages for the next quarter as well, which is the current quarter.
So, we are quite confident of maintaining the cost-to-income at 47%. We are currently at 45 as we speak.
We haven't changed any rate of interest for gold loans. We are at the same rate, and we continue to do the same.
532210|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and specific on asset quality, recoveries and growth targets, repeating FY27 guidance from the Q4 call. It was cautious on margins, cost-to-income and fee income, and deflected on the MSME utilisation decline and gold pricing rather than offering new numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided to 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters from 3.78% in Q1, as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps to 5.60-5.70%; cost-to-income rising to 47-48% for FY27 from 45.42%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gold-loan branches rose from 700 to 1,000 and the branch rollout is front-loaded this year, though no new plant or capex quantum was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27; advances up 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crore and deposits up 21% to Rs 79,342 crore, but MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance (ROA 1.55-1.65%, cost-to-income 47-48%, slippages Rs 700-750 crore) and guided NIM lower, so no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fee income fell about 15% YoY and exit ROA of 1.60-1.65% depends on fee recovery, while MSME utilisation at 70% vs 73-74% norm and cost-to-income rising to 47-48% are headwinds.

rows.label: Term deposit rate increases on high demand
rows.why: Management expects term deposit rates to rise; cost of deposits guided to 5.60-5.70% from 5.56% in Q1, a ~5 bps hit to NIM.

rows.label: MSME utilisation recovery with textile demand
rows.why: MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74% norm; management expects recovery after the European trade agreement, but this is conditional and not quantified.

rows.label: Fee income catch-up
rows.why: Fee income fell about 15% YoY; non-treasury other income was Rs 243 crore in Q1 vs roughly Rs 300 crore a year ago, and management expects catch-up from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 1.73%, recoveries above slippages for about 10 quarters) and held FY27 guidance, but cautious on NIM, cost-to-income and fee income; analysts pressed on MSME growth lagging the system (about 15% vs above 20%) and utilisation falling to 70%.

532218|2026-03.headline: South Indian Bank FY26 net profit rose 12% to INR1,455 crore; Q4 PAT INR408 crore, GNPA down to 1.43% for the year.
532218|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the bank's highest-ever annual profit, with deposits up 15% and gross advances up 14.5% (about 15.8% excluding the INR1,163 crore technical write-off). Asset quality improved sharply, with gross NPA at 1.43% and net NPA at 0.29%, and Q4 credit cost was 3 bps. Q4 non-interest income fell mainly because Treasury income was near nil versus about INR77 crore in Q3, and employee costs were lowered by an INR80 crore actuarial write-back. Management said credit cost and slippages are likely to rise from here, and it flagged a CEO succession process, with the current term ending September 30, 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR342 crore in Q4 FY25
Q4 NIM up 9 bps QoQ; Q3 up 6 bps
GNPA down 177 bps from 3.2%; NNPA down 63 bps from 0.92%

financial_highlights.value: 15 bps in Q4 (not annualised); 72 bps for FY26

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book grew 46% in FY26 to INR24,729 crore, average LTV 57.18%, average ticket about INR2.71 lakh. Management said the vast majority is organic; buyouts and co-lending are about 8-10% of the book.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate is about 38% of the loan book; management targets about 33% over time, with ultra-short-duration corporate lending falling from roughly 20-25% of book to about 10%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 15% YoY. Sequential decline of about 2% was attributed to a INR554 crore write-off, per management, with no material stress seen.

segments.name: Retail and mortgage/auto
segments.commentary: Management reported significant YoY growth in mortgage and auto loans. Personal loans are largely pre-approved sales to existing customers, with loss rates of about 3.5-4% against spreads of 11-12%.

segments.name: Treasury and fee income
segments.commentary: Treasury income was nil in Q4 versus about INR77 crore in Q3, which drove the non-interest income dip. FX revenue grew substantially; a new TF Online export platform is planned.

guidance_outlook: Loan growth guided at 15-16% for FY27, and the bank aims to match industry growth if industry grows faster.
NIM expected to keep widening through asset mix shift to retail and MSME, repricing of about 60-65% of deposits during FY27, and possible rate hikes, where the bank would be a large beneficiary.
Operating expenses will rise as the bank invests in distribution and technology, but management aims for positive operating leverage for a third straight year.
Management expects credit cost and slippages to trend upward from current lows due to Middle East geopolitical stress; it sees Q3 credit cost of 3 bps as the trough.
Branch network to grow selectively in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and New Delhi; branches fell from 955 to 948 over the past seven to eight quarters.
Corporate share targeted to fall from 38% to about 33% of the loan book over two to three years.
capex_capacity: Branch count at 948, down from 955 over seven to eight quarters; selective additions planned in several states.
SIB RED, a full digital bank offering, launched towards end-March 2026.
New TF Online platform under development for export and trade finance for corporate and MSME clients.
Management said investment in distribution, manpower and technology will start, after costs were held flat for eight to ten quarters.
demand_pricing: Deposit cost rose about 3 bps QoQ in Q4 as the bank selectively repriced deposits to fund growth; management said it had been priced below competitors.
NRI deposits grew 12% in FY26 versus 7% in FY25; management said there is no stress from West Asia conflict, with a slight pickup in inward remittances.
Management said the new ECLGS-type scheme targets airlines and MSMEs, and it did not expect a material drawdown given the current borrower stress levels.
Gold price fell from about $5,500 to about $4,100 per ounce in January-February; margin calls were met promptly and gold loan risk is managed with a 30-day VaR framework and standard-deviation caps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vinod Francis said Treasury income was almost nil in Q4 versus about INR77 crore in Q3 because of market conditions. Management said the drop was industry-wide and that the shift to retail and MSME should raise fee income over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off in employee expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was an actuarial valuation write-back of close to INR80 crore at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost and ECL transition look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 credit cost of 3 bps is the trough and expects slippages and credit cost to rise given geopolitical stress; it cannot quantify this. For ECL transition, no floating provision is held and no material one-time impact is expected, given SMA 1 and 2 at about 0.6% of the book and PCR near 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the cost of deposits rise, and will NIM keep improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank repriced deposits slightly to support growth, adding about 3 bps. It said NIM rose about 15 bps over two quarters and expects further widening from mix, repricing of 60-65% of deposits, and rate hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CEO succession on track?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO P.R. Seshadri said the Board is actively searching and will send names to RBI in time. His term ends September 30, and management expects the new incumbent to be in place before or just after that date.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank add branches or expand distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will add branches selectively in the under-penetrated states, and rely more on DSAs, digital channels and the SIB RED digital bank.

risks_watch: Rising slippages and credit cost, which management expects from Middle East stress; the outcome is unquantified.
Gold price volatility on a book of INR24,729 crore; a fall beyond the VaR-based caps would hit the bank, and the portfolio's LTV is blended.
Fee income volatility from Treasury; Q4 Treasury income was near nil.
Deposit cost pressure from selective repricing, versus expected repricing benefit in FY27.
CEO succession: the search is ongoing and the term ends September 30, 2026.
Old and new book classification was debated internally; the old book was about 12% of gross advances, and the Q4 GNPA reduction was largely driven by INR1,048 crore of technical write-off.
Possible difficulty recovering the 25% ECLGS guarantee portion if settlements are made with borrowers.
532218|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on profitability, asset quality and NIM direction, but cautious on credit outlook, where the CEO said he could not quantify the impact. Evasive on the CEO succession timeline and on some data points, which were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: The bank declared its highest ever net profit for the year at INR1,455 crores for the financial year 2025-2026, which implies a growth of 12% compared to INR1,303 crores in the prior year.
