532218|2026-06.headline: South Indian Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 17% YoY to INR378 crore, with record NII of INR1,025 crore and NIM of 3.23%.
532218|2026-06.overview: Net profit grew 17% YoY to INR378 crore, and net interest income hit a record INR1,025 crore, up 23% YoY and INR110 crore QoQ. NIM recovered to 3.23%, up 28 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY, helped by repricing of high-cost deposits, CASA growth and a 50% cut in bulk deposits. Gross advances grew 17% YoY and gross NPA fell to 1.38%. Non-interest income was soft: core fees fell to INR179 crore from INR191 crore in Q4, and management called this a one-off. Management said the call was the last for MD and CEO P.R. Seshadri, who is leaving.

segments.name: Business loans (MSME)
segments.commentary: Business loans rose to INR14,391 crore from INR12,660 crore; growth was 18% excluding a INR554 crore charge-off. Management said MSME growth was muted versus expectations this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book reached INR24,930 crore, up 43% YoY, with average LTV of 65.25% and average ticket size of INR2.94 lakh. QoQ growth was only about 0.8% because co-lending and portfolio purchases of about INR270 crore ran off after an RBI circular effective April 1.

segments.name: Mortgages, home and auto loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage loans grew 34% YoY, home loans 19% and auto loans 34%, excluding IBPC/DA impact.

segments.name: Corporate book
segments.commentary: Corporate lending grew in Q1 as pricing hardened on short-tenor facilities. Corporate is about 40% of the loan book against a stated long-run target of about 30%.

guidance_outlook: NIM: no numeric guidance. Management believes the rate cycle has turned, so NIM should harden as repo changes pass through on a T+1 basis. Management also said the sharp deposit-repricing gains are unlikely to repeat.
Opex: management expects full-year opex growth of about 5-6% and aims for positive operating leverage for the full year. Q1 did not have positive operating leverage.
Fees: management called the fee decline a one-off. Trade and FX platform is expected to go live by end-September 2026.
Slippage: management expects FY27 slippage of INR500-750 crore, with INR800 crore as the maximum even with West Asia stress. Recoveries are expected at INR800-1,000 crore.
Credit cost: management said the 9 bps Q1 cost is probably generous and could moderate.
ROA: management said ROA should move from 100-110 bps toward 120-125 bps over time. No explicit ROE target was given, and the CEO declined a firm multi-year number.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion restarting on a small scale after about 3 years of freeze; branch count had fallen slightly and is being rebuilt in key locations.
Trade and FX digital platform targeted to go live by end-September 2026, covering FX bookings, LCs, guarantees and export/import bill settlement.

Capital: management plans to grow the balance sheet at market growth plus about 2%, shifting mix toward higher risk-weight retail and MSME assets. Risk density is expected to rise, so CRAR will fall from 19.62% over time.
demand_pricing: Deposit costs fell as high-rate deposits repriced down 40-60 bps between January and June 2026. Average CASA grew 19%, and bulk deposits were cut about 50% YoY.
Asset yields rose 5 bps, helped by mix shift, T-bill-linked corporate pricing and firmer corporate pricing on short-tenor loans. Retail pricing did not move up.

FCNR(B) deposits grew about 6% QoQ. Management expects a large share of inflows in August and September before the scheme closes on September 30. Inflows are unlevered because the bank has no external credit lines or GIFT City entity.
Recoveries of INR179 crore in Q1 against slippages of INR128 crore. Q1 is seasonally weak for recoveries.
SMA-1 and SMA-2 rose about INR80 crore QoQ. Management called it seasonal and said the constituents are reversible.
ECLGS: limit of about INR400 crore, disbursed about INR238 crore, with utilised book of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in cost of deposits and the yield rise on advances, and what is the NIM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: High-rate deposits repriced 40-60 bps, CASA grew, and bulk deposits were halved. Yield gains came from mix shift and T-bill-linked corporate pricing. Management gave no numeric NIM guidance, but expects NIMs to harden if the rate cycle has turned.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex and hiring rise for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Branch rollout is restarting in key locations. Opex growth is expected at about 5-6% for the year, with positive operating leverage targeted for the full year after Q1 lacked it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income soften, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Core fees fell to INR179 crore from INR191 crore, partly from a product renewal fee-charging error that will be fixed. Treasury income fell to INR44 crore and Q1 FY26 PSLC sale income of about INR60 crore did not recur. Management called this an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Why is corporate share about 40% against a 30% target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate pricing improved and liquidity was available, so the bank added short-tenor, high-quality corporate loans. Management still intends to reduce corporate exposure over the long run.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost run rate, and what about SMA-1/2 and ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost was 9 bps. Management called that generous and expects moderation. FY27 slippage is seen at INR500-750 crore. Management expects no material NII impact from ECL effective-interest changes.

qa_highlights.question: Is FCNR(B) growth sustainable after June, and what is the landed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows are strong and expects most in August-September. Pricing matches domestic rupee liquidity levels. Landed cost was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for excess capital and the ROA and ROE path?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance sheet to grow at market growth plus about 2%, with mix shifting to higher risk-weight retail and MSME. ROA target path is 100-110 bps moving toward 120-125 bps; no firm ROE guidance was given.

risks_watch: Leadership transition: the MD and CEO is leaving, and management declined to commit to multi-year ROA or ROE targets that would bind a successor.
NIM tailwind may fade: management said the sharp deposit-repricing benefit is unlikely to repeat at the same scale.
Corporate exposure at about 40% of the book, above the 30% target, with West Asia uncertainty cited.
Gold loan QoQ growth was only about 0.8% after the RBI circular, and bulk-deal run-off is ongoing.
FCNR(B) inflows depend on the Dubai rep office permissibility and on foreign bank credit lines that have not yet materialised.
SMA-1/2 rose about INR80 crore QoQ; management attributes this to seasonality, but the trend needs monitoring.
Fee income recovery: management has to show that core fees rebound from INR179 crore and that the trade/FX platform goes live by end-September.
532218|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins, asset quality and capital, but cautious on fees and MSME momentum. The CEO said the rate cycle has turned and avoided numeric NIM and ROE guidance, citing his exit.
key_quotes: And so now we are in a position where our belief is the rate cycle has switched. So it's more likely to increase than to reduce.
We think that the 9 basis points that we currently have is probably on a generous side.
So with respect to fees, my own view is that it's a one-timer. We shouldn't read this as something that is going to last forever.

532218|2026-09.headline: South Indian Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 21% YoY to INR426 crore, with NIM at 3.33% and gross NPA at 1.24%.
532218|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 net profit was INR426 crore, up 21% YoY from INR351 crore, the bank's highest quarterly profit as stated. Deposits grew 19% YoY to INR1,37,279 crore and gross advances grew 19% to INR1,09,517 crore (about 20% excluding the INR1,163 crore technical write-off last year). NIM rose 10 bps QoQ to 3.33%, ROA was 1.08% and ROE 14%. Management said credit cost rose to 0.14% from a conservative top-up in account-level provisions, not a specific one-off, and that the current-account jump was partly one-off IPO-related inflows. The call also covered the new MD and CEO transition from P.R. Seshadri, the 15-16% growth guidance and the medium-term ROA and NIM targets.

financial_highlights.change: +19% YoY from INR92,286 crore; about 20% excluding technical write-off
Analyst calculated about 60 bps on a different basis

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate share of advances fell to 39% from 40%. Management targets about 35%, and corporate loans are priced off repo and T-bills, with new bookings up 25-30 bps over three months.

segments.name: Retail, agri and MSME
segments.commentary: Now 61% of advances. Retail, MSME and agri disbursements are growing faster than wholesale. Retail is targeted to grow faster than corporate.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about INR26,000 crore (INR15,000 crore retail, INR10,000 crore agri), growing about 41%, with 25% of advances. Blended yield about 10%; retail yields at most 25 bps above agri. Target is 30-32% of advances in the first phase, then 35%.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Miscellaneous income of INR190 crore includes INR73 crore recovery from technically written-off accounts and bancassurance income of INR30-35 crore per quarter. Core fees are about INR198 crore and treasury forex about INR80 crore.

demand_pricing: Current account balances rose 20% QoQ, partly from one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end; management expects some slippage in CASA.
Bulk deposit growth reflected cheaper bulk rates after FCNR(B) inflows. Deposit repricing is expected to be limited in the next two quarters because rates are lower than a year ago.
Around 43% of the book is EBLR-linked (20-23% repo or T-bill linked), with MCLR about 5% and fixed about 47%. EBLR loans reprice on repo changes almost immediately.
Repo rate was raised by 25 bps. New corporate bookings reflect this, but gold loan spreads have not been raised yet.
Third-party distribution is about 5-7% of fee income, so the IRDAI bancassurance draft circular has limited impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and was there any floating or contingent provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no specific one-off. The higher provisions were account-based and conservative, with no floating or contingent provisions. ECL impact is expected to be modest given low SMA and NPA levels.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 20% QoQ rise in current account balances?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end. Some slippage is expected, though core CASA growth is stable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15-16% growth guidance be met and can the bank outpace the system?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will aim for the higher end of 15-16% and grow faster than the market if it is above the market. Retail is to grow faster than corporate, with corporate share targeted down to about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank planning to raise capital?
qa_highlights.answer: No capital raise is planned at 19.40% CAR. The Board has approved INR500 crore of Tier 2 bonds, and capital needs will be reassessed once growth picks up.

qa_highlights.question: Can opex growth stay in single digits while the bank expands branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth will be lower than loan growth, not substantially higher. Cost-to-income is targeted at about 50%, with income growth expected to absorb the added branch and hiring costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate sensitivity of the investment book?
qa_highlights.answer: Each 1 bp move in yields changes MTM by about INR1-1.1 crore. NII benefits from repo hikes through EBLR loans and new gold loans at higher rates.

But there is no major technology overhaul or anything -- any of that things are required.
It may not be very encouraging. But we are not really marginalizing corporate, but we are progressively improving the contribution of retail and MSME to the bank.

Corporate share of advances targeted at about 35% (from 39%), with retail growing faster than corporate; gold loans targeted at 30-32% of advances in the first phase and then 35%.

ECL transition: management said the impact is not substantial, but has not yet decided whether to take the glide path.
Gold loan spreads have not been raised despite the 25 bp repo hike; management said it would act if needed. Repricing of deposits expected to be limited for the next two quarters.
Fee recovery from technically written-off accounts is expected to decline over time, which will weigh on miscellaneous income.

532221|2026-03.headline: Sonata Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 17.7% QoQ to Rs 2,536.2 Cr, while PAT rose 25% QoQ to Rs 130.5 Cr on International margin gains.
532221|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 2,536.2 Cr declined 17.7% QoQ and 3.1% YoY, while PAT rose 25% QoQ to Rs 130.5 Cr. International services delivered EBITDA (before other income and forex) of 20.2%, up 70 bps QoQ, helped by utilisation of 91.8% and an offshore mix of 68%. Domestic business revenue of Rs 1,759.2 Cr was down 25% QoQ, and gross contribution fell 3.9% YoY as an OEM began direct billing some large customers. The call also covered a leadership transition: Rajsekhar Datta Roy was appointed CEO for International after Samir Dhir declined to extend his contract.

financial_highlights.change: flat QoQ; +0.6% QoQ in constant currency

financial_highlights.metric: International EBITDA before OI and forex Q4 FY26

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Q4 gross contribution Rs 75.3 Cr (-1% QoQ, -3.9% YoY); Q4 PAT Rs 46.3 Cr (+3.9% QoQ). FY26 gross contribution Rs 288.7 Cr (-3.5% YoY). SMC and corporate segment grew about 27% YoY.

Management is open to investing for AI-led growth, which could reduce margins if needed.

International growth expected to continue at a similar trajectory in the short term; medium-term growth expected to be gradual.

No M&A plans at present; will wait a couple of quarters and may revisit in the medium term.

Large-deal pipeline count: management's explanation for the drop from 28-32 to 11 needs confirmation in next quarter's investor deck.

we believe that during this fiscal year we should be back to our growth trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the strategy shift for International, investment focus by vertical and sub-vertical, medium-term growth, and the role of M&A.
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Datta Roy (about 15 days into the role) said verticals will continue, with sharper sub-vertical focus, investment in go-to-market, partnerships and AI delivery; specifics to follow in a couple of months. Jagannathan CN said there are no current M&A plans, to wait a couple of quarters and possibly revisit in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether International margins can hold at 91.8% utilisation or whether investment will reduce them, and what the medium-term margin is.
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a similar margin in the short run; utilisation may fall a little with business requirements; offshore mix (68%) is among the best. The company will invest if growth requires it. Endeavour is to maintain EBITDA at a similar level.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked why the large-deal pipeline count fell to 11 from the usual 28-32 range.
qa_highlights.answer: Shilpa Kolhatkar said the overall trajectory is unchanged and the drop reflects two large deals announced in the quarter. Jagannathan CN said the count is a point-in-time figure as of March 31 and that deals converted at year-end are no longer counted.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked when the Domestic business returns to growth on gross contribution and beta basis, and whether direct billing risk remains.
qa_highlights.answer: Sujit Mohanty said the earlier large-customer loss has been almost fully covered over four quarters and the business should return to its growth trajectory this fiscal year. Management does not expect further large-customer losses to direct billing, though it has no written policy from the OEM; two to three customers in discussion were moved to the partner route.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked what is holding back International traction despite AI focus, given the modest size of the business.
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Datta Roy said clients are taking larger AI bets rather than experiments, with green shoots especially in engineering, but decisions are elongated by the client's macro environment rather than technology capability.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the capex jump and the steady-state level, and whether the first-half capex annualised is a fair run-rate.
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan CN said the Q4 increase was a one-time Chennai facility for a large BFSI client. FY27 capex is expected at similar levels to FY26 on a full-year basis; first-half annualisation is not appropriate, and the full figure will be shared separately.

capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 capex spike was a one-time new facility in Chennai to serve one large BFSI customer; management said no plans to expand any other facility at present.
Management said FY27 capex is expected at similar levels to FY26 on an annual basis; the first-half annualised capex figure was not endorsed, with the full-year number to be shared separately.
Facilities were optimised where possible; the company had no comparable facility spend in earlier quarters.
Utilisation at 91.8% in Q4 FY26 (vs 90% in Q3); management said utilisation may come down a little depending on business requirements, having reached its best achievable level.
demand_pricing: International AI-led order book was $16.9 mn in Q4 FY26 and $49 mn for FY26, about 18% of total order book; AI-led pipeline $280 mn as of Q4 FY26.

Q4 FY26 order book $95 mn with book-to-bill of 1.16x; eight large deals won in FY26, two of them in Q4 (including a global fintech core banking modernisation and a multi-year managed services contract with a PE-backed B2B SaaS company).
Top 10 clients contributed 54% of revenue; 12 clients above $5 mn run-rate and 9 clients in the $3-5 mn band (up one from Q3); seven new customers added in Q4 and 23 in FY26.

Healthcare, HLS and BFSI together contributed 30% of Q4 FY26 revenue. BFSI remains under pressure from a large client ramp-down and possible contraction at existing clients; TMT top-client upturn described as early and under watch for sustainability.

532221|2026-06.headline: Sonata Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10.6% YoY to Rs 3,279.1 Cr, but PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs 108.6 Cr on Rs 35.4 Cr forex hit.
532221|2026-06.overview: International services revenue was flat QoQ in constant currency (+0.1%) at $82 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.4% from 20.2% as utilisation dropped to 88.5% on a delayed large-deal ramp-up, a one-time compensation benefit reversed, and AI talent investments rose. Domestic revenue was Rs 2,505.6 Cr with gross contribution up 4.2% QoQ and 14.5% YoY, and management said an OEM direct-billing risk has been partly reversed through contract renewals. Management reiterated an AI-native, engineering-led strategy and an AI order book of $21.4 million, but declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin or formal guidance.

segments.commentary: Revenue $82M, flat QoQ cc and +2.1% YoY cc; EBITDA 15.4% vs 20.2% in Q4 on utilisation drop, one-time Q4 compensation benefit (~2 pts), ~50 bps forex hit and AI talent investments. Headcount 6,293 (vs 6,283), attrition 13%, offshore mix 70%.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,505.6 Cr and gross contribution Rs 78.5 Cr (+14.5% YoY). SMC and corporate software business grew ~82% YoY. DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days, which management attributed to seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA to show positive traction each quarter this year, with some one-time items normalising in coming quarters; it declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin as guidance.
Large-deal ramp-up expected to complete in Q2 FY27; management said margin trajectory should turn positive from next quarter.
Domestic management expects financial performance to keep improving in Q2 and the rest of the year.
Normalised effective tax rate guided at about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit.
Medium-term: management expects gradual improvement in revenue and EBITDA, supported by AI pipeline.
capex_capacity: Utilisation at 88.5% vs 91.8% in Q4; attributed to delayed large-deal ramp-up and AI capability incubation.
Forward deployed engineer pool being expanded to about 100 people by August 2026.
Sonata University has trained 93% of workforce in AI.
Workbench agentic AI service delivery platform launched in the quarter; several clients have shown interest.

About seven new international customer wins in the quarter, including a three-year multimillion-dollar modernisation and managed services deal; a global beverage brand deal (800+ locations, 11 countries) was also won.
Top 10 clients were 51% of international revenue; management declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue, which an analyst said declined QoQ.
Clients above $5M run rate: 12 (flat QoQ); $3-5M: 9 (flat QoQ); clients above $10M run rate: eight.
Management said 21% of engagements are output-based; cloud share of revenue reported at 62% vs 53% a year ago (per analyst question).
Domestic: some customers in the probable direct-billing list were retained through contract renewals after an OEM moved to direct billing with large customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic business confident of sustaining double-digit YoY gross contribution growth, and how are the nine micro-verticals and six value pools defined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management (Jagannathan) said it is confident domestic growth momentum will continue as past issues are behind it. Rajsekhar said the six value pools are customer engagement and ops transformation, agentic AI, legacy modernisation, AI-ready data, resilient AI backbone and AI-native service delivery; micro-verticals include payments, mortgage and lending, healthcare, clinical ops, logistics and retail manufacturing, and are sharpened existing areas rather than new ones.

qa_highlights.question: Top-10 client revenue fell about 6% QoQ and has been weak for six quarters; is productivity pass-through the cause, and what is the absolute top-10 figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan attributed the lower top-10 share (51%) to growth in the 11-20 client bucket and new wins, with no discounts or productivity pass-through and no major top-10 account declining. He declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue, citing risk of exposing top-5 client revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BFSI/retail and manufacturing vertical revenue decline QoQ, and when will they recover; what is the outlook for TMT?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the BFSI share grew beyond expectations, so R&D as a percentage of revenue fell; this is not a standalone R&D issue. Rajsekhar said TMT growth will come from hyperscalers and enterprise product and packaged software organisations, with early pipeline signs from new leadership.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the international margin drop and how will the outcome/output-based model keep margins on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajsekhar said the large-deal ramp-up is largely behind, billing/paperwork delays were one-time, and AI advisory and forward-deployed engineer investments will continue for a couple more quarters; he expects a positive margin trajectory from next quarter. Jagannathan said the top-five accounts appear stable with no major threat, with growth expected in a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net cash fall QoQ, and what is the cash conversion picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the decline reflects domestic vendor payouts tied to turnover and deal completions, with gross cash about Rs 565-567 Cr vs Rs 605 Cr and net cash about Rs 65 Cr vs Rs 30 Cr. He said there was no one-time payment and international collections and DSO were stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state international EBITDA margin, and what is the domestic large-deal margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin, saying it would become guidance; he said margin will move positively in coming quarters. For the domestic large deal, management measures success by absolute gross contribution, which is positive and accretive, not by percentage margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised tax rate and does the R&D tax credit affect cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the normalised ETR is about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit that reduces the cash tax liability.

532234|2026-03.headline: NALCO FY26 revenue rose 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore and PAT 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore, with FY27 alumina guidance of about 25 lakh tons.
532234|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as the best ever year on physical output, sales and financials, with revenue from operations up 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore, EBITDA up 8.72% to Rs.8,613 crore and PAT up 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore. Alumina realisation fell from about $580/t (FY25) to about $370/t (FY26), offset by higher volumes and a metal realisation rise to about $2,700/t. Management guided to lower alumina prices of $300-310/t for FY27 and LME averaging around $3,000-3,100/t as Middle East smelter curtailments unwind. The 5th stream refinery (2 lakh t) is scheduled for commissioning from June 2026, with the smelter and captive power plant project (0.5 mtpa) planned for ordering in FY27.

Management expects FY27 PBT to stay above about Rs.2,000 crore per quarter run-rate if volumes hold and cost does not rise; alumina price decline seen as offset by metal prices.
Employee cost guided lower in FY27 as about 250 superannuations are offset by recruitment; pay revision impact of 10-15% expected from January 2027 (FY28 onwards).

Capex: about Rs.2,000 crore in FY26-27, Rs.4,000-5,000 crore in FY27-28, peaking at Rs.8,000-10,000 crore in FY28-30 for the 0.5 mtpa smelter (about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore) and power plant (about Rs.12,000 crore, to be shared 50:50 with NLC JV).
capex_capacity: 5th stream alumina refinery (2 lakh t): commissioning to start June 2026, taking 3-4 months to reach 50-60% of rated capacity; about one to two months delay possible. Capital work in progress about Rs.6,300 crore, of which about Rs.5,500 crore relates to the 5th stream and is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Proposed 0.5 mtpa aluminium smelter with 270 MW captive power plant: DPR and technology licensor under way; board approval targeted around Aug-Sep 2026; tendering 6-7 months; groundwork from around April-May 2027; completion targeted December 2030 to early 2031.
Power plant to be a 50:50 JV with Neyveli Lignite Corporation (MoU signed, advanced negotiations), with NLC's Talcher coal mine nearby for coal security.
Additional wire rod mill of about 60,000 t (roughly two years) and MI annealing furnace to lift rolled products from about 2,000 t/month to 2,500 t/month.
Utkarsh JV with Mishra Dhatu Nigam discontinued; the Board cited negative IRR on a Rs.4,500-5,000 crore capex plan.
Captive coal target 4.8 mt in FY27; EC clearance for the enhanced coal output expected in about three to four months.
demand_pricing: Middle East smelter curtailments (Qatalum, EGA, Dubal and one other, cut around 50%) reduced alumina demand; Middle East used to take about 40-50% of alumina exports.
Spot alumina tenders recently at $310-336/t; company is relying only on spot tenders with no long-term contracts at present. Recent long-term contract priced at 11-11.5% of LME versus 15-17% earlier.
Japan and Asian premiums rose sharply; NALCO's export premium is fixed for six months via tenders, with the next export tender expected within a month or two.
Domestic alumina sales target of 2.5-3 lakh t in FY27 (about 1.4 lakh t in FY26).

Aluminium cost of production about Rs.155,000-160,000/t (FY26 average about Rs.156,000/t); alumina cost about Rs.20,000-22,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: How much alumina export volume was there and what share goes to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports about 13.09 lakh t and domestic about 1.37 lakh t. Middle East historically took 40-50% of exports, now sharply reduced; no volume impact yet per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 0.5 mtpa smelter capex be phased and what are the numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about Rs.4,000-5,000 crore in FY28 (in management's FY27-28 wording), rising to Rs.8,000-10,000 crore in FY29-30 peak; total smelter about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore and power plant about Rs.12,000 crore, with JV share reducing NALCO's cost to about Rs.23,000-24,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the employee cost and other expenses jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employee cost fell 18% to 15% YoY, with about 351 retirements and 358 inductions in FY26 saving about Rs.65 crore. Other expenses included about Rs.40 crore red mud pond provision and Rs.54 crore additional fly ash transport provision, which are non-cash.

qa_highlights.question: What are alumina and aluminium price expectations for FY27 and what is the margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Alumina $300-310/t average; LME about Rs.3,000-3,100/t on average. Management said the metal price gain (about $400/t vs FY26 at $3,000-3,100) would offset alumina decline; metal is about 73% of revenue vs 27% alumina.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coal mix and cost per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Total requirement 7.2 mt; captive 4.8 mt target FY27 (4.0 mt FY26); balance mainly FSA linkage from Coal India, with e-auction only 10-15%. Captive about Rs.1,500/t, linkage about Rs.1,800/t, e-auction about Rs.2,100/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the wage revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Pay revision from January 2027 expected to raise employee cost 10-15% (possibly 12-13%) in FY28; FY27 impact estimated around Rs.100 crore additional, per management. Per-tonne cost expected to fall with volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 5th Stream refinery commissioning delayed by about 6 months?

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall, and will it stay low through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Average CTC fell from about INR 36 lakh to INR 33 lakh due to superannuation of high-paid staff and entry-level hiring. Last year's provisions for leave and gratuity and lower PRP accruals also contributed, and the trend should continue for the next three quarters. Q4 will rise because of the pay revision.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost inflation erode margins as aluminium prices soften?

qa_highlights.question: Is there any LME-linked alumina term contract for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Coal stocks and monsoon risk for the refineries?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive coal covers about 60-70% of smelter power needs at Angul. Refinery coal stock is only 2-3 days against a 10-15 day norm because of rake priority to power plants. Management expects improvement after summer.

qa_highlights.question: How will the smelter and power capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex to FY31 is about INR 24,000 crore, with the JV's 30:70 debt-equity split. NALCO's cash reserves of about INR 10,500 crore and internal accruals of about INR 3,500 crore a year are expected to fund the smelter without new borrowing.

532259|2026-03.headline: APAR Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR6,603 crores; PAT of INR254 crores was INR285 crores before INR31 crores of one-offs.
532259|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR6,603 crores, with domestic sales up 33.6% and exports up 13.3% YoY. Reported PAT of INR254 crores (3.8% margin) included about INR31 crores of one-offs (gratuity/leave encashment, ECB mark-to-market, and a legal provision); management says the operating PAT was about INR285 crores, up around 14%. FY26 revenue was INR22,902 crores (+23.3%), EBITDA INR2,067 crores (9% margin) and PAT INR977 crores (4.3% margin). Management flagged a near-term slowdown from the Middle East war, metal and freight cost spikes, polymer shortages and project deferrals, while reiterating medium-term growth and raising FY27 capex to about INR1,500 crores.

FY26 revenue INR5,373 crores (+6%), EBITDA INR5,943/KL vs INR6,145/KL. Domestic transformer oil +12.2% for FY26.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,903 crores (+35% YoY); EBITDA INR202 crores at 10.6% margin (+34.5%). FY26 revenue INR6,220 crores (+25.8%), EBITDA INR633 crores at 10.2% margin; cables overtook oil as the second-largest segment. Order book about INR1,800 crores.

guidance_outlook: Conductor medium-to-long-term EBITDA guided at INR35,000-36,000/MT plus tailwinds; no explicit FY27 guidance given.
Cable volumes targeted to grow about 25% a year; conductor volumes about 10% a year.
FY27 capex about INR1,500 crores (Conductor ~INR400 crores, Cables ~INR850 crores, Oil ~INR200 crores), on top of INR740 crores spent in FY26.
Management expects a short-term slowdown in orders and deliveries across India and the US, with US business to grow in FY27 and further in FY28 under Section 232 tariffs.
Middle East business expected to stay subdued until the war is resolved; Iraq conductor deliveries pushed out.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation: Conductor about 90-95%, Cables about 85-90%, Oil about 65-70%; lubricant small-can and bucket filling at 85-90%, with debottlenecking capex planned.

Cable capex is building toward the INR10,000 crore revenue goal, with about INR400 crores spent in FY26 and about INR850 crores carried into FY27; spend is being pulled forward by about INR400 crores.
Cable expansion covers medium-voltage XLP and EPR/rubber cables for data centres, plus wind, solar, railways and defence.
Conductor is at 5 expansion phases; exports of CTC have started to Middle East manufacturers, with Europe and US approvals in progress.
Management says the capex cycle has lengthened from order to installation.
demand_pricing: Conductor order book INR7,671 crores at March 31; premium products are over 50% of the current order book, versus 45.8% of FY26 revenue.
US demand is led by data centres: about $15 million of cables supplied to 3 data-centre projects so far; US cable revenue rose 52.2% YoY in Q4 and 46.7% for FY26.
Section 232 duty is 25% on copper and aluminium cables and 50% on aluminium conductors, which management sees as giving landed-cost visibility.
Domestic HVDC transformer oil awards have just been made; conductor and oil supply for these projects is expected to come later, running through FY27-FY28.
Competition: domestic players are adding capacity, pressuring prices; UltraTech and Adani are seen as focused on building and light-duty wires, while APAR focuses on specialty cables.
Specialty polymer prices and availability were hit by the Middle East war, which limits near-term specialty cable order booking and will hurt volumes and margins.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the US data-centre opportunity, and how should FY27-28 US growth and the capex be read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong US traction led by data centres, with RFQs rising and US demand for both cables and conductors growing; a larger US presence is expected in FY27. Management also said it is not seeing hyperscaler capacity blocking of the kind seen in fibre.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 conductor profitability be thought of?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-to-long-term conductor EBITDA is guided at INR35,000-36,000/MT plus tailwinds; the company does not give next-year guidance and will update as visibility improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and the breakup of the INR1,500 crore FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is Conductor 90-95%, Cables 85-90%, Oil 65-70%. FY27 capex splits into about INR400 crores Conductor, INR200 crores Oil and INR850 crores Cables.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dependence on the Middle East for specialty oils, sourcing and sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing from Saudi Aramco's Yanbu refinery has continued without interruption. Shipments to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait stopped in March and April and resumed in May at higher freight; the Middle East business is expected to stay subdued until the war ends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for premium conductor volumes and CTC exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium conductors were 45.8% of FY26 revenue and over 50% of the order book. CTC exports to Middle East manufacturers have started, with Europe and US approvals in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Will the capex raise cable volumes, and does domestic competition affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across specifications, and the capex is pulling forward spend toward the INR10,000 crore cable target. Management said new entrants may cost a few percentage points of EBITDA, but the market is growing.

risks_watch: Metal price spikes: aluminium at the SHFE premium of about $330-360/t and higher MJP premium, plus freight and insurance cost increases from the war.

Forex and ECB mark-to-market exposure; INR15 crores forex provision in oil in March.

532259|2026-06.headline: Apar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29.1% to INR6,591 crore and PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore, a record quarter.
532259|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 29.1% YoY to INR6,591 crore, with EBITDA post open-period forex up 62.7% to INR814 crore and margin at 12.4% versus 9.8%. PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore (7.1% margin), which management called the highest quarterly sales and profit in company history. Oil division was the largest incremental contributor, helped by inventory gains on rising fuel prices, partly offset by a ~INR94 crore provision. Conductor volumes fell 6.7% as customers deferred manufacturing clearance on conventional conductors amid the aluminium price spike, while premium mix rose. Management declined to answer guidance, forecast or funding questions because of a pending shareholder approval for securities issuance.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to low-cost historical inventory being sold at higher market prices as fuel prices rose. It would not say whether such margins recur, and noted provisions were made as of 30 June per accounting standards.

qa_highlights.question: Why were US exports weak, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a Section 232 disruption in the prior quarter halted US orders, and most US deliveries are on DDP terms, so revenue recognition lagged. It said recent approvals and two large utility contracts support future shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the conductor backlog is executable and what is its geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding the two large orders, most backlog should execute in about a year, with some spill-over. Exports (56.8% of INR10,190 crore) are spread across North and South America, Europe, Africa, and Asia.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is HVDC and premium products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HVDC ordering so far is small; one US utility order includes a high-voltage line, and most HVDC ordering is still to come. No specific premium share in the book was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a difference in margin between domestic and export conductors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export margins depend on product specification and do not always run lower. Domestic conventional products earn lower margins than export ones because of quality standards. Blended EBITDA per ton was given; the split was not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume and realisation split for cables and conductors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave revenue growth only, not volume, and said US sales by geography are not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How are metal-price swings affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said primary sales fell due to customer stocking and deferral, while secondary sales held up and fundamental demand is intact.

qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 45 to 50 days, broadly stable; conductor debtor and inventory days improved QoQ.

US tariffs: Section 232 at 50% on aluminium and conductors; Section 301 at about 10% for India is still under review.

532281|2026-03.headline: HCLTech Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3.3% QoQ to $3,682M with FY27 guidance of 1%-4% cc growth, weighed by two US clients and a soft software quarter.
532281|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was $3,682M, down 3.3% QoQ but up 2.4% YoY in constant currency, with services flat QoQ and software down 28.1% QoQ on seasonality and delayed March deal decisions. Operating margin was 16.5% (17.7% ex-restructuring), and net income was $486M at 13.2% of revenue. Management cited cuts in discretionary telecom spend at two large US clients and two discontinued SAP programs, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 1%-4% cc with EBIT margin of 17.5%-18.5%, excluding two pending acquisitions. The company also extended its capital allocation policy for five years, committing to return at least 75% of net income.

segments.commentary: Q4 fell 1.3% QoQ and grew 3.8% YoY; FY26 grew 9.8%. A manufacturing client with both ER&D and BPO work is among the FY27 headwind clients.

Europe is softening due to geopolitical escalation; North America is broadly robust apart from the two client issues.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said deflation is concentrated in SDLC productivity and could run higher there, but it kept 2%-3% for HCLTech's portfolio, citing limited autonomous production-fix capability. AI Factory is seeing the most traction, with two major clients and three to four more expected.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two SAP programs and two telecom accounts linked, and is there a broader vertical problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the telecom clients and the two other clients (a manufacturing and a retail client, about 50 bps combined) are unrelated with no overlap. The lower end of guidance assumes softness continues; outside these items, business is said to be on the same pace.

qa_highlights.question: Is the telecom impact a full-quarter drag of roughly 1% on growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the SOWs were expected in CY26 spend and were cancelled after dragging, so the impact is more than one month. It assumes the impact lasts through year-end and that it is included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Are the SAP program cancellations budget-driven or technology-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said they were budget-related: clients de-prioritized modernization, and SAP timeline extensions may be a factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the software/products business?
qa_highlights.answer: Data and operations (IntelliOps, AEX) are growing and will offset declines in the experience portfolio. FY27 expectation is low-single digit, flattish or marginally declining; perpetual license timing is hard to predict, especially government buying.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 software spillover return in Q1, and what is the trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say whether deals will return, as timing is unpredictable. It noted total revenue growth is 0.5% below services growth, the first such gap in recent years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI-driven pricing deflation already visible, and is it bigger than traditional renewal cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the AI effect is incremental to normal productivity pass-through, very little has played out yet, and it expects the impact from FY27 on, which is why guidance is lower.

532281|2026-06.headline: HCLTech Q1 FY27 revenue $3,650M, down 0.5% QoQ but up 2.6% YoY in constant currency; record Q1 net new TCV of $2.4B; FY27 guidance held at 1-4%.
532281|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was seasonally weak sequentially, with revenue down 0.5% QoQ and EBIT margin at 16.9% (up 39 bps QoQ, helped by lower restructuring). Services grew 3.5% YoY, with ITBS up 4.2% and ER&D up only 0.3% YoY after a 3.7% QoQ decline. Net new TCV of $2.4B was the highest ever Q1, excluding a mega deal signed in early July. Management kept FY27 organic guidance of 1-4% revenue and 17.5-18.5% margin, and announced entry into AI datacenters with an up to INR3,500 crore initial investment.

qa_highlights.question: What limits raising guidance given record Q1 bookings and the early-July mega deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the band is broad and only Q1 is done; the mega deal transitions over a couple of months with steady state only by April 2027 and negligible FY27 revenue impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the AI datacenter investment look like a colocation-cost build (about $7M per MW), and what further commitments follow?
qa_highlights.answer: INR3,500 crore is only an initial fraction of the long-term 50 MW plan; it is a full-stack play, not colocation, with further investment tied to free cash flow and funded via partners, client commitments, hardware financing, and equity/debt mix.

qa_highlights.question: Token costs: will they collapse or stay high, and what does that mean for services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token prices may fall but total token consumption will rise, so total cost rises; tiered architecture with enterprise SLMs creates a new engineering services wave in data work and training.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 18-19% soon, perhaps in FY28?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ER&D decline and will it continue?

qa_highlights.question: Why enter datacenters now, and how does this differ from the cloud cycle? Also, what about GPU oversupply risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued private AI stacks and SLMs differ from the cloud cycle, that megawatts are an anchor and value lies in wrapped services, and that the market remains GPU-starved; no explicit utilisation or tenancy assumptions were given.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance include amortization from M&A, and is the services outlook tougher than at the start of the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is organic and excludes acquisitions including Jaspersoft and CTG; macro view is unchanged since March and management will revisit after Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How big will Jaspersoft be, and when does CTG close?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaspersoft is expected to add about $10-15M per quarter with seasonality, consolidated from Q2; CTG expected to close later in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How is value shared between frontier AI labs and managed services, and how will it look in steady state?

qa_highlights.question: Who is HCLTech competing with in Advanced AI deals?

qa_highlights.question: When will FCF-to-net-income conversion return to the 3-4 year average?

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the top end of guidance given strong Services growth and a seasonally strong Q3?

qa_highlights.question: Are the AI engagements with OpenAI/Anthropic under T&M or fixed price, with meaningful TCV?

qa_highlights.question: Are the ramp-downs in top-20 clients behind us?

qa_highlights.question: Why does Software margin expand while revenue declines, and how do Services margins look?
qa_highlights.answer: Software Q1 had a one-off restructuring cost; excluding it, lower employee costs and lower amortization drove the QoQ margin gain. Services margins benefited from Project Ascend and the higher Advanced AI mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic decline in Software and how long can ARR-to-revenue disconnect last?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue fell about 15% YoY on an organic basis while ARR rose 2.6% ex-Jaspersoft. Management attributed the gap to upfront recognition of multiyear licences and perpetual licence timing, expecting renewals to return in FY28 and FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in HPE Telco Solutions (Aruba TS) revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only two months were consolidated and extrapolating to three months should be right; there may be small seasonality but nothing major.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q3-Q4 Services sequential growth expected to decelerate versus Q2 organic growth of about 2.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the mega deal not contributing until Q1 FY28 as the main outlier, and said it is being conservative given uncertainty, with Services likely above the midpoint.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from ecosystem partners, and what is the impact of frontier-lab partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not track partner-channel revenue reliably, much of it is influenced rather than direct. It is a small but growing professional services partner for hyperscalers and frontier and GPU companies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the earlier aspiration of 18%-19% remains the desired band, but he would not commit to it now, preferring to invest in capability and differentiation.

Macro and geopolitical volatility (Middle East conflict cited) and US PERM program suspension (management says immaterial).

532285|2026-03.headline: Geojit's FY26 profit absorbed planned investments; distribution income up 10% and equity MF net inflow share rose to 0.40 from 0.33.
532285|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as the first year of "Geojit 2.0", a shift toward recurring income (mutual fund distribution, advisory, PMS, insurance) with investments in sales headcount, IT and brand. Net sales headcount rose by about 700 to 3,768, including 650 in sales, at a cost of about INR29 crores, and brand spend rose by about INR15 crores. Profitability was hit by these investments, with about INR54 crores of transformation expenses booked and ROE reduced as brokerage income fell. Management said the next two years would carry similar investment costs, and it stopped field hiring for the current year because of the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.metric: Equity MF net inflow market share
Transformation / investment expenses booked in FY26

financial_highlights.change: total cash about INR1,115 crores, of which INR700-800 crores already deployed in MTF and lending
PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY; INR450 crores in FY23
NRI income about INR90 crores in FY26

segments.name: Broking and distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution income grew 10% in FY26 while brokerage income declined, which management cited as the reason for lower ROE. Legacy clients (7+ years) contribute 58-60% of broking and MF income.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Equity MF net inflow market share improved to 0.40 from 0.33 while industry equity net inflows were down about 20%. MF AUM per client rose to about INR5 lakh from about INR3.5 lakh in FY22.

segments.name: Insurance distribution
segments.commentary: Health insurance premium of close to INR22 crores in its first year of distribution, previously life only.

segments.name: Private Wealth
segments.commentary: AUM about INR2,400 crores; about 55 RMs and 90 staff; plans to hire 25-30 RMs in FY27; around 5 to 8 branch cities with no new cities planned.

segments.name: DIFC / Middle East
segments.commentary: DIFC entity licensed and operational since February 2026 as an external asset manager to private banks; 3 staff and client onboarding expected to start by end of May 2026. Minimum ticket size about USD 1 million.

segments.name: PMS / AIF
segments.commentary: PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY; one AIF via GIFT City in application stage; 1-2 more PMS schemes expected in FY27.

Management expects the domestic MF industry to grow at least double digits over 2-5 years.
Insurance (including health) is being used as a substitute for market-linked products when equity markets are weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is the DIFC entity traction, and how does it differ from the existing Middle East JVs? What is the NRI AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: DIFC is a private banking external-asset-manager business that started operations in February 2026, with client onboarding expected by end-May 2026. Existing Middle East entities are retail-focused. NRI AUM is INR12,000-13,000 crores, with about INR90 crores of income in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring and capex plans for the current year?
qa_highlights.answer: Field hiring has been stopped because of the West Asia crisis; only replacements will be made. IT spend of about INR30 crores is planned over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback plans and borrowing to fund MTF, given cash of about INR1,100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that borrowing is cheaper than using own cash and said it intends to borrow for MTF, LAS and NBFC needs. Buyback will be considered after SEBI rules are issued.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic client reaction in March and April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clients increased investments in MF, and that April was too early to judge given the ceasefire uncertainty. Management expects short-term apprehension but long-term industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: ROE trajectory and dilution from the strategic shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward ROE guidance. It said ROE fell because brokerage declined while distribution income rose; no equity raise is planned and the transformation will be funded internally.

qa_highlights.question: PMS growth is modest. What are the bottlenecks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY to INR1,450 crores and that the team has been selling PMS for only three years.

risks_watch: Profitability pressure from about two more years of investment costs, with ROE already lower because brokerage income fell.

532285|2026-06.headline: Geojit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR160.4 crore and PAT to INR19.8 crore, but management guided to continued cost pressure and no hiring for several quarters.
532285|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR160.40 crore, up 11% YoY, with PBT of INR25.99 crore (up 4% QoQ) and PAT of INR19.83 crore (up 14% QoQ). Employee cost rose INR18 crore on sales force expansion, DIFC hiring, tech team additions and higher incentives, though management said employee cost would normalise after a lower insurance-incentive quarter. Customer assets reached INR1.11 lakh crore (up 15% QoQ), mostly from market appreciation, with recurring assets at INR26,000 crore. Management said margin benefits from FY26 investments would take a couple more quarters, and that hiring has been paused except for replacements due to Middle East conflict and market conditions. Leadership succession was also confirmed, with Jones George becoming MD from 1 October.

financial_highlights.change: Net inflows about INR2,000 crore over the year

financial_highlights.value: INR17,778 crore (as read in call; speaker first said INR1,778 crore)

financial_highlights.metric: Lending book (MTF and loan against shares)

financial_highlights.value: About INR1,000-1,100 crore; about 70% deployed in MTF/NBFC lending and trading, rest in FDs and AIF

segments.name: Insurance distribution
segments.commentary: Gross premium of INR103 crore in the quarter. Cross-sell penetration is under 5%, and growth is limited to existing clients.

segments.commentary: Asset management AUM about INR17,778 crore per the analyst's figure. Yield Plus AIF has run 11 months and is sold only to in-house clients so far; third-party distribution not yet appointed.

segments.commentary: GCC AUM is a little under USD 1 billion. Revenue is booked at share of JV profit (Barjeel 30%). Middle East business is under pressure since March, and expansion is paused. DIFC business only recently started booking.

Recruitment paused except for replacements until the geopolitical and market outlook is clearer; earlier plan had been aggressive hiring.

Insurance income was lower in April-June than in Jan-Mar, reducing incentive outflows and employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: Are the FY26 investments starting to show up in financial performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some productivity gains are visible, but covering costs will take longer because most recurring MF, PMS and AIF revenue is trail-based.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March quarter carried high insurance incentive payouts, while April-June had lower insurance income, so employee cost normalised; fresh hiring is slow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East outlook and the GCC contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC AUM is a little under USD 1 billion. Middle East investment decisions are on hold, and no expansion is planned until stability returns.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net cash levels and buyback plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is about INR1,000-1,100 crore, with about 70% deployed in MTF/NBFC lending and trading. A buyback is being considered but has no timeline; consolidation opportunities may take priority.

qa_highlights.question: Why do investors choose Geojit given weak PAT over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Geojit focuses on delivery and MF trail income rather than F&O. It expects margins to improve in coming quarters, not immediately.

SIP and new-client momentum has slowed, and productivity of the expanded sales force is still unproven.
Middle East and GCC NRI business faces conflict and FCNR-related outflows, with no expansion planned.
Customer asset growth was mostly market-driven, so flows need to be tracked against market moves.
Buyback and capital allocation remain undecided, with consolidation as a possible alternative use of cash.

532286|2026-03.headline: Jindal Steel Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,647 crores (INR 10,093/t) on ASP up INR 4,743/t QoQ, with FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt.
532286|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery: consolidated gross revenue rose 28% QoQ to INR 19,399 crores and adjusted EBITDA reached INR 2,647 crores, helped by a rise in HRC and TMT rebar prices and Angul volume ramp-up. Sales volume grew 15% QoQ to 2.62 Mt as the Angul expansion took steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa. A one-time impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated) was booked on the Australian WCL asset after the shaft was closed. Management said the major capex programme is essentially complete and the focus shifts to asset sweating and deleveraging.

segments.name: Steel (India, Angul/Raigarh/Patratu)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 9.25 Mt (+14% YoY) and sales 8.68 Mt (+9% YoY). Q4 production 2.65 Mt (+6% QoQ, +26% YoY) and sales 2.62 Mt (+15% QoQ, +23% YoY). Flat/long mix was 52:48 in Q4 and 49:51 for FY26.

segments.name: Raw materials / overseas mines
segments.commentary: Iron ore sourcing about 60% outside purchases and 40% captive, with pricing described as stable. Mozambique is EBITDA positive, South Africa operating but not EBITDA positive, and Australia is closed with minimal cash burn.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi power plant commissioned (two 525 MW modules); ramp-up to complete within H1 FY27. Surplus power to be sold but described as not material to financials.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 11–11.5 Mt and sales at 10.5–11 Mt.
Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to rise by USD 20–25/t sequentially; iron ore movement of plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil–Angul) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; savings of about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps up.
Port facility to be commissioned; DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) expected towards end of FY27; PP2 also remaining.
Capex guidance of INR 7,500–10,000 crores for expansion and sustenance capex; remaining programme capex INR 11,545 crores.
Leverage expected to normalise by Q2 FY27; value-added flat mix expected to move from about 50% toward 70%.
Start-up costs of INR 125 crores in Q4 are said to be finished and not recurring.
capex_capacity: Steelmaking capacity raised to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa after BOF2 and BOF3 (3 Mt each) at Angul; iron-making capacity increased by 6.6 Mt through BF2 (4.6 Mt, operational) and DRI2 (2 Mt, under construction).
Cold rolling complex of 1.2 Mtpa commissioned at Angul to support value-added product mix.
Coal pipe conveyor from Utkal C thermal coal mine to Angul is operational; slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul close to completion.
Total planned capex programme INR 47,043 crores: INR 25,924 crores spent up to FY25 and INR 9,574 crores in FY26, leaving INR 11,545 crores.
Thakurani-A1 iron ore block declared preferred bidder; Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block awarded at end of last year.
Rail rake programme of about 79 rakes: 72 acquired, remainder expected within 2–3 months.
demand_pricing: Management expects India steel demand growth of about 9–9.5% and cites FY26 finished steel consumption of 164.2 Mt (+8% YoY) and Q4 consumption of 44.6 Mt (+10% QoQ).

Realisations lag because the order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations. Management said the market is holding firm despite a slight dip in recent weeks.
Management declined to give a Q1/Q2 realisation upside estimate, saying the market is hard to predict.
Flat sales focus is on infrastructure first, then building and construction, downstream products and automobiles. HSM grades developed for niche products are ramping in the current quarter.
Management said the Q4 sales run rate reflects seasonality, so no large sequential volume pickup is expected.
Safeguard duty on flat steel imports reduced to 11.5% from 12% effective 21 Apr 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will steel and realisation gains continue into Q1, and have contracts been reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts on earlier prices continue and ASP rose strongly in Q4 because of the spot/contract lag; the market is holding firm, though slightly softer recently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company shift to asset sweating rather than further capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the capex programme is essentially complete and the focus is on sweating assets, with INR 7,500–10,000 crores allocated to expansion and sustenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value-added share falling and what is the target mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the priority during ramp-up is utilisation, with mix optimisation starting in H1 FY27 and stabilising in H2. Flat mix is about 50:50 today and is expected to reach about 70% flat over time.

qa_highlights.question: What were the start-up costs this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q4 start-up costs at INR 125 crores, most of which were booked in Q3, and said these will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the slurry pipeline savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slurry savings are about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps. Full utilisation is not expected this year, but per-tonne savings do not depend on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further write-downs on overseas assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no further write-downs are expected, based on an independent valuation. Australia has minimal cash outflow, and Mozambique is EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: What are the raw material cost moves into Q1?

Management said new anti-infectives in the US market total about $1 billion; the company does not plan to create new demand but to take share, with price neutrality.
Competition: cefiderocol (Fetroja) cited as the closest competitor; management claimed Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile, without numerical head-to-head data.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from Zaynich over the next 6 to 24 months, and capex and commercial costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman expects slow initial revenue growth, a hockey-stick curve after 12-18 months, INR200-300 crore capex over three years, and no capex for sales build-out, only revenue cost. Breakeven expected in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Does Zaynich qualify for the 10% PLI and what is the China strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Government funding recognised but immaterial versus R&D spend. China: Chinese patients in trial were insufficient; a small China study is ongoing and a partner may be sought.

qa_highlights.question: Will Zaynich be made in Europe for the US and in India for emerging markets?
qa_highlights.answer: US supply from an FDA-inspected European site as a de-risking step; India supply from India; emerging markets from India or Europe depending on timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wockhardt exit US generics and will it re-enter?
qa_highlights.answer: US generics were about 5% of the portfolio and loss-making, amid the 2012-13 FDA import alert. Management said it is re-entering with innovative products sourced from European manufacturers, with India production for India.

qa_highlights.question: Patent life and exclusivity for Zaynich, Emrok and Miqnaf?
qa_highlights.answer: Zaynich patent runs to 2038 in India with further filings planned; Miqnaf patent to early 2033 in India. QIDP status gives five extra years in US; minimum 10-year market exclusivity in US and Western markets.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and patient targets for FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: US price about $1,200-1,500 per day, typically $10,000-15,000 per course; India priced about 75-80% below US. Long-term share of 20-25% of resistant cases, with no FY28-29 patient numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Peak sales of Zaynich?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $1.5-2 billion per year globally at peak, not cumulative, with US around 40% of global revenue.

risks_watch: Commercial execution: a new US sales model for antibiotics with a commercial operating partner, 6,000 US hospitals to segment, and a first-time anti-infective launch for the company.
Losses or breakeven in the first 12-18 months from US launch costs; Chairman's comments on profitability were clarified as Zaynich-only.

Zaynich Phase 2 waiver for the aztreonam combination (Odrate) not expected; Odrate timing about four years.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the CDMO contribution in Q1 and what growth to expect from the Viatris partnership over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Aggarwal said Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) booked only about ₹5-6 crore in Q1, with growth reflecting in Q2 and Q3. He said about ₹100-130 crore is expected from these two products, not the full ₹200 crore in year one, and that it would build over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are export margins for CDMO and own-brands, and how will the ₹250 crore cash and Synthimed stake be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gross margin is about 55%. The ₹250 crore cash will be deployed as capex over about 2.5 years (warehouse, existing capacity, Jammu). No plans to divest the Synthimed stake this year; Synthimed budgeted EBITDA is about ₹750 crore and Q1 results are on track.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% EBITDA margin sustainable, and could it rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is fully sustainable and could reach 21-22% if sales grow quarter on quarter. It denied calling Q1 a turnaround, citing litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business for about 1.5 years that are now over.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 revenue guidance of ₹1200 crore not being raised, and when does growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not revise at this stage and will revisit by year-end. Growth is H2-weighted via Arrotex Macrogol in Q2 and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4. FY27 expectation is about ₹900 crore, with export sales of about ₹750 crore, roughly 45% from CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D capability was retained?
qa_highlights.answer: The API business was sold to Synthimed in FY24 for net about ₹2000-2100 crore, used to repay group debt of about ₹1250-1300 crore. Retained R&D in Panchkula handles regulatory compliance, tech transfer and global filings, with new land bought for a further R&D facility.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and will there be a capacity shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen and granules ran at about 70% in Q1 on pilot batches. Management expects 90% utilisation of the FY29 plan over time and sees no capacity dearth. Capex for new molecules will follow only after filings are complete.
