532309|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PBT from continuing operations hit INR 119 crore, but one-offs (incl. ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal) drove much of it; underlying FY26 EBITDA margin 11%.
532309|2026-03.overview: GE Power India reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 316 crore (up from INR 266 crore YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR 1,269 crore (up 21%), led by Core Services (+14%) and Upgrades (+24%). Profit before tax and exceptional items from continuing operations was INR 119 crore in Q4 versus a loss of INR 15 crore a year earlier, and INR 340 crore for FY26 versus INR 22 crore, with management flagging sizeable one-offs in both periods. Order intake fell sharply to INR 877 crore for FY26 from INR 2,183 crore, and order backlog declined to INR 1,628 crore from INR 2,662 crore, mainly due to termination of FGD-EP contracts. Management is pushing a service-led, short-cycle strategy, has settled with BHEL and Jaypee, and has signed a Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy, with a recommended dividend of INR 7 per share (70% of face value).

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% YoY and core orders rose 32% YoY; Core Services order backlog up about 40% YoY. Management says about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book executes in FY27 (12-month cycles).

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by upgrade volumes in Q4; Vindhyachal and Wanakbori complex upgrade orders of INR 591 crore were booked in FY25.

segments.name: New Build / FGD EPC (AQCS)
segments.commentary: In close-out mode; FGD-EP contracts of Jaypee Bina and Nigrie (INR 775 crore) were terminated, driving backlog decline. Seven operational acceptances and four unit completions achieved in FY26.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Being demerged to JSW Energy; asset of about 660 acres, reported losses in recent quarters. Five-year JSW supply and capacity agreement signed to protect core services manufacturing needs.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give numeric FY27 guidance; CFO said the FY26 underlying EBITDA base (11%) is set and FY27 margins should be at par or better, without a range.
About 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book (INR 1,628 crore) expected to execute in FY27, implying roughly INR 1,380-1,470 crore; this is a management estimate from the call, not formal guidance.
Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy: filed with NCLT; target completion in calendar 2026, and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026 at the latest.
Core Services target addressable fleet of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore; company holds about 18% share and aims to grow it before considering other areas.
Management says the ECL impact from the BHEL settlement is fully recognised as of 31 Mar 2026, so no similar reversal is expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Durgapur manufacturing facility to be demerged to JSW Energy; a five-year agreement with JSW covers reserved manufacturing capacity and supply for core services boiler components.
Management aims to build an alternate supply chain for boiler components within about 18 months to become independent of JSW after the five-year agreement.
Three PG tests completed for key new-build units and multiple synchronisations and facility closures achieved in FY26.
Eighteen new first-of-its-kind service products ordered during FY26; first-time generator repairs, turbine upgrades and control system solutions delivered.
demand_pricing: Management says thermal plant PLF and availability are rising, increasing services demand; target addressable market quoted at INR 3,500-4,000 crore.
Q4 order intake of INR 254 crore was below the prior-year INR 285 crore (which included INR 52 crore O&M); FY26 orders fell 60% YoY on the FY25 FGD-EP and complex upgrade wins.

FGD mandate: per the July 2025 notification, Category C plants (over 200 GW) were removed and Category A (about 8 GW, mainly Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra) must install FGD; Category B is optional with no tariff pass-through if they opt in. Management says the mandate has limited near-term order impact.
Management is pursuing 13 countries for boilers, including Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Indonesia, while stating its perimeter remains India-only for GEPIL and non-GEPIL assets.

qa_highlights.question: Does GEPIL participate in gas turbine, HRSG or combined-cycle business?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said no; HRSG and gas-plant business belong to GE Vernova's gas business and fall outside GEPIL's objects, which are steam and thermal only.

qa_highlights.question: Of the order book, how much is executable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aashish Ghai said short-cycle orders typically complete within 12 months, so about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book is expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will backlog grow after the current book runs off, and is the business widening beyond core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is new-build close-out. Core backlog is up about 40% YoY; the company plans to grow its 18% share of the INR 3,500-4,000 crore fleet before expanding to other areas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 450 crore loan and what yield does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said it is surplus cash lent to a promoter-group cash pool benchmarked to HSBC, with rates of 5.5-6.35% in FY26, about 0.25% above commercial bank deposit rates. Lending is board-approved, shareholder-approved and audited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the FGD opportunity and the margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: Roshan Singh outlined the notification: Category A (about 8 GW) must install FGD, Category B is optional, and Category C was removed. He said the mandate has limited weight for GEPIL unless utilities act proactively. No margin range was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 880 crore net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said the cash is under evaluation for deployment into growth in services, with no specific plan disclosed yet and shareholder value as the stated priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Durgapur demerger timeline and benefit to minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said the NCLT petition is filed, creditor and shareholder approvals and tax/bank NOCs are required, and completion is targeted for this calendar year and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026. Shareholders receive entitlement shares in the resulting company.

qa_highlights.question: Will the demerger affect manufacturing needed for core services?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no, because a five-year JSW Energy agreement reserves manufacturing capacity at pre-set schedule and price. An alternate supply chain is targeted within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the underlying EBITDA margin excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said FY26 normalised entity-level EBITDA was 11%, with Q4 at about 18%. He declined to give a numeric margin range for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL-related reversals continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no; the BHEL settlement is fully executed, with the final tranche received in March 2026, and the ECL impact is complete as of 31 Mar 2026.

532321|2026-03.headline: Zydus Q4 FY26 revenue up 16% YoY to ₹75.9bn with EBITDA margin at 33.7%; FY27 guided to high-teens consolidated growth and >24% margin.
532321|2026-03.overview: Zydus closed FY26 with consolidated revenue of ₹271.5bn (up 17%) and EBITDA of ₹84.8bn (up 20%), with a record 31.2% full-year EBITDA margin. Q4 revenue of ₹75.9bn rose 16% YoY and 11% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 33.7%, helped by product mix, operating leverage and forex. The company made several acquisitions (Comfort Click, Amplitude Surgical, LiqMeds) and proposed the Assertio Holdings deal for US specialty oncology, while net debt/EBITDA was 0.5x at March 2026. Management guided FY27 to high-teens revenue growth and EBITDA margin above 24%, with US growth in single digits on a high base.

segments.name: Medical devices
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.8 billion; focus on orthopedics (Amplitude portfolio, Andy robotic surgical system), cardiology and nephrology, including a planned high-end dialyzer membrane facility.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: strong double-digit revenue growth; India mid-teens, international and US around single digit per management (US single-digit cited in response to a question).
EBITDA margin guidance of 24%+ maintained for FY27, assuming Saroglitazar investment ramps in H2 FY27.
Other expenses run-rate of about ₹1,900-2,000 crore per quarter, all-inclusive of Saro costs, excluding R&D.
FY27 capex guided at about ₹1,500-1,600 crore.
Saroglitazar US launch targeted for FY28 (April 2028); first two years mainly investment, meaningful revenue from years two and three.
Long-term EBITDA margin ambition of 28-30% as branded share moves toward two-thirds of revenue over roughly five years.
US launches planned for FY27: 30-40, at least 30+ including specialty.
Vaccines revenue target of ₹300-400 crore on track.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at ₹1,500-1,600 crore; Q1 capex rose sharply, driven by SEZ 3 facility, expansions at Moraiya, Goa, Baddi and SEZ Units 2 and 3, a new formulations R&D centre, a CAR-T facility for biologics, a new vaccines DS facility, Zylidac investments, and a one-time wellness land acquisition.
Injectable facility at Zydus Biotech Park received an EIR with VAI classification after GMP inspections in April and May 2026.
Joint venture with Sunshine Healthcare signed to build a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Sri Lanka.
High-end dialyzer membrane facility planned for medtech nephrology.
demand_pricing: India branded growth of 20% driven by chronic portfolio, innovation brands (Lipaglyn), biosimilars and vaccines scaling; semaglutide is a small contributor to growth per management.
Aflibercept biosimilar launched in India (first mover) with good early traction per management.
Desidustat approved in China; NRDL reimbursement needed for major share; management expects a couple of quarters before more visibility. Competitor molecule reportedly at $200+ million in China.
Saroglitazar US peak sales view of $200-300 million (conservative) and $400+ million (optimistic); competitors upgraded guidance, indicating a larger market.
Mirabegron remains a profitable semi-exclusive product despite royalty and settlement costs that weigh on gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 strong topline growth implying growth above the FY27 double-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the guidance of strong double-digit growth for the year; India expected mid-teens growth, 300-500 bps above market, with international and US around single digit.

qa_highlights.question: How will opex (employee, SG&A) rise with Assertio and Saro, and is the 24%+ margin still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Saro costs have started, with a meaningful increase in H2; 24% margin guidance maintained. Other expenses run-rate of ₹1,900-2,000 crore per quarter, all-inclusive. Management said about 80% of the increase is acquisition-driven (Zylidac, Assertio) plus freight.

qa_highlights.question: Capex color and full-year number?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex guided at ₹1,500-1,600 crore, spread across multiple capacity and R&D projects plus a one-time wellness land purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Saro ramp and peak sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch in April 2028 (FY28); first two years are investment-led; conservative peak $200-300 million, optimistic $400+ million.

qa_highlights.question: US branded revenue composition and Assertio contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Branded is about 10% of US revenue; Sentynl about $60 million last year (ultra-rare); the rest is 505(b)(2) products; Assertio adds from next quarter at $15-20 million per quarter run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin dip QoQ and YoY: is Mirabegron the reason and will it normalise in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to higher Mirabegron settlement/licensing costs under the Innovator arrangement. CEO said Mirabegron is profitable and semi-exclusive, and guidance still assumes 24% EBITDA margin.

risks_watch: Saro launch investment in H2 FY27 and FY28 could compress margins against the 24%+ guidance.
US generics pricing and Mirabegron royalty/settlement costs weigh on gross margin; monitor whether they normalise.
Slower-than-expected uptake of 505(b)(2) product BEIZRAY; monitor scale-up in FY28.
Desidustat China ramp depends on NRDL reimbursement, expected in 2-3 quarters.
Amortisation from acquisitions (Assertio purchase price allocation within 12 months) and Mirabegron licensing amortisation until Q2 FY28 will keep depreciation and amortisation elevated.
ALS (Usnoflast) phase 2b data expected FY28 end or early FY29; US biosimilar scale-up expected in calendar 2029.
Injectable facility VAI classification at Zydus Biotech Park could affect injectable supply and US approvals.

532341|2026-03.headline: IZMO Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR109.16 crore (+82.5% YoY), with FY26 revenue up 26.8% to INR284.88 crore.
532341|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 posted the highest quarterly revenue in company history at INR109.16 crore, up 82.5% YoY and 84.7% QoQ, with net profit of INR17.3 crore. Management attributed the jump partly to a one-off special project for a client group, where a large share was passed through as outsourced expense, which lifted other expenses to about INR69 crore. FY26 consolidated net profit was INR47.56 crore, broadly flat YoY, which management tied to izmoMicro investment-phase costs. Management guided FY27 izmoMicro revenue to INR45-50 crore, EBITDA margin to 20-25%, and said it is raising about INR150 crore (equity-cum-debt, not yet finalised) mainly for capex.

Sharp rise YoY; linked to pass-through project costs

Per analyst question; not contested by management

segments.commentary: Most established division with steady subscription revenue; completely redesigned portal launched last year is gaining traction with rental, insurance, leasing and dealer customers.

segments.name: izmoCars (automotive digital marketing)
segments.commentary: Completed Stellantis rollout across its European aftersales network; some Q4 revenue came from one-off OEM projects, per management. US organic client additions continued, and Geronimo (UK) added OEM and dealer clients in Germany and Central Europe.

segments.name: FrogData (decision intelligence)
segments.commentary: Products include FDAP, Warranty Boost+, FixedOps Mojo and FixedOps Velocity; gross revenue retention above 93%. Revenue was flat for two quarters, which management attributed to a sluggish market, and it says a resurgence began in Q4; Ford partnership extends to FordDirect's The Shop.

segments.name: izmoMicro (semiconductor packaging and silicon photonics)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR40-60 crore (figures given differ within the call) with pipeline of about INR100 crore; FY27 revenue guided at INR45-50 crore. Capacity about INR150 crore top line today, with expansion to about INR1,200 crore addressable top line. Defence supply contracts and a German subsidiary were added.

guidance_outlook: izmoMicro FY27 revenue guided at INR45-50 crore, against about INR18-19 crore in FY26; management said quarterly timing may be lumpy.
FY27 blended EBITDA margin guided at 20-25%; FY28 blended EBITDA margin guided at around 30%-plus.
Overall FY27 revenue growth expected, but management declined to commit to 30-35%, and said 20-25% is the target.

Capex plan of about INR150 crore in FY27 (about INR125 crore capex, INR25 crore working capital), with expansion targeted to come on stream around mid-FY27 and revenue from Q3 FY28 per management timeline.
Other expenses expected to fall in the next quarter after the one-off project.
capex_capacity: Current silicon photonics/packaging capacity is about INR150 crore top line; the current INR40 crore order book would take about 9 months to execute.
Post-expansion addressable top line about INR1,200 crore; management said it could reach about INR200 crore top line once the expansion is in place.
Phased utilisation plan post-expansion: about 20% for the first 6 months, then 50-60%, then 80-90%.
Expansion targeted by mid-FY28 implementation per management timeline; the project takes about one year to implement.

demand_pricing: Management cited hyperscaler data centre investments in India of over INR3 lakh crore and a global silicon photonics TAM of about $30 billion, expected to reach about $80 billion in a couple of years.
Packaging cost share: 8-10% of chip cost at OSAT level, about 50% for advanced packaging, and about 80% for silicon photonics, per management.
Gross margin on packaging is 50-60%, with silicon photonics higher, per management.

Receivables are about 100-110 days; large clients such as Hertz, Stellantis and Avis pay in 4-5 months, and management said operations remain cash-flow positive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline YoY and is the current margin normalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin dip was a conscious choice to build revenue and client campaigns, and that margins should recover as izmoMicro scales and the cost base stays flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the izmoMicro FY27 revenue and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 izmoMicro revenue guided at INR45-50 crore; order book about INR40 crore with a pipeline of about INR100 crore, though the call also cited INR60 crore earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump to INR69 crore and will they persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a special project for a client group led to large outsourced, pass-through expenses; costs should decline next quarter, but a similar pass-through project may recur in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will izmoMicro be funded, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is raising INR100-150 crore, as equity-cum-debt; the route and split are not yet finalised, with an announcement expected within 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly is the order book executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timelines range from 3 months to 2 years depending on the project; the INR40 crore order book would take about 9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and why the delay in raising it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR150 crore is being raised, with about INR125 crore for capex; the delay was due to firming up technology and machine choices before starting the fundraise in May.

532343|2026-03.headline: TVS Motor FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 47,270 crores with record Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores and 13.1% EBITDA margin.
532343|2026-03.overview: TVS Motor reported record FY26 volume of 5.9 million units (up 24%), revenue of INR 47,270 crores (up 30%) and operating PBT of INR 4,975 crores (up 40%). Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores grew 36% YoY with EBITDA margin of 13.1%, against 6.5% when the margin recovery began. Management flagged near-term supply disruptions (gas, labour at Tier 2 suppliers, raw material timing, container lead times) and 3-5% commodity cost inflation, and guided to a strong single-digit industry growth in FY27 with capex of about INR 3,500 crores.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 37% from INR 4,450 crores; margin up 60 bps from 12.3%
vs INR 1,172 crores in Q4 FY25
vs INR 851 crores in Q4 FY25
PBT up 22%; book up 15% from INR 26,647 crores

segments.name: 2-wheeler ICE (domestic)
segments.commentary: FY26 2W ICE sales grew 22% vs industry 12%; Q4 domestic ICE grew 26% vs industry 24%. Scooter category share is about 38% (including EV), which management expects to exceed 40%.

segments.name: Electric 2-wheeler
segments.commentary: FY26 EV 2W sales of 3.7 lakh units, up 33% from 2.8 lakh; Q4 EV sales 115,000, up 51%. EV penetration rose to 6.6% for FY26 (6.2% prior) and 7.8% in Q4 (7.1% prior). FY26 EV revenue about INR 5,000 crores.

segments.name: 3-wheeler
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 220,000 units, up 63% from 135,000; Q4 60,000 units, up 65% from 37,000.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record FY26 international sales of 15.8 lakh units, up 33%; Q4 international revenue INR 2,999 crores. Q4 international sales grew 23%. Spare parts revenue in Q4 about INR 1,122 crores.

segments.name: TVS Credit
segments.commentary: FY26 PBT INR 1,248 crores (up 22%); Q4 PBT INR 348 crores (up 15%). Added about 53 lakh new customers, total base about 2.4 crore; rated AA+.

segments.name: Norton (overseas subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Majority of the roughly INR 2,400 crores FY26 investment went to Norton; new models Manx, Manx R, Atlas and Atlas GT to be launched with Q2 FY27 as a key milestone. Some models to be built at Solihull and others at Hosur.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic industry growth guided at a strong single digit; TVS aims to grow ahead of the industry in both domestic and international markets.
Q1 FY27 expected to show very good growth ahead of the industry in both retail and dispatches, as supply constraints ease in May and are expected to clear by end-May or early June.
FY27 capex expected at about INR 3,500 crores: about INR 2,000 crores on product development, over INR 1,000 crores on 1.5 million unit capacity addition, and higher R&D spend.
Overseas investment in FY27 expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (INR 500-600 crores lower than INR 2,400 crores), though not zero.

Management declined to give margin guidance; said cost inflation of 3-5% of revenue is significant, with about 35% offset so far through price increases, and cited mix, scale and cost reduction as offsets.
Management expects 2W EV and scooter segments to grow well in FY27; the economy segment is expected to face challenges.
capex_capacity: Immediate plan to add about 1.5 million units of capacity, taking total to about 8.3 million units; work started in Q4 FY26 and the first significant addition in 12 months.
Capacity planning for FY28-29 under review quarter by quarter; aim is for capacity not to constrain growth.
EV production currently averages around 40,000 units/month (FY26 average 30,000-32,000), with a target of 50,000 per month soon.
Norton products in development at Hosur and Solihull; new Norton models expected in Q2 FY27.
Overseas: Dubai strategic investment about INR 300 crores made; TVS Credit investment about INR 200 crores in FY26.
demand_pricing: Demand described as strong across domestic and international for all models, but supply was the binding constraint. Dealer inventory is kept at 21-30 days and is being rebuilt; channel stock is expected to normalise by end-May or early June.
Commodity cost inflation (steel, aluminium, crude derivatives, gas) estimated at 3-5% of revenue; about 35% offset through price increases so far.
PLI incentive income for Q4 was about 0.9% of revenue.
Ronin monthly domestic volume crossed 8,000 units; management targets above 10,000. Indonesia averaged about 20,000 units per month, up from 17,000.
Africa and Asia are core; LatAm is a multi-year focus. International container lead times rose about 15% (around 8-10 days) amid geopolitical disruption.
3-wheeler: VAHAN share of EV 3W rising; new launches include King Kargo EV and King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG cargo; Hyundai JDA signed to co-develop an EV 3W.

qa_highlights.question: What growth is expected in FY27 for domestic and international, and how will segments perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong single-digit industry growth, with scooters, EVs and premium/super-premium growing well and the economy segment facing headwinds. TVS expects to outgrow the industry.

qa_highlights.question: What commodity inflation and price increases are expected in Q1 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation is about 3-5% of revenue, with about 35% offset by price increases so far. Mix, scale and cost reduction are the other levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are current 2W and 3W production capacities and the planned additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is being increased by 1.5 million units to about 8.3 million. Management said this is the first significant addition in 12 months, and capacity will not constrain growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where are supply-chain constraints (raw materials, labour, rare earths) and channel stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Constraints are energy/gas, Tier 2 labour shortages and raw material timing. May is better than April, and channel stock should normalise by end-May or early June. Q4 international revenue was INR 2,999 crores and spare parts INR 1,122 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management cautious for the next two quarters, and what are the risks to demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is strong and the uncertainty is on raw material timing and Tier 2 disruption, which it expects to clear within 2-3 weeks. Geopolitical risk is monitored industry-wide.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 investment plan and what is the Norton spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas investment is about INR 2,400 crores in FY26 (mainly Norton) and is expected to be about 70% of that in FY27. Total FY27 capex is about INR 3,500 crores, of which about INR 2,000 crores is product development.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV capacity and international EV plan?
qa_highlights.answer: EV output is about 40,000 units per month, moving toward 50,000. Asian markets are taking a growing share of EV volumes, with iQube and Orbiter launched there.

qa_highlights.question: Will Norton products be made in India, and what is the Hyundai EV 3W partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: One high-end Norton model will be built at Solihull and the others in India, using the Hosur plant. The Hyundai JDA is for co-developing an EV 3W, with Hyundai leading design; management gave no revenue or timeline details.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation of 3-5% of revenue with only about 35% offset so far; margin sustainability beyond Q1 FY27 is uncertain.
Supply-chain disruption from gas prices, Tier 2 labour shortages and raw material timing; management expects normalisation in 2-3 weeks.
International container lead times up about 15%, with West Asia conflict and logistics delays affecting distributor planning.
Economy segment demand pressure from inflation and fuel prices; El Nino risk to rainfall and rural demand in Q3-Q4.
Norton and other overseas investments (about INR 2,400 crores in FY26) must yield revenue; Norton launches expected in Q2 FY27.

532343|2026-06.headline: TVS Motor Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% to INR 13,896 crore and operating EBITDA rose 41% to INR 1,779 crore, with margin at 12.8%.
532343|2026-06.overview: Total volume grew 28% YoY to 1.63 million units, with revenue of INR 13,896 crore (+38%) and PAT of INR 1,174 crore (+51%). Operating EBITDA margin expanded 30 bps to 12.8%, helped by price increases and cost actions despite a sharp commodity spike linked to the West Asia conflict. International sales hit a record 4.68 lakh units (+33%), and EV sales grew 86%. Management guided Q2 as better than Q1 and expects FY27 industry growth in double digits, with capacity expansion to 8.3 million 2W units by Q4.

financial_highlights.change: +51% YoY (INR 1,050 crore); includes ~INR 150 crore fair value gain vs ~INR 28 crore last year

segments.name: 2-wheeler domestic ICE
segments.commentary: Sales grew 21% YoY versus industry growth of 13%. Overall 2W ICE grew 23% against industry growth of 21%.

segments.name: 2-wheeler EV
segments.commentary: Volume rose to 130,000 units from 70,000 in the prior-year quarter, up 86%. June EV penetration was above 10.6%, and management said EV penetration in 3W crossed 40%.

segments.name: 2-wheeler international
segments.commentary: International market ICE sales grew 31%. Africa, Asia and LATAM contributed, with HLX crossing 5 million cumulative units.

segments.name: 3-wheeler
segments.commentary: Total sales rose 48% to 67,000 units from 45,000 units.

segments.name: TVS Credit
segments.commentary: Disbursed to over 14 lakh new customers, taking the customer base to about 2.6 crore. Book size grew 19% and PBT rose 16% to INR 283 crore.

segments.name: Norton
segments.commentary: Manx and Atlas production has started, with Atlas rolling out from Hosur in June. Cumulative investment is about INR 2,000 crore to INR 2,500 crore over the last 4-5 years.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be better than Q1; 2W ICE growth could be slightly better than Q1 and EV growth similar or slightly better.
Management expects FY27 industry growth of at least double digits in ICE, with EV growth well above penetration levels of about 10.6%.
International growth expected at the same rate or slightly better in Q2.
Price increases of about 1.5% were taken in Q1 and about 0.5% are planned in Q2, subject to market conditions.
Q3 is the key watch item due to El Nino, the base effect and GST benefits starting late September.
Festive season launches are planned for October and November.
capex_capacity: 2W capacity is planned to rise from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by Q4 FY27, in stages over Q2 and Q3.
3W capacity is planned to rise from about 0.25 million to about 0.42 million units, with a good share in EV.
Total capex, including new products and capacity expansion, is about INR 3,500 crore.
Capacity additions take about 3 to 4 months to commission.
Partnership with IOC for last-mile LPG cylinder distribution and cargo EV mobility.
demand_pricing: Commodity costs rose about 3.5% in Q1 and about 0.5% more in Q2, a total of about 4%; about 30% was passed through as per the last call.
Dealer inventory is kept at 25-30 days, with up to about 30 days during the festive season.
Management says it keeps less than 30 days of stock with dealers and cites JD Power rankings of No. 1 and No. 2 in the scooter category.
Scooter category share is about 40% including ICE and EV.
Production was disrupted in April by supply issues but recovered in May and June.
PLI incentive is about 0.6-0.7% of turnover, and about INR 600 crore of PLI is receivable.
Exports are about 26% of turnover; management aims to grow this materially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV capacity and how is EV demand developing?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler capacity is about 40,000 units moving to 50,000+. 3W capacity is moving from about 20,000 to 30,000 units, with EV a good share. EV demand is spreading from urban to semi-urban areas, and some buyers are moving from motorcycles to scooters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is TVS gaining share against a competitor discounting in scooters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a broad scooter range, frequent feature upgrades, durability and JD Power rankings. It said dealer stock is kept below 30 days and that retail financing supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commodity headwind and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the impact was in Q1, with some further pressure from aluminium and oil-linked plastics. Price increases were about 1.5% in Q1 and about 0.5% in Q2, with the rest offset by mix, scale and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is EV profitability improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV contribution is improving quarter after quarter, but it expects the EV margin to reach the company's target over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall capacity and investment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: 2W capacity is moving from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by Q4, with 3W capacity rising to about 0.42 million. Total investment is about INR 3,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Norton strategy, investment and volume ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Four Norton models (Manx, Manx R, Atlas and Atlas GT) are launching across the UK, Europe, India and later the US. The model uses independent dealers and multi-brand premium outlets, with cumulative investment of about INR 2,000-2,500 crore. Management gave no breakeven volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses decline and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April production loss and supply issues drove some cost control. It said brand spend as a percentage of sales will not change much, and launch costs will add to expenses when new products are introduced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 600-700 crore PLI receivable collectible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 600 crore is PLI receivable and is fully collectible, with the government having always supported the scheme.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility from the West Asia conflict (aluminium, steel, oil-linked plastics) and a possible further 0.5% cost pressure in Q2.
Supply chain availability, which was disrupted in April.
Q3 demand risks from El Nino, the high base from last year's GST effect and monsoon progression.
Draft Delhi EV policy may ban ICE 2-wheeler sales from around 2028.
Receivables of about INR 600-700 crore, mainly PLI, that need to be collected.
Norton ramp-up and breakeven volumes, which were not disclosed.
Q1 PBT includes about INR 150 crore of fair value gains that are non-operating.
Deep Vakil asked about gearing and a preference share redemption on 1 September; management did not answer this.
532343|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, share gains, exports and Q2, while cautious on commodity costs and Q3 timing. Management was evasive on Norton breakeven volume, PLI receivables and the gearing question.
key_quotes: The company's operating EBITDA margin improved by 30 basis points at 12.8% during the first quarter and this is against 12.5% last year first quarter.
So, as a year, we should estimate an industry growth of double digit.
Yes, INR 600 crores is about PLI, that's a receivable.

rows.why: 2W capacity is going from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units (+22%) in stages over Q2 and Q3 with 3-4 month commissioning, and 3W from about 0.25 million to 0.42 million (+68%), both already under construction.

rows.why: Q2 2W ICE growth guided slightly better than Q1's 21%, EV growth similar or slightly better than Q1's 86%, international growth same or slightly better, and FY27 industry growth at least double digit.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided Q2 as better than Q1 and FY27 industry growth at double digit, with Q1 volume up 28% and 2W ICE up 23% versus industry 21%, though Q3 faces El Nino, high base and GST timing risks.

rows.why: Q3 is flagged as the key watch item due to El Nino, the high base from last year's GST effect and monsoon progression, and commodity costs could add about 0.5% more pressure in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Festive season launches are planned for October and November, and four Norton models (Manx, Manx R, Atlas, Atlas GT) are rolling out across UK, Europe, India and later the US, with Manx and Atlas already in production.

rows.label: PLI receivable of ~INR 600 crore collection
rows.why: About INR 600 crore of PLI (about 0.6-0.7% of turnover) is receivable, which management says is fully collectible, though the company did not give a timeline and analysts pressed on it.

rows.label: International growth and exports push
rows.why: International sales hit a record 4.68 lakh units (+33%), with international growth guided at the same or slightly better rate in Q2, and exports (INR 3,634 crore, about 26% of turnover) to grow materially.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, share gains (scooter share about 40%, JD Power No.1/No.2), exports and Q2, and cautious on commodity costs and Q3 timing; analysts pushed on Norton breakeven, PLI receivables and gearing, which management was evasive on.

532348|2026-03.headline: Subex Q4 FY26 revenue rose 3% QoQ to INR 72.96 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5% and FY26 order intake up 24%.
532348|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 72.96 crores versus INR 70.79 crores in Q3, with EBITDA of INR 10.58 crores (14.5% margin) and normalized PAT of INR 11.51 crores. Management said FY26 full-year total income grew 6% YoY, partly supported by interest income, and that FY25 is not like-for-like because non-core businesses were exited. Order intake grew 24% in FY26 and management highlighted AI deal wins, though it acknowledged top-line growth lagged its ambitions. Middle East exposure, the geopolitical backdrop and slow new-purchase decisions were flagged as the main near-term risks, with revenue conversion expected to improve as implementations finish.

segments.name: Revenue streams: License, Implementation, MS (managed services), AMC
segments.commentary: Management indicated license gross margin is near 90-100%, implementation gross margin 40-45% (up to 60% depending on complexity), MS above 50% and AMC above 70%. These are gross margins before R&D, GTM, G&A and lease costs.

segments.name: Products
segments.commentary: Four core products: Revenue Assurance, Fraud Management, Partner Settlement (wholesale billing) and Enterprise Asset Management. FraudZap is the newer AI fraud product, with one paid customer that onboarded three Telcos through an intermediary.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Management said about 31% of revenue comes from the Gulf region, and that APAC and Europe are steady. Africa is seeing momentum and the Americas will get heavy investment in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical FY27 guidance was given; management described the team as 'very bullish' and said it expects to beat FY26 results.
Management expects revenue conversion to improve quarter by quarter as implementations of FY26 wins finish, with an uptick expected around the middle of FY27 if there are no delays.
INR 100 crores per quarter revenue was described internally as a target ('war cry'), with no timeline committed.
Management plans to pursue tuck-in acquisitions in FY27, which the board is actively discussing.
Management said the goodwill impairment test is complete and auditors found no impairment needed on carrying value of about INR 190 crores.
capex_capacity: Team of LLMs product has completed POCs and is in talks with two or three customers to go commercial this quarter, but GPU hardware constraints are slowing deployment.
Management is working on running agents on CPU or a laptop-sized 'agent in a box' to get around the GPU constraint; it said it is also looking at neuromorphic hardware.
GenAI-based software development is being embedded across the MCLC to lift developer productivity and reduce engineering cost.
key_quotes: I'll be direct anytime that you ask that question of me.
So, I believe that the reset is done. The foundation is built and FY27 is where we will convert it.
I truly believe that the stock is materially undervalued related to our fundamentals and our trajectory.

Management said the company is targeting data centers, mobile money, MVNO, IoT assurance and Telco FinTech as adjacencies, and sees a TAM of about 4.3 million that did not exist two years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order intake not converting into revenue faster, and will Q1 improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wins are multi-year, so revenue will come as implementations finish. Subscription revenue starts after go-live, and conversion should improve each quarter through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and the impact of AI competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said work is being moved offshore to Bangalore, renewals look secure, and new wins are the risk. It sees OpenAI-type tools as a tailwind and positions Subex as a system-of-record with an SOI layer on top.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new-product margins and the existing margins different?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy MS and AMC products carry the margins described earlier. Management declined to give product-level margins because they are competition-sensitive.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Gulf region hit the business and what share of revenue is it?
qa_highlights.answer: A management response put the Gulf share at about 31% of revenue. APAC and Europe are steady. Management said the main risk is delay in new purchases, not renewals.

qa_highlights.question: Is the goodwill write-off a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual impairment test is complete. Auditors found the carrying value is fine and no write-off is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning acquisitions or changes to the OnGrid stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is discussing tuck-in acquisitions with the board. It is not divesting OnGrid because the investee is doing well and the company has enough cash for its own bets.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: about 31% of revenue from the Gulf; new-purchase decisions and contract signing could slip further.

GPU hardware constraint may delay commercialization of Team of LLMs and agent products.

Management declined to share milestone-based payment schedules, which limits visibility into revenue timing of large deals.
Currency: customers are pushing for local-currency contracts, which the company is resisting.

532348|2026-06.headline: Subex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.7% YoY to INR 79.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21.2% and management signalling margins will be held in a range.
532348|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 8.9% QoQ and 19.7% YoY to INR 79.45 crore, with EBITDA of INR 16.87 crore (21.2% margin) versus INR 10.58 crore in Q4. Normalized PAT was INR 16.09 crore versus INR 11.51 crore previously, and reported PAT was INR 14.22 crore. Management framed FY27 as a growth year, while saying it will hold margins in a range and reinvest excess cash in R&D and AI. Cash stood at INR 184.8 crore, and management declined to give a funnel number, order-book value or a revenue target, citing competitive sensitivity.

segments.commentary: Management called it an under-invested business that has been rebuilt; it renewed a Tier 1 Asia-Pacific PEM engagement this quarter and sees stronger deal flow. No quantified revenue was given.

segments.commentary: Secured new business assurance and fraud management deal with a leading European operator; a FraudZap customer deal was said to be slipping into this quarter. Management said FraudZap's investment is already recovered, though no margin figure was given.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not give forward guidance on the call; expects 'double-digit' or 'high single digit' growth, to be decided.
Margins to be held 'in the ballpark' of the FY26 close and the mid-to-high teens was not confirmed; management will hold margins in a range and reinvest excess cash in R&D/AI.

US described as better; Europe described as okay; APAC and Africa described as slower; contracts slipping by a month or two.
Deals above USD 0.8-1 million go through RFP; management would not disclose margin thresholds for contract acceptance.

qa_highlights.answer: CEO said it was discussed at the board meeting held the day before; a consultant will be appointed, and it is a long process requiring board, shareholder and NCLT approval.

qa_highlights.question: Size of executable pipeline and total order wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave qualified pipeline at 3-4x target but declined to give absolute numbers, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Where will EBITDA margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected 'in the ballpark' of current levels; management will not cap margins but will reinvest excess cash in R&D and AI.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated about INR 3 crore of currency gain in the quarter; QoQ FX gain was small.

532349|2026-06.headline: TCI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew ~9% (24th straight quarter of growth) while standalone profit turned slightly negative on lower JV dividends and bunker costs.
532349|2026-06.overview: Management reported 9% consolidated top-line growth and 7% standalone growth for Q1 FY27, with the freight business up 10-11%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 1.6% and PAT slightly negative, largely because JV dividend income was lower; consolidated EBITDA was about 5%. Seaways margins were flat as bunker prices rose to around Rs 86,000/ton, partly offset by rate increases; the Concor JV grew about 88% and Cold Chain about 48%. Management guided supply chain to 12-15% growth and freight to 10-12%, with capex of Rs 550-600 crore for FY27 (Rs 167 crore spent in Q1).

segments.name: Supply chain (standalone)
segments.commentary: Growth moderate against a high base; EBITDA margin slightly improved but EBIT flat. Management expects 12-15% top-line growth for FY27, pick-up in H2 from new contracts and diesel pass-through bills.

segments.name: Freight
segments.commentary: Top line up ~10-11% with slight margin improvement; 10 of planned 30 new branches opened in Q1. FY27 guidance 10-12% growth with higher profitability.

segments.name: Seaways
segments.commentary: Revenue up on pricing with similar voyages (one ship dry-docked); margins flat. Bunker prices at ~Rs 86,000/ton; Q2 EBITDA guided at 25-30%, and new ships expected Sept-Oct and Oct-Nov.

segments.name: Concor JV
segments.commentary: Grew ~88% per management; revenue moderated vs last quarter per Q&A. Rail shift from road limited due to lean season and rail congestion.

segments.name: Cold Chain JV
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~48% from contracts won in Q3-Q4 FY26; still small in quantum.

segments.name: Trans System JV (Toyota-linked, Mitsui partner)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~11.5%, but margin fell to ~9% from 14-15% on pricing pressure and production cuts; profit run-rate down to ~Rs 30 crore from Rs 40-42 crore. Management sees ~10% margin as reasonable.

guidance_outlook: Supply chain revenue growth 12-15% for FY27, with pick-up expected from Q2 onwards.
Freight revenue growth 10-12% for FY27 with higher profitability year on year.

The distillery segment staged a sharp turnaround on record volumes and lower maize costs, while sugar crush fell 8.8% to 8.25 million tonnes. segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: Record production and sales volumes with FY26 revenue net of excise of ₹1,550 crore. Realisation averaged ₹61/litre (lower due to FCI rice mix), and grain made up 56% of ethanol sales (maize about 33%). Management said conversion and raw-material costs fell significantly.

532388|2026-03.headline: IOB posted FY26 net profit of about Rs 5,208 crore (up 56.16%) and advances growth of 24.16%, with GNPA down to 1.42%.

Management guided to 14-16% industry credit growth, flagged ECL front-loading of about Rs 3,000 crore (Rs 1,750 crore already provided), and said it sees no West Asia stress so far.

532395|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue grew 12.4% to 1,159 crores and EBITDA rose 24.6% to 178 crores, but reported PAT fell 4.3% to 72 crores after a 142 crore Q4 revenue deferment.

FY27 consolidated revenue is guided at about 1,377 crores (52% growth on the retained base), and the company reiterated its 9,000 crore FY30 revenue target.

532424|2026-03.headline: GCPL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth; EBITDA up 10% at 21.7% margin, with a revenue-presentation change.
532424|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 10% with a 21.7% margin, and reported PAT grew 10%. India standalone was the standout: 8% volume growth, 10% sales growth, 18% EBITDA growth and a 24.7% margin, led by Home Care (+12%). Africa/US/Middle East grew 20% in sales but EBITDA rose only 2% after doubling media spend, and Indonesia grew 3% in sales with 4% volume growth. From this quarter, customer-related trade spends are netted off revenue following an ICAI Expert Advisory Committee opinion, with no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT. Management guided to margin pressure in Q1 and likely Q2 FY27 from crude-linked and palm oil input inflation of roughly 7-9%, offset by price hikes and share gains.

532424|2026-06.headline: GCPL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY on 9% underlying volume growth, EBITDA up 14% with 19% margin; India gross margin hit by war-linked input costs.
532424|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY with underlying volume growth of 9%, EBITDA rose 14% at a 19% margin, and net profit grew 11%. India gross margin fell sharply as LPG, kerosene and LABSA roughly trebled during the war-driven spike, with India cost impact near 6% over plan. Africa (GAUM) delivered an exceptional quarter with constant-currency growth around 25% and EBITDA margins moving to mid-teens, while Indonesia returned to stable growth at about 10%. Management says it is on track for full-year guidance and expects to exceed it on revenue, and possibly on EBITDA and volume.

segments.name: India Household Insecticides (HI)
segments.commentary: Management says GCPL gained overall HI market share in Q1 FY27 for the first time in almost a decade, driven by incense sticks, not premium segments. June was very weak due to rain and poor fill rates; July first half also poor.

segments.name: India Air care / Speedboats
segments.commentary: Speedboats grew about 3% in Q1 per analyst calculation; salience about 15% and management expects roughly 100-150 bps rise per quarter. Air care in India hit by LPG-linked fill rate falls of 20-25%.

segments.name: Africa / GAUM
segments.commentary: Constant-currency growth about 25%, driven by FMCG (air care at double-digit market share in South Africa within six months of launch) and hair extensions cost improvements. FY26 growth split was about 50:50 FMCG and hair.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Growth about 10% on a slower base, step-up in air media, and early El Nino benefit; Stellar business growing faster.

segments.name: Soaps (India)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew positively in Q1; management expects early single-digit growth in Q2 and Q3, soap margins at normative levels.

segments.name: Muuchstac (acquired DTC brand)
segments.commentary: Growth of about 70-80% from acquisition run rate; EPS accretive from day one, profitable digital-first brand.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Committed INR500 crore capital; additional INR200 crore rights commitment referenced by analyst. Product-market fit achieved in Tamil Nadu; expansion to rest of South India under way.

qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is broadly on plan; air fill rates in India fell and salience rises about 100-150 bps per quarter, so full-year targets may be exceeded.

qa_highlights.answer: Q1 India volume 7% is at the lower end; India volume expected to rise about 100 bps a year. Pricing about 5% taken with more possible, but caution as costs fell.

532440|2026-03.headline: MPS FY26 revenue rose 5.7% to INR 768 crore and EBITDA 11.8% to INR 236 crore; FY27 EBITDA guided to comfortably exceed INR 300 crore.
532440|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as the most profitable year in company history, with EBITDA margin at 30.7% and PAT up 16.3% to INR 173 crore. Q4 revenue grew 12.7% to INR 205 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 32.9%, helped by Research and the Unbound Medicine acquisition, which closed on 9 February 2026. Corporate Learning revenue fell 16.5% for the year but returned to positive year-on-year growth in Q4. Management guided FY27 EBITDA above INR 300 crore on an organic, bottom-up basis, and no final dividend was recommended for FY26 because capital was deployed into Unbound and the M&A pipeline.

segments.name: Research Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 464 crore, EBITDA margin 39.9% (+330 bps); organic growth 17% ex-AJE. Q4 revenue INR 120 crore (+7.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 50 crore at 41.6% margin; organic core grew 23% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: Education Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 209 crore, organic growth 28.6%; EBITDA INR 82 crore at 39.2% margin, up 42.6% reported. Q4 revenue INR 60 crore (+30.5% YoY). Unbound contributed INR 11.78 crore over 50 days, about 19.6% of Q4 Education revenue.

segments.name: Corporate Learning (Liberate Global)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 96 crore, down 16.5% YoY; headcount down about 32% YoY. Q4 revenue INR 25.5 crore (+2.4% YoY, first positive print of year); Q4 EBITDA INR 6.7 crore at 26.3% margin, up 55% QoQ.

Management argued AI commoditises basic production work and raises demand for trusted, verified AI in high-stakes knowledge workflows; company's share of serviceable market is about 0.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is MPS's right to win in a market where it holds only about 0.5% share, and what capabilities are needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an AI-first knowledge positioning in high-stakes layers, an integrated platform stack (HighWire, Think365, RIC, Bridge AI, Unbound, DigiCore), 200+ MPS Labs engineers, and deep expansion within large accounts. The target path is 0.5% to 1% to 2% over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,500 crore FY28 revenue target still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is intact and in line of sight. FY27 INR 300 crore EBITDA is organic and excludes new acquisitions; any further M&A would sit on top. Tighter FY28 guidance to come at end-Q3 or Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions, and has Unbound been paid for?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbound is mostly fully paid, with only small closing amounts left. Pipeline is active, with a Western Higher Ed carve-out the most advanced. Management will disclose material deals in the ordinary course.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a margin in the 30%-35% range, with expansion as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is Unbound's revenue and EBITDA, and how will it move in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Given AI disruption, what protects the business model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI compresses commoditised production work but raises demand for trusted AI in medicine, scholarly publishing and regulated learning. It sees agentic AI as a tailwind, with verification as the gating constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin dip and ex-AJE headcount rise, and what drives FY27 growth and the FY28 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AJE headcount moved offshore to India while Research headcount rose ahead of expected growth, causing a timing-related ex-AJE margin softness in Q4. Growth drivers are the four Research product layers, Education, and the accessibility line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Corporate Learning investment shift, and why did clients rise while revenue per client fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Work has moved from compliance content to AI, AR/VR and simulation-led performance enablers. Unbound added a long tail of smaller institutional accounts, which lowered average revenue per client without any anchor client billing less.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA split and main risk to the INR 300 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a ballpark split of Research 55%, Education 35%, Corporate 10%. It sees no company-specific risk, only broader geopolitical and macro risk. Management disputed the analyst's constant-currency framing.

532440|2026-06.headline: MPS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.4% to INR 224.24 crores and EBITDA rose 53.0% to INR 76.96 crores, with margin at 34.3%.
532440|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 20.4% YoY to INR 224.24 crores, while EBITDA grew 53.0% to INR 76.96 crores and margin expanded to 34.3% from 27.0%. Excluding AJE's deliberate pruning, underlying revenue grew 28.4% to INR 198.47 crores with a 32.4% margin. Unbound Medicine was in its first full quarter and drove Education growth, and Corporate Learning margins recovered sharply on a leaner headcount. Management reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA of comfortably above INR 300 crores and framed FY28 targets of about INR 1,500 crores revenue and INR 450 crores EBITDA.

segments.name: Education Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 73.41 crores, +42.2% YoY and +22.1% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 35.1%. Growth includes Unbound Medicine's first full quarter.

segments.name: Corporate Learning (Liberate Global)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 27.60 crores, +6.9% YoY; EBITDA +60.7% with margin at 25.3% vs under 17% a year ago. Headcount about 33% lower YoY.

segments.name: AJE (within Research)
segments.commentary: Deliberately shrinking consumer base in author solutions; management says revenue is smaller but more profitable. Pre-Submission Peer Review launched in April 2026 with demand ahead of plan.

segments.name: Unbound Medicine (within Education)
segments.commentary: Monthly run rate about USD 800,000; current EBITDA margin 18-20%, with a target of mid-to-late 20s. Team of 35 people.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA expected to comfortably cross INR 300 crores, described as a floor; implies roughly 21% three-year EBITDA CAGR from FY24.
FY28 targets of about INR 1,500 crores revenue and around INR 450 crores EBITDA, per Q&A.
Management aspires to Rule of 50 for the full year but declined to promise it every quarter.
Corporate Learning steady-state target: 30% EBITDA margin and organic growth near 12%.
Unbound expected to reach Rule of 40 (mid-to-late 20s EBITDA margin) over time.
capex_capacity: Unbound acquisition financed partly by INR 37.63 crores of borrowings; management sees acquisitions of INR 300-500 crores as doable from cash plus debt, with no equity planned.
Cash generation of about INR 15-18 crores per month cited as first source for M&A.
AJE's US roles fully offshored to India by end of last fiscal year; little US headcount in Q1.
Headcount: Research 2,262 to 2,452; Education 799 to 765 YoY.
demand_pricing: Research market growing 8-9% versus MPS research growth of roughly 15% per management.
Education market growing about 15%; corporate learning market 12-13% versus MPS at 6-7%.
Manuscript acceptance rate of about 52% in controlled work vs industry baseline near 32%.
MPS now second-largest peer-review provider by volume and targets first place by end of this year.
Management says it has pricing power at Unbound and sees room for price increases across parts of its portfolio.
Corporate Learning enterprise engagements approaching USD 1 million; more AI-led wins and new logos in pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have there been management exits and replacements, and how is culture preserved after acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a growing talent machine with more internal promotions than prior years; values of excellence, efficiency and empathy plus an ownership mindset are used to integrate acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the headcount reduction affecting quality as gig and AI workflows expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Soma said Corporate Learning headcount fell about 33% YoY through redundancy removal, a shift to variable gig capacity and productivity gains; senior design and client-facing teams untouched. Rahul said NPS rose in Research and Education.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the client count fall from 906 to 841 QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the only pruning was at AJE, as described on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 target INR 1,500 crores revenue, and how will acquisitions be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 targets are about INR 1,500 crores revenue and about INR 450 crores EBITDA. Acquisitions of INR 300-500 crores are to be funded by cash accruals and debt; equity not planned. Assets below USD 15 million revenue are generally avoided, with a preference for Education.

qa_highlights.question: What is Unbound's monthly run rate and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Prarthana said monthly run rate is around USD 800,000 with EBITDA margins of 18-20%, rising from there.

qa_highlights.question: Can organic growth be pushed higher, and does Corporate Learning growth reflect FX?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul said management aims to outgrow markets in all three segments, targeting late-teens organic growth. On FX, he said North America is a smaller share of Corporate Learning, so dollar tailwind is smaller there.

risks_watch: Corporate Learning organic growth at 6.9% lags its 12-13% market and the stated 12% steady-state target.
Client count fell QoQ to 841 from 906; management attributes this only to AJE pruning.
Unbound margin at 18-20% is below the group level; renewal-cycle and synergy timing are still being learned.
Headcount cuts and gig/associate shift in Corporate Learning need to be watched for quality and client retention.
Acquisition pipeline is active; execution on INR 300-500 crore deals and debt use is a watch item.

532443|2026-03.headline: Cera Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.2% from 18.3% on brass costs and trade discounts.
532443|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, led by volume (about 12%), with management citing early retail recovery from Q3 and continued project strength. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 98 crore (15.2% margin) from INR 106 crore (18.3%), driven by brass input costs, elevated trade discounts and pre-operating costs for Senator and Polipluz. Price increases were taken in March (11% effective) and April-May (surcharge then 8% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware), with management targeting a 14-15% EBITDA margin. Morbi gas disruptions were cited as an opportunity, with Cera running inventory and internalising outsourced SKUs. FY26 revenue was INR 2,050 crore, and FY27 guidance is 18-20% growth.

segments.commentary: 46% of Q4 revenue, up 10.7% YoY; capacity utilisation 70% in March. Outsourcing about 60% of sanitaryware volume, mostly from Morbi. One kiln closed in March and kept closed in April.

segments.commentary: 43% of Q4 revenue, up 24.3% YoY; utilisation 106% in Q4. Output of 4.3 lakh pieces/month in March; capacity moves to 5 lakh pieces/month from Q4 FY27 at about INR 4-5 crore capex. Outsourcing about 46%.

segments.commentary: 9% of Q4 revenue, down 8.3% YoY. Almost fully outsourced, so Q1 FY27 expected to be impacted by Morbi supply.

segments.name: Senator and Polipluz (new brands)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 19 crore (Senator about INR 10.5 crore, Polipluz about INR 8.5 crore); FY26 combined losses about INR 8.5 crore. FY27 target INR 70-80 crore; 40 Senator stores to become 60, Polipluz to grow to 200 distributors and 2,000 dealers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth guided at 18-20%: sanitaryware about 12% (volume 7%, price 5-6%), faucetware about 18% (volume 10-12%, price about 8%).
Tiles and construction chemicals expected to contribute about INR 250 crore in FY27 with 20%-plus growth once Morbi supply normalises; Senator and Polipluz INR 70-80 crore.
EBITDA margin expected to sustain at about 14-15% as discounts are controlled from Q1 FY27.
Employee costs expected to rise about 10% in FY27; a pending labour long-term settlement could add wage cost.

FY27 capex about INR 43-45 crore (routine about INR 25-30 crore, faucetware INR 5 crore, office space about INR 15 crore). Greenfield plant first phase estimated at about INR 150 crore, with construction timing dependent on demand.

Senator publicity expected at INR 10-12 crore in FY27; Senator and Polipluz salary cost about INR 15.5-16 crore, with the sub-brand portfolio expected to turn profitable after publicity in FY28 per management.
capex_capacity: Faucetware capacity to rise from 4.3 lakh to 5 lakh pieces/month by debottlenecking the brownfield setup, at about INR 4-5 crore capex, operational from Q4 FY27.
Sanitaryware utilisation about 70-75% in March-April; one kiln closed in March and kept closed in April, with the second kiln expected to restart soon.

Greenfield sanitaryware plant: land of INR 27 crore already bought; first phase now estimated at about INR 150 crore (vs INR 130 crore earlier) with construction timing to be decided in coming quarters.
Internalisation of sanitaryware categories previously sourced from Morbi, expected to be available for sale from Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says retail demand improved from Q3 FY26, continued through Q4 and into April 2026; project share has risen from about 30% to 39-40% and is expected to stabilise, with a 60:40 retail-to-project split.

Price actions: 11% effective March 1 (faucetware and sanitaryware); April surcharge of 10% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware; then removed and replaced by 8% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware price increase. Management says the two-month effective increase is 12% for sanitaryware and 16% for faucetware, applied to retail; projects keep old prices for up to one year from booking.

Brass prices up about 29-30% YoY, moving from late INR 600s to INR 800-850 per kg range (as stated). Management says the 16% faucetware price increase covers about 18% COGS impact, leaving a 1-2% gap to be recovered through discount control.
Q4 volume-led growth: volume about 12%, product mix 3-4%, price/discount drag about 3%. Product mix: premium 41%, mid 38%, entry 21%. Tier-3 40%, Tier-1 36%, Tier-2 24%.
Peers' price increases reportedly 16-18% for faucets and 10-12% for sanitaryware; management says Cera is in line.
FY27 volume guidance: sanitaryware 7-8%, faucetware 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: How is retail demand likely to evolve in FY27, and what is the institution-versus-retail balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail recovered from Q3 and continued into April, and project share rose from about 30% to 39-40%. It expects a stable 60:40 retail-to-project mix and FY27 volume growth of 7-8% for sanitaryware and 10-12% for faucetware.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the price increase delayed, and how much more is needed to protect the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Brass rose from late INR 600s to INR 800-850 per kg with about 29-30% YoY. Cera has taken about 12% on sanitaryware and 16% on faucetware over two months, with project pricing lagging by about six months. The remaining 1-2% gap is expected to be recovered through discounts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Senator and Polipluz revenue, target and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue was about INR 19 crore (Senator 10.5, Polipluz 8.5), with a FY27 target of INR 70-80 crore. Management said the brands make a small profit before publicity and expect to be profitable after publicity next year.

qa_highlights.question: How does 18-20% overall growth reconcile with 12% sanitaryware and 18% faucetware growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance comes from tiles and construction chemicals (about INR 250 crore, 20%-plus growth once Morbi normalises) and Senator/Polipluz (INR 70-80 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Why are trade discounts still high when retail demand is recovering, and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said discounts rose through the downturn and cannot be cut immediately; control starts from Q1 FY27. Q4 margin rose to 15.2% from 10.2% in Q3, and management expects 14-15% to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sanitaryware capacity utilisation, inventory and supply outlook for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware utilisation was 70% in March; one kiln was closed. Management said inventory covers about 2-3 months of forecast demand, and tiles are expected to be impacted in Q1 because they are fully outsourced.

qa_highlights.question: What are the employee cost trends and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 included about INR 5 crore of wage code provision, and Q4 had a INR 10 crore exceptional write-back on gratuity and PL liability. Employee cost is expected to rise about 10% in FY27. Capex is guided at about INR 43-45 crore including office space of about INR 15 crore.

risks_watch: Morbi gas-driven supply disruption: sanitaryware outsourcing is about 60% (mostly Morbi) and tiles are almost fully outsourced; management expects Q1 FY27 tiles to be impacted and Morbi sanitaryware output to stay slow through monsoon, with internalised SKUs only available from Q2 FY27.

Price-cost gap: management says the 16% faucetware and 12% sanitaryware price increases cover brass costs only partly (about 1-2% gap on faucetware), and project pricing lags by about six months since projects keep old prices for up to a year from booking.
Trade discounts: margin recovery to 14-15% depends on discount control starting Q1 FY27; Q4 margin was 15.2% versus 10.2% in Q3, and Q4 benefited from inventory liquidation during Morbi disruption.

FY27 growth bridge: 18-20% overall growth relies on tiles and construction chemicals (about INR 250 crore, 20%-plus growth) and Senator/Polipluz (INR 70-80 crore) versus FY26 Senator/Polipluz revenue of about INR 19 crore and losses of about INR 8.5 crore; sustained losses and publicity spend (INR 10-12 crore) are a watch item.

Cost and capex items to track: pending labour long-term settlement could add wage cost on top of about 10% employee cost rise; greenfield sanitaryware first phase now about INR 150 crore with construction timing undecided; sanitaryware utilisation at 70-75% and second kiln restart timing.
key_quotes: Since Q3 of the current financial year, we have started seeing an improvement in the retail demand, and we saw this sustaining through Q4 also.
So, these trade discounts are again can be corrected it in the coming quarters.
Tiles will be impacted, because in the month of March, also later part of March, most of it is dependent upon outsourcing.
So, we anticipate that the current situation would be playing well for us going forward in Q1 and Q2.
532443|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on demand recovery and volume guidance, citing retail improvement from Q3 through April 2026, but was noticeably cautious on margins and Morbi-linked supply, repeatedly saying discount control is a gradual journey starting Q1 FY27. Answers on the FY27 growth bridge and Senator/Polipluz breakeven were direct, though several figures (capex total, Senator/Polipluz revenue split) were restated during Q&A.
